units.title: Lines 1–2
units.summary: Line 1 (monumental script) is Shabaqo's full titulary carved as two mirrored halves running outward from a central ankh: Horus, Two Ladies and Golden Horus names (all Sbq-tꜣwy), Dual King Neferkare, Son of Re [Shabaqo], beloved of Ptah (left) / Sokar (right) South-of-his-Wall, living like Re forever. Line 2 is the dedication: the king found the ancestors' writing worm-eaten and illegible and had it copied anew in Ptah's temple.
units.translation:
Line 1 (each half): The living Horus Sebeq-tawy; the Two Ladies Sebeq-tawy; the Golden Horus Sebeq-tawy; the Dual King Neferkare; the Son of Re [Shabaqo]; beloved of Ptah (right half: Sokar) South-of-his-Wall; living like Re forever.
Line 2: His Majesty had this writing copied out anew in the house of his father Ptah South-of-his-Wall. His Majesty had found it as a work of the ancestors that the worms had eaten away, so that it could not be understood from beginning to end. Then [His Majesty] had it copied out anew, so that it is finer than it was before, in order that his name might stand firm and his monument be established in the house of his father Ptah South-of-his-Wall for the length of eternity, as something the Son of Re [Shabaqo] made for his father Ptah-Tatenen, so that he may be given life forever.
(Breasted's version, for comparison: 'His majesty wrote this document anew ... his majesty having discovered it, a work of the ancestors, being eaten of worms; it was not legible from beginning to end.' (Breasted))
units.lacunae: (1) Line 1 left nomen cartouche, A2 x 1127-1337, y 392-502 (end-bar at ~1105): deliberate erasure, a pecked hollow with nothing of the name left. (2) Line 1 right nomen cartouche, x 4482-4690, y 393-505 (end-bar ~4700): same treatment. (3) Line 2 nomen cartouche, x 4815-4900, y 532-605: same. All three are Shabaqo's personal name; the erasure is conventionally attributed to Psamtik II's proscription of the Kushite kings. The prenomen cartouches (Neferkare, x 1490-1690 and 4137-4340) were NOT hacked out; only their interior signs are shallow (right one mostly worn). Breasted shows all three erased ovals as plain shaded cartouches with no traces, which agrees with the stone. (4) Line 2 x ~2700-3050: heavy wear plus a pitted, broken patch at x ~2860-3000 (above the central millstone hollow; Breasted hatches x ~2870-2950). ꜥḥꜥ.n sphr survives only as traces, and the agent/object after sphr is lost ([jn ḥm.f] Sethe / [sš pn] Breasted). (5) Line 2 x ~3250-3460 (nfr sw r): worn, signs only as traces. (6) The left edge of line 2 at x<450 is broken.
breasted_issues: Line 1 right prenomen: Breasted draws a complete kꜣ (D28) and nfr (F35). The stone shows only the base of kꜣ and a trace of nfr, so he probably completed them from the left-hand copy.

Line 2 'nfr sw': where Breasted saw a damaged owl (m), Sethe reads w (G43). The stone has only a bird's back at x~3395-3420, which settles neither reading. Breasted also leaves out the complements of nfr and the sw-sedge that Sethe gives; nothing certain of them survives.
Line 2 x~2700-2900 (ꜥḥꜥ.n sphr): Breasted's full mast, s and two ovals are over-complete. The stone shows traces only (one oval and faint horizontals).
Line 2: Breasted's isolated tall stroke (B1272) inside the damaged patch is not supported by either relief.
Line 2: Breasted's leading dot (B3) sits on the broken edge and is not a sign. The S29 at the head of the line (B2) is not clearly visible.
The 'traces' inside his shaded nomen cartouches (B467-471, B1863-1868) are parts of the shading, not signs, and nothing survives inside. His shading itself is correct.
Registration: in line 2's left part his boxes sit about 20-35 A2 px left of the carved signs. This is a warp offset, not a copying error.
units.confidence: Line 1: high. The signs are large and clear, every element is confirmed in both reliefs, and the reading is formulaic. Line 2: medium for words and reading (well established, and it matches Sethe), but low to medium for sign-level identification in the worn stretches (x 2700-3050 and 3250-3460) and for some small signs that Breasted did not box separately. Many line-2 'confirmed' statuses mean the sign is present at the right place with a compatible shape, not checked stroke by stroke.

words.gloss: Golden Horus (falcon on gold collar, G8 written as G5+S12)
Ptah (god's name written first: honorific transposition before mry)
like Re (Rꜥ written before mj; honorific/graphic transposition, same on the right end)

units.title: Column 3
units.section: Ptah, king of the Two Lands
units.summary: First preserved line of the theological text: Ptah is identified with 'this [land]' and said to be proclaimed with the great name [Tate]nen. Upper and lower parts are blank/erased; only a block of ~20 signs in the middle survives.
units.translation: […] Ptah: this [land] it is, which was proclaimed with the great name '[Tate]nen' […]
units.lacunae: y 690-1335: no carved signs; smooth, worn surface with a single diagonal scratch (x 495-520, y 1240-1265) and a faint horizontal edge at y~1330 that is probably the edge of the erasure. y 2085-2900: no signs; mottled millstone wear. The text is lost by deliberate erasure/wear at both ends, not by a carved vacat.
breasted_issues: Ptah's h (V28) drawn in two disconnected pieces (B4 + unnumbered) - one continuous sign on the stone.
B22 drawn as a distinct small sign; stone shows only a faint stroke (probably not a sign).
B27 pot drawn as a hexagonal ring rather than a vessel.
B29 (under the owl) and B7/B24 (under the vulture) are base strokes, not independent signs.
Swallow (G36) split into three boxes (B9, B34, B35).
B40 at the bottom (y 2842-2913) is Breasted's plate apparatus (line-number/annotation), not a hieroglyph; nothing is carved there.
units.confidence: high for the surviving block (signs are crisp in both reliefs and agree with Sethe 1928); low for 3.8, 3.12, 3.14.

words.note: Sethe assumes tꜣ 'land' (a single stroke in the Vorlage) was dropped before pn; no trace of it on the stone.
Only the -nn survives; the name is restored from 13c.

units.title: Column 4
units.section: Ptah, king of the Two Lands
units.summary: Continues the Memphite identification: the land of Upper and Lower Egypt; the Uniter of this [land] appeared as King of Upper and King of Lower Egypt (the last clause written in two parallel half-columns).
units.translation: […] it is the land of Upper and Lower Egypt. The Uniter of this [land] has appeared as King of Upper Egypt and has appeared as King of Lower Egypt […]
units.lacunae: y 690-1330: blank/erased, no traces in either relief (only isolated pits). y 2080-2900: no signs; worn and pitted surface (millstone wear).
breasted_issues: B49 (Upper Egypt sedge) and B68 (Lower Egypt papyrus) are badly drawn: the stone shows clear M26 and M16 plants.
smꜣ (F36) drawn but not numbered.
Several signs (B52 etc.) sit ~20 px higher in the copy than on the stone.
B58 owl drawn over-large, encroaching on the right half-column.
The two crowned determinatives (B61, B79) are drawn as indistinct figures; the stone does not allow better.
B62, B63, B80, B81, B82 at the bottom (y 2870-2918) are Breasted's plate apparatus (line numbers/annotation), not carved signs.
units.confidence: high for 4.1-4.16 and 4.18-4.21; low for the two crowned determinatives and for 4.10.

words.gloss: the land of Upper and Lower Egypt
words.note: Two city determinatives (O49) after the two plant signs.

units.title: Column 5
units.section: Ptah, king of the Two Lands
units.summary: Entirely blank. Sethe (1928) explains this as a deliberate vacat by Shabaqo's scribe marking a large worm-eaten lacuna in the old original; the stone confirms that no line of text was ever carved here (or that nothing survives).
units.translation: (vacat - no text)
units.lacunae: Whole column (y 690-2900). Upper part (690-1330) smooth and featureless in both reliefs; middle (1600-2060) shows only chips and pits (e.g. bright chips at x 650-690, y 1630-1720; a deep pit at x 700-720, y 1845-1870) and faint scratches near x 700-735, y 1880-2050 that do not form signs; lower part (2060-2900) millstone-worn. No trace of carved signs anywhere, including the zone at y 1340-2080 where cols 3, 4, 6 and 7 preserve text.
breasted_issues: None: Breasted also leaves col. 5 empty. B75/B80/B89 listed for this column belong to col. 4/6 or to his plate apparatus.
units.confidence: high that no signs are visible; medium on whether the blank is an original vacat (Sethe) or total loss - the surface in the text zone looks like the surrounding uninscribed surface, which favours an original vacat.

units.title: Column 6
units.section: Ptah, king of the Two Lands
units.summary: Isolated fragment set in mid-column with blank space above and below (Sethe: 'freier Raum'): 'the one who begot himself', so said Atum, 'who bore the Ennead'. Acknowledges Ptah as self-created creator.
units.translation: […] 'He who begot himself', so said Atum, 'he who bore the Ennead' […]
units.lacunae: y 690-1330: blank, no traces in either relief (probably the scribe's vacat, 'freier Raum'). y 2095-2900: no signs; worn surface with pits and a groove at x 845-860, y 2100-2150 (col 6/7 border). Signs 6.12-6.14 are worn.
breasted_issues: Breasted's copy is registered ~25-40 px too high through 6.7-6.15 (shape-match is fine).
B98 drawn only as a dashed fragment; the bird is complete on the stone.
B117/B103/B118-119 (the ms + psḏ group) are drawn more confidently than the stone supports.
B122 at the bottom is plate apparatus, not a sign.
units.confidence: high for 6.1-6.11 and the flags; low for 6.12-6.14.

words.note: Introduces the speaker after a quotation.
N9 doubtful; nine flags in three groups.

units.title: Column 7
units.section: Ptah, king of the Two Lands
units.summary: Short narrative fragment set in mid-column: the Ennead gathered to him (Geb), and he judged between Horus and Seth. Leads into the division of Egypt in col. 8.
units.translation: […] the Ennead gathered to him, and he judged between Horus and Seth […]
units.lacunae: y 690-1330: blank, no traces in either relief (only a single pit at x~845, y~1250). y 2075-2900: no signs (worn, pitted). 7.17 almost entirely lost.
breasted_issues: Leg sign drawn in two pieces (B127 + unnumbered stem).
Copy registered 25-35 px too high from the flags downward.
V28 drawn as disconnected loop + X.
Seth (B152) drawn as a full sign; only traces survive.
B153 at the bottom is plate apparatus.
units.confidence: high except 7.1-7.3 (identity of the group) and 7.17.

words.note: Reed + leg; reading uncertain, Sethe notes the unusual arrangement.

units.title: Column 8
units.section: Ptah, king of the Two Lands
units.summary: Full-length narrative line: Geb prevents the quarrel and installs Seth as King of Upper Egypt in Su, where he was born, and Horus as King of Lower Egypt where his father was drowned (continues into col. 9 with the place name Psšt-tꜣwj).
units.translation: He prevented their quarrelling: he set Seth as King of Upper Egypt in the land of Upper Egypt, at the place where he was born, in Su; and Geb set Horus as King of Lower Egypt in the land of Lower Egypt, at the place where his father had been drowned, [in Pesheset-tawy] (continued in col. 9).
units.lacunae: No major lacuna. Damaged zones: y 1065-1110 (Seth sign, 8.13) and y 1100-1190 (owl 8.14, cracked/abraded); y 2140-2350 worn (8.41-8.44 faint); y 2685-2745 (8.53) worn.
breasted_issues: B211 is only the head of an owl whose full body is visible on the stone (8.14).
B212 drawn as a stroke where the stone has a hemisphere t (8.16).
The nswt determinative (8.17) is broken into four boxes (B168-170, B214).
B228 is a tiny circle mis-placed ~40 px too high for the city sign O49 (8.33).
From y~1850 down the copy is registered 40-80 px too high (B229, B184, B185, B186 ... ); shapes match.
B209 and B205 are separate boxes for what are only the ends of water lines.
B235 is a ground line under the owl, not a sign.
B196 (large C-shape at 8.53) is not supported by the stone.
M26 and O49 at y 1380-1463 are drawn but unnumbered.
units.confidence: high overall (a well-preserved line, readings agree with Sethe 1928); low for 8.11 identity, 8.13, 8.14, 8.17, 8.53.

units.title: Column 9
units.section: Ptah, king of the Two Lands
units.summary: Ends the division narrative: [Horus king] in Pesheset-tawy; so Horus and Seth each stood on a place and were content regarding the Two Lands in Ayan - 'that is the boundary of the Two Lands' (the last phrase written twice). Text stops at y~2450; the rest of the column is blank (Sethe: 'Absatz').
units.translation: […] in Pesheset-tawy. So Horus and Seth: (one) stood on a place and (the other) stood on a place, and they were at peace concerning the Two Lands in Ayan - that is the boundary of the Two Lands. (Repeated:) The Two Lands in Ayan - that is the boundary of the Two Lands.
units.lacunae: No lacuna within the text (y 700-2450). y 2450-2900: blank (end of paragraph; Sethe 'Absatz'); only worn surface and a chipped patch at x 1060-1100, y 2720-2760. No traces of further signs below the last w-chick.
breasted_issues: From y~1450 down the copy is registered ~45 px too high (shapes match).
B265 is a ground line under the w-chick, not a sign.
B281/B293 cartouche-with-fish signs are rendered reasonably; no substantive errors found in this column.
B249 (shared with col. 8) is the reed of jm at the foot of col. 8, not a col. 9 sign.
units.confidence: high: very well preserved and the sequence matches Sethe 1928 sign for sign; medium for the phonetic analysis of 9.4 and 9.9.

Here written with t instead of ṯ.

units.title: Column 10
units.summary: Geb's first speech in the dialogue (10a: to Seth, sending him to his birthplace), the scene notes Seth / Upper Egypt (10b), and the start of the narrative on Geb's dissatisfaction with an equal division (10c).
units.translation: (10a) Geb, speaking words to Seth: “Go to the place where you were born.” (10b) Seth. | Upper Egypt. (10c) It was bad in Geb's heart that the share of Horus was (only) like the share of Seth.
units.lacunae: 10a ends at ≈1520; ≈1520–1650 is blank (end of the short verse line, as in 11a, not damage). No losses in 10b. 10c complete to ≈2890; surface rougher (millstone pitting) between ≈1840–2050 and 2280–2340 but all signs remain legible.
breasted_issues: 10c, first pšš.t (≈2360–2550): Breasted drew all five signs, but only the bar (B371/B372) carries a box id; the Q3, N37, X1 and Z9 are confirmed on the stone.
10a: Breasted's G17 (B348/B349) is fragmentary; a faint owl outline is visible.
Reference boxes in 10a ≈1250–1500 sit 30–40 px above the carved signs (registration/spacing of the copy, not missing signs).
units.confidence: high: top and bottom registers well preserved and the formula is fixed by 11a/12a; minor doubt only about the reading of the knobbed bar in pšš.t.

registers.note: two small fields: field 1 ≈1650–1745 (person addressed), field 2 ≈1745–1832 (land assigned)

units.title: Column 11
units.summary: Geb's second speech (11a: to Horus, sending him to the place where his father drowned), the scene notes Horus / Lower Egypt (11b), and the narrative of Geb giving his whole inheritance to Horus (11c).
units.translation: (11a) Geb, speaking words to Horus: “Go to the place where your father was drowned.” (11b) Horus. | Lower Egypt. (11c) Then Geb gave his inheritance to Horus — he is the son [of his son, his first-born] (continued in 12c).
units.lacunae: No real lacunae. 11a ends ≈1570 with a blank to 1650. In 11c the surface is pitted around 2320–2380 (the w-chick is reduced to traces) and a fresh flake sits at ≈2730–2750 just above Q3.
breasted_issues: 11c: Breasted's sign sequence is complete, but his copy compresses the lower half of the column: from ≈2100 down, every reference box sits 60–170 px above the carved sign (largest offset at the final G43, ≈2825–2895 on the stone vs. B416 at 2661–2725). Positions here are taken from the stone.
11b: B398–B400 are parts of the single Horus falcon, not separate signs.
11a: the suffix basket k (B395) is at ≈1428–1445 on the stone, below the viper, not beside it.
units.confidence: high for 11a/b, medium-high for 11c (all signs located, but the w-chick at 11.29 is only traces)

units.title: Column 12
units.summary: Geb's third speech (12a: to Horus and Seth together, 'I have separated you'), the scene notes (12b: field 1 blank, field 2 Lower and Upper Egypt), and the end of the narrative sentence identifying Horus as son of Geb's first-born (12c).
units.translation: (12a) Geb, speaking words to Horus and Seth: “I have separated (judged) you.” (12b) [blank] | Lower and Upper Egypt. (12c) … of his son, his first-born.
units.lacunae: 12a ends ≈1060; ≈1060–1650 blank (short verse line). 12b field 1 (≈1650–1745) is uninscribed (vacat, not erased: no tool marks). 12c ends ≈2210; ≈2210–2915 is blank (paragraph end, as Sethe noted).
breasted_issues: 12a: B444 (two small marks) is not supported by either relief.
12a/12c: Breasted's F13 is drawn as a narrow V; the stone has a broad, rounded U-curve in both places.
12a: B448–B450 are three boxes for a single water-line N35.
units.confidence: high

units.title: Column 13
units.summary: First of six parallel columns of Geb's speech to the Ennead (13a 'I have appointed…', 13b Horus / 'you as the wtw-jackal'), with the narrative 13c on Horus standing as king and the land united under the name Tatenen South-of-his-Wall, lord of eternity.
units.translation: (13a) Geb, speaking words to the Ennead: “I have appointed (13b, pointing to) Horus — you (to be) the wtw-jackal.” (13c) Horus stood (as king) over the land. Then this land was united, proclaimed by its great name: Tatenen, South-of-his-Wall, lord of eternity. There grew …
units.lacunae: 13a ends ≈1050; ≈1050–1280 blank (short verse line). 13b complete. 13c complete; the surface is rough (millstone pitting) between ≈1830 and ≈2240, which makes the small signs 13.20 and 13.22 hard to read, but nothing is lost.
breasted_issues: 13a: Breasted's plain bar B477 is a zigzag water-line N35 on the stone.
13a: an extra short horizontal stroke at y≈1004–1016 (x 1283–1322) is not in Breasted (or Sethe).
13c ≈2380–2600: several signs that Breasted drew carry no box id (lens, double bar, two small plant signs, a plant beside the wall sign); all are on the stone.
13c: B528 (beside the bird) is only a short stroke; Sethe's ꞽw is not verifiable.
B519 (long vertical, 1364–1457) is the field divider of 13b/14b, not a sign.
units.confidence: high for 13a/13b; medium for 13c (all signs present, but several identities are left open)

units.title: Column 14
units.summary: Second column of Geb's speech to the Ennead (14a 'you alone', 14b Horus / 'my inheritance'); 14c continues the narrative: the two crowns grow on Horus's head and he appears as dual king, uniting the Two Lands in the Wall-nome.
units.translation: (14a) Geb, speaking words to the Ennead: “(You) alone — (14b) Horus — (my) inheritance.” (14c) … the Two Great-of-Magic on his head. So it is Horus who appeared as King of Upper and Lower Egypt, uniting the Two Lands in the Wall(-nome), in the place where the Two Lands are united.
units.lacunae: 14a ends ≈1030; blank to 1280. 14b: surface worn (centre of the millstone wear), signs faint, a deep pit at ≈1395–1410. 14c ≈1800–2120 lies in the most heavily pitted band of the millstone wear: Breasted's signs there (B567–B579, B624, B633) cannot be verified and are marked uncertain. 2120–2350 faint but readable; 2350–2910 well preserved.
breasted_issues: 14a header: Breasted draws the disk N9 and the t (X1) but they carry no box id; both are on the stone.
B548 belongs to col. 14 (left limb of its cobra outline), not to col. 13.

14c ≈1800–2120: Breasted's copy shows complete signs in an area where the stone now has only pitted, abraded surface; these are probably restorations or readings from a squeeze/older photo and cannot be confirmed.
14c: F36 (B592) — Breasted's box covers only the top of the stick-and-heart sign.
units.confidence: medium: 14a/b and lower 14c secure; upper 14c largely unverifiable

units.title: Column 15
units.summary: Third column of Geb's speech to the Ennead (15a 'to that heir', 15b Horus / 'my inheritance'); 15c narrates that rush and papyrus were set at the double gate of Ptah's house, symbolising Horus and Seth reconciled and united.
units.translation: (15a) Geb, speaking words to the Ennead: “To that heir — (15b) Horus — (my) inheritance.” (15c) It came about that rush and papyrus were set at the double gate of the House of Ptah: that is Horus and Seth, reconciled and united; they fraternised so that their quarrel ceased …
units.lacunae: 15a ends ≈1225; blank to 1280. 15b worn (central millstone wear), pit at ≈1395. 15c ≈1790–1960 lies in a flaked/pitted band (top edge of the millstone damage) where Breasted's small signs B678–B681, B627–B628 are not verifiable. ≈1960–2910 legible; the Ptah shrine (B634) is clear.
breasted_issues: 15b: X1 (≈1490–1503) is drawn by Breasted but has no box id.
15b: B676, the tall sign below F44, is only a faint vertical trace; its reading as suffix .ꞽ is unconfirmed.
15c ≈1790–1960: Breasted's small signs here (B627, B628, B678–B681) cannot be confirmed on the flaked surface.
B717 and B657 (thin verticals) are column rules, not signs.
units.confidence: medium: 15a and lower 15c secure; 15b faint; a band of 15c unverifiable

units.title: Column 16
units.summary: Fourth column of Geb's speech to the Ennead (16a 'to the son of my son', 16b Horus / 'the Upper-Egyptian jackal'); 16c continues the narrative: Horus and Seth united in the House of Ptah, the 'Balance of the Two Lands'.
units.translation: (16a) Geb, speaking words to the Ennead: “To the son of (my) son — (16b) Horus — [the Upper-Egyptian jackal].” (16c) … [wherever] they reached … united in the House of Ptah, the ‘Balance of the Two Lands’, in which Upper and Lower Egypt were weighed.
units.lacunae: 16a ends ≈1085; blank to 1280. 16b worn (centre of millstone wear); field 2 reduced to faint lines. 16c ≈1800–1935 lost in a flaked band (Breasted hatches it, B720); ≈1935–2200 pitted with only faint traces; ≈2200–2910 legible.
breasted_issues: 16a: B711 is part of the first pintail duck, not a separate stroke.
16b: Breasted's fully drawn jackal-on-standard (B675) is not supported by the stone, which shows only a few lines; Sethe likewise saw only a vertical trace.
16c ≈1935–2200: several of Breasted's signs (B721–B723, B726, B764) cannot be verified in the pitted surface.
16c: the sign Breasted draws as a pillar (B737/B738/B776) is the balance mḫꜣt (as Sethe noted).
units.confidence: medium-low for 16b and the upper half of 16c; medium-high elsewhere

registers.note: field 1 ≈1280–1360 (Horus, pointed at), field 2 ≈1360–1655 (continuation of Geb's words)

units.title: Column 17
units.summary: Fifth column of Geb's speech to the Ennead (17a 'one who opened the womb', 17b Horus / 'Opener of the Ways'); 17c, mostly lost, ends with '… of Osiris in the House of Sokar', introducing the story of Osiris's death.
units.translation: (17a) Geb, speaking words to the Ennead: “(To) the one who opened the womb — (17b) Horus — Opener of the Ways.” (17c) [This is the land …] … of Osiris in the House of Sokar.
units.lacunae: 17a ends ≈1080; blank to 1280. 17b worn, with a round pit at ≈1370–1400 over the first sign of field 2. 17c: ≈1660–2370 lost (worn smooth by the millstone, with a large flake ≈1800–1950); only faint dashes at ≈2245 survive; ≈2380–2900 legible.
breasted_issues: 17c: Breasted's L-shaped sign B766 (2178–2219) is not on the stone; probably restored (Sethe also found nothing).
17b: B759 (horns) sits on a pit and cannot be verified; the jackal B761 survives only as scattered marks.
17c: the k of Skr (B779/B805) is drawn by Breasted as a lens identical to r.

A vertical incised column line at x≈4022 bounds the column on the left. B1513 is the divider dash; B1521/B1537/B1538 are numbers. B1535/B1536 (x 4048-4071, y 2742-2845) belong to the frame of the Ptah list (unit 48-52), not to this column.

The lower loop of the figure-8 sign is not supported.

units.title: Columns 48–52
units.summary: Tabular section. A horizontal heading (l.48) 'the gods who took form in Ptah' sits over four sub-columns (49-52), each with an upper entry (a: name, then a shrine with a standing Ptah figure as determinative, then an epithet below the shrine) and a lower entry (b) of which only the ends survive near the bottom of the stone.
units.translation: (48) The gods who took form in Ptah: (49a) Ptah upon the Great Throne … [epithet lost]. (50a) Ptah-Nun, the father who [made] Atum. (51a) Ptah-Naunet, the mother who bore Atum. (52a) Ptah the Great, [heart and] tongue [of the Ennead]. (49b) [Ptah …] … [who bore] the gods. (50b) [Ptah …] … [who bore] the gods. (51b) [lost]. (52b) [Ptah … Nefer]tem at the nose of Re every day.
units.lacunae: Heading and upper names well preserved. 49a/50a epithet zone y~1015-1070 eroded; under-shrine epithets y~1260-1480 very worn (a large feldspar crystal at x~4170-4230,y~1310-1365 mimics a dotted sign). A diagonal millstone/abrasion band crosses y~1450-1800 (left lower to right upper), and a horizontal gouge band at y~2200-2370 (millstone groove); everything between ~1480 and ~2390 is lost. Lower b-texts survive only y~2390-2860; 51b shows nothing. Bottom ruled line at y~2915.
breasted_issues: Top band boxes B1540, B1609, B1610, B1611 (and B1669) are drawn as long curved signs along the upper ruling; the stone shows only the straight ruled border there — they are not signs of the heading.
Heading: Ptḥ's p is drawn as an open 'C'; stone has a closed rectangle. The third god-flag (B1542) is drawn smaller than the stone warrants.
Shrines of 49a and 50a: Breasted draws full standing figures; the interiors are eroded — restored.
51a: the tall stalk-with-crossbar (unboxed, F31-like) is not visible on the stone; an extra rounded sign right of nw (B1619) is visible but undrawn.
52a: worn sign traces at y~985-1020 are not drawn.

52b: Breasted omits two crisp large lenses (y~2400 and ~2448) at the top of the surviving text, draws the thin bar at y~2424 as a small oval, and draws nb (V30) as a flat bar; the r–fnḏ–Rꜥ–rꜥ nb sequence becomes much clearer with them.
B1567, B1568, B1589, B1606, B1605, B1692, B1659 are Breasted's printed line labels (49b, 50b, 51b, 52b), not signs.
Breasted's dotted rectangle B1581 coincides with a natural crystal patch; only a bar beneath it is carved.
units.confidence: medium for the heading and the four Ptah names (clear on the stone); low for the under-shrine epithets and the b-register, which are traces read with help of the expected text (Sethe 1928) — those signs are marked uncertain.

units.title: Column 53
units.summary: Opening of the theology proper: a twin (split) column 'there came into being in the heart / there came into being on the tongue' something in the form of Atum; then 'great and mighty is Ptah', who gave [life/power to all the gods] and their kas through this heart and this tongue.
units.translation: There came into being in the heart, there came into being on the tongue (something) in the image of Atum. Great and mighty is Ptah, who hand[ed on …] … [to all the gods] and their kas … through this heart [and this tongue] …
units.lacunae: Diagonal wear/abrasion band y~1455-1625 (signs between swḏ and kꜣw lost). Below y~2105 no carving is discernible in the photo down to the bottom ruling (y~2915); at the bottom the column lies at x~4360-4440 because of the overall leftward slant of the columns. Breasted shows it blank; Sethe (fn. 4) states the space was NOT left free. The photo cannot settle it: the surface is pitted but shows no sign edges.
breasted_issues: B1695, B1755 above the top ruling belong to the horizontal line above, not col 53.
B1723-B1731 are fragments of Breasted's hatching of the wear band, not signs.
B1740: drawn as a tall stroke; stone has a broad bowl/basket sign.
B1741/B1742 split one lens into two boxes.
U15 (B1708/1709): the comb-like teeth are restored; only the bar is visible.
Twin opening: the signs for 'heart' and 'tongue' (B1699-1701, B1760-1762) are drawn more completely than the stone now supports.
units.confidence: medium: the twin opening, m tjt Tm, wr ꜥꜣ Ptḥ are clear in sequence and match the expected text; the section after the wear band (kas … this heart) is low confidence.

units.title: Column 54
units.summary: Twin top 'Horus took form in it / Thoth took form in it, as Ptah'; then the control of heart and tongue over every limb, because the heart is in every body and the tongue in every mouth of all gods, people, cattle and creeping things that live, thinking and commanding whatever it wishes.
units.translation: Horus took form in it (the heart), Thoth took form in it (the tongue), as Ptah. So heart and tongue gained control over every limb, [according to the teaching that it (the heart) is] in every body and it (the tongue) in every mouth of all gods, all people, [all cattle, all creeping things] that live — thinking and commanding everything that it wishes.
units.lacunae: Diagonal wear band y~1400-1630 (most of 'over every limb, according to the teaching that it is …'); horizontal millstone/wear band y~2295-2365 (end of mnmnt nbt / ḏdft nbt). Column slants left by ~70 px from top to bottom.
breasted_issues: Bottom group: the ring ḫ (Aa1) and nb basket of 'ḫt nbt' are placed ~50 px too low in Breasted's plate; the long diagonal hoe (mr of mrr.f) is drawn as a lens (B1804); an extra t (X1) next to the ring is undrawn.
B1784 and B1794/1849: baskets (V30) drawn as lenses or misplaced.
B1777 is a long horizontal sign, drawn much too small.
B1756 (scarab) and B1758 (lens), listed for this unit, actually belong to col 53's twin top; col 54's own top is B1757 + B1815/1817.
Several signs in the twin top (falcon, lens, t of Ptḥ) are drawn but not boxed by the OCR clustering.
B1810/B1811 below the bottom ruling are Breasted's line label, not signs.
units.confidence: medium: the lower half (n nṯrw nbw rmṯ … ꜥnḫ … ḫt nbt mrr.f) is clear on the stone and matches the expected text; the upper middle is worn and read largely through Breasted and the known text.

units.title: Column 55
units.summary: His Ennead before him is teeth and lips, i.e. the semen and hands of Atum: the Ennead of Atum came into being through his semen and fingers, but the Ennead is (really) the teeth and lips in this mouth that pronounced the name of everything, from which Shu and Tefnut came forth.
units.translation: His Ennead is before him as teeth and lips — that is, the semen and the hands of Atum. For the Ennead of Atum came into being from his semen and his fingers; but the Ennead is (in truth) the teeth and lips in this mouth which pronounced the name of every thing, and from which Shu and Tefnut came forth …
units.lacunae: Diagonal wear band y~1400-1500 (a few signs of 'jw psḏt Tm ḫpr …' lost); horizontal wear band y~2310-2365. Otherwise the column is among the best preserved in this part; bottom ruling y~2915.
breasted_issues: Unboxed but drawn signs (wavy n, bars, X1) recur; OCR clustering missed them.
Lower part: a clear lens at y~2250 and an hourglass/trapezoid sign at y~2425-2452 are not in Breasted's copy.
B1848 is a straight bar, not a hook; B1941 is a hexagonal/rounded small sign rather than a perfect circle; the small sign at y~2600 is a rectangle, not a circle.
Comb group B1883/B1966: stone shows stacked horizontal strokes; Breasted adds uprights.
Signs B1900-1902, B1983 inside the diagonal wear band are restorations.
units.confidence: medium: sign shapes are mostly clear; but the alignment of individual signs to words between y~800 and ~2400 is tentative — I have matched the expected text (Sethe/Breasted) where the signs allow, and left many signs unidentified rather than force them.

units.title: Column 56
units.summary: End of 'which bore the Ennead'; then the senses: the sight of the eyes, hearing of the ears, breathing of the nose report to the heart, which brings forth every understanding, and the tongue repeats what the heart has devised; so all the gods were born, Atum and his Ennead.
units.translation: … [which bore] the Ennead. The sight of the eyes, the hearing of the ears, the breathing of the nose — they send (their reports) up to the heart; it is the heart that brings forth every understanding, and it is the tongue that repeats what the heart has devised. So were born all the gods, Atum and his Ennead …
units.lacunae: No large lacuna: the diagonal band is above/left of this column; the horizontal wear band crosses y~2370-2400 (one or two signs). Bright feldspar patches at y~1515-1545 and ~2055-2075 imitate sign detail.
breasted_issues: Eyes: Breasted draws ear-like hooks (B2046/2047) where the stone shows further eye-shaped signs with pupils.
B1971/B2051: one long undulating sign split into two short ones.
B1981: star/cross-like sign drawn as a circle; B1975 crossed sign drawn as an L.
Several clear signs (lens at y~1275, triangle at y~1630, bar/lens pairs at y~1660-1690, basket at y~1830) are drawn but not boxed, or omitted.
B2030/B2031 below the bottom ruling are a line label.
units.confidence: medium-high for sign presence (this is one of the best-preserved columns); medium-low for the sign-to-word alignment in the middle, which I give only tentatively.

words.note: scarab, flags and nb clear; detailed alignment tentative

units.title: Column 57
units.summary: Creation by the word: every divine word came about through what the heart devised and the tongue commanded; so the kas and the hemsut were made, which provide all food and offerings, by this word; justice/injustice, life to the peaceful and death to the wrongdoer; then (end of column) all work and crafts, the doing of the arms and the going of the feet.
units.translation: … every divine word came about through what the heart devised and the tongue commanded. So the kas were made and the hemsut appointed, which make all provisions and all offerings, through this word. [Justice is given] to the one who does what is loved, [wrongdoing] to the one who does what is hated; life is given to the peaceful one and death to the wrongdoer. So too were made every work and every craft, the doing of the arms, the going of the feet …
units.lacunae: Column is generally well preserved. Signs y~1950-1975 and ~2055-2220 are worn (the 'justice/wrongdoing' clauses that Sethe brackets); the horizontal wear band crosses y~2330-2410. Bottom ruling y~2915.
breasted_issues: Many clear signs (eyes D4 at y~960, ~1875; lenses; baskets; the ankh at y~2250) are drawn but not boxed, or drawn at noticeably different positions.
B2131-2133: drawn as two small ovals and a rectangle; the stone shows a dome and a long bar with central upright (offering-table type sign).
B2152/B2085: drawn as a U-shape + dome; stone has a short bar with a small upright.
B2101 above the top ruling and B2098 below the bottom ruling are not signs of col 57.
units.confidence: medium: sign presence is high-confidence for most of the column; word alignment in the middle (y~1700-2450) is tentative and I have not forced identifications there.

units.title: Column 58
units.summary: Continues the 'heart and tongue' theology: the movement of every limb follows the command devised by the heart and uttered by the tongue; then Ptah is proclaimed maker of Atum and creator of the gods, Tatenen from whom all food and offerings came.
units.translation: … the moving of every limb, according to this command which the heart devised and which came out on the tongue, which makes the worth of every thing. Then it came to be said of Ptah: 'the one who made Atum, who caused the gods to come into being'. Tatenen, he it is who bore the gods; every thing came forth from him, as provisions and offerings (the two words cut side by side), as …
units.lacunae: The section y≈1690–1975 is heavily abraded (surface pitting, no millstone grooves here); signs there are traces only. Smaller worn patches at 2690–2780. From y≈2696 to 2830 the words ḏfꜣ.w and ḥtp are cut side by side (left and right halves of the column) rather than in sequence.
breasted_issues: Bird of the wḏ group (y≈995–1052) clearly cut but not rendered recognisably by Breasted (2240/2241).
First vulture of kꜣꜣ.t (y≈1170–1212) and its adjacent dome are not drawn as signs by Breasted.
House-plan O1 (pr.t, y≈1265–1293) is clear on stone; Breasted's 2179/2180 are fragmentary.
Water-line N35 at y≈2470 drawn as straight bars.
B2292/B2293 (circle and tall rectangle at x≈4800–4828, y≈2815–2902) are numbered with col. 58 in the box list but lie right of the column rule; they belong to col. 59.
B2229/B2230 lie below the bottom frame line (y≈2911–2923); nothing supports them as text.
Signs in the abraded zone 1690–1975 (B2192–B2201, B2274) are largely restoration; only scattered traces survive.
B2166/B2234 (y≈681–696) belong to the horizontal line above, not to this column.
units.confidence: medium: upper (700–1680) and lower (2030–2700) parts are clear and agree with Sethe's text; the abraded middle and the split-column ending are low confidence.

units.title: Column 59
units.summary: Ptah's supremacy is recognised and he 'rests' (ḥtp) content after making everything and every divine word; then the founding acts begin: he bore the gods, made the towns, founded the nomes and installed the gods.
units.translation: … divine offerings and every good thing. Then it was found and perceived that his strength is greater than (that of) the gods. And so Ptah was content (or: came to rest) after he had made every thing and every divine word. He bore the gods, he made the towns, he founded the nomes, he set the gods in [their cult-places] …
units.lacunae: Abraded zone y≈1700–1820 (m-ḫt) with only traces; minor wear at 2670–2760. No millstone damage in this column.
breasted_issues: The ibis at y≈1140–1185 is drawn by Breasted on a standard (Thoth emblem); the stone shows a free-standing ibis (gm), so his reading 'He is Thoth' rests on a misdrawing.
ms sign F31 (y≈2143–2198) and the adjacent S29 drawn as two plain arches.
Pick-in-ground U17 of grg (y≈2475–2502) drawn as a plain rectangle.
The sꞽꜣ cloth (fringed, y≈1238–1260) drawn as a closed rectangle; the vulture and following signs (B2313–B2318) are displaced by up to c. 40 px in the overlay.
Leopard heads of pḥty (y≈1385–1425) reduced to small blobs.
Lower part (2445–2810) is drawn by Breasted but has no box numbers; B2291–B2293, numbered with col. 58, belong here.
B2355 lies below the bottom frame line.
units.confidence: medium-high for 700–1700 and 1820–2900 (clear relief, agrees with Sethe); low for the abraded section 1700–1820 and for several small unexplained signs.

units.title: Column 60
units.summary: Ptah organises the cult: he establishes the gods' offerings, founds their shrines and makes their bodies to their liking; the gods then enter their bodies of every wood, stone and clay and of everything that grows upon him.
units.translation: … their [cult-places]. He established their offering-loaves, he founded their shrines, he made their bodies to their hearts' content. Then the gods entered into their bodies of every wood, of every stone, of every clay, of every thing that grows upon him …
units.lacunae: Worn patches at y≈985–1035, 1195–1245 and 1300–1440 (surface abrasion; no millstone grooves). Lower half (1600–2900) is well preserved.
breasted_issues: The flying duck pꜣ (y≈862–925) is clearly cut but drawn by Breasted only as disconnected strokes (2433/2434).
Three shrine signs (B2444, y≈1230–1284) are not verifiable; the stone shows bars and a water-line here with only faint traces above.
Three separate grain dots at y≈2565 drawn as a continuous bar (B2409).
Hook-shaped sign at y≈1505–1550 reduced to a bar.
Several unnumbered but drawn signs (N35 at 1290, X1 at 2620); B2394 (x≈4930–4939, y≈1835–1971) coincides with the column rule rather than a sign.
B2421/B2422 lie below the bottom frame line; B2473 belongs to col. 61.
units.confidence: medium: overall sequence agrees with Sethe and the relief is good below 1600, but many small signs in the smn/ḏt/ꜣwt-ꞽb passages are only tentatively identified.

units.title: Column 61
units.summary: The gods and their kas gather to Ptah, who is lord of the Two Lands; Memphis, the 'Great Seat' and granary of the god in the House of Ptah, is described as the source of the Two Lands' sustenance.
units.translation: … [in which they took shape]. Then all the gods gathered to him, and their kas, content and united, [with] the lord of the Two Lands. The granary of the god is the Great Seat, which gladdens the heart of the gods who are in the House of Ptah, the mistress of all life, through which the sustenance of the Two Lands is provided …
units.lacunae: Upper column (y≈700–1000) badly abraded: only isolated traces. Further worn zones 1400–1470, 1500–1700 and 2465–2510. Lower half well preserved.
breasted_issues: The enclosure at y≈2240–2312 is ḥwt-Ptḥ: the left inner sign is a twisted wick (V28) cut as stacked X-shapes, not an ankh-like loop.
A large rounded outline at y≈2160–2200 is visible on the stone but Breasted shows only a single vertical stick (2536).
Breasted's three ovals and ankh at y≈2565–2665 are registered c. 30–40 px too low.
Signs in the top 300 px (2489–2497) are drawn more completely than the worn surface supports.
B2485/B2618 lie below the frame line.
units.confidence: low-medium: much of the upper two-thirds is worn and many signs are identified only by shape; the overall sense rests on Sethe's restoration. Lower third is reliable.

units.title: Column 62
units.summary: Explains Memphis' role: Osiris drowned in its water while Isis and Nephthys watched; they saw him and were dismayed, and Horus ordered Isis and Nephthys to take hold of Osiris quickly and stop him from drowning.
units.translation: … because Osiris drowned in its water, while Isis and Nephthys were watching. They saw him and were dismayed at him. Then Horus commanded Isis and Nephthys at once that they should take hold of Osiris and prevent his drowning …
units.lacunae: Worn patches y≈1600–1710, 1795–1830 and 2455–2505; the rest is well preserved.
breasted_issues: Seat sign of Wsꞽr (y≈830–880) is L-shaped on the stone; Breasted draws a narrow rectangle (2629).

The names Isis and Nephthys are cut side by side twice (y≈1330–1452 and 2098–2213), each with t and seated-woman determinative; Breasted's pairs agree but several signs are schematic.
Water determinative at the foot (y≈2810–2870) is a bracketed pool (N36), not a set of loose wavy lines.
B2574 (large K-shape, y≈1610–1698) is not supported by the relief; B2669 coincides with the column rule.
B2618/B2619/B2681 lie below the frame line.
units.confidence: medium: overall structure (Osiris drowning, paired Isis/Nephthys, Horus' command) is clear on the stone; many individual signs in between remain uncertain.

units.title: Column 63
units.summary: Isis and Nephthys bring Osiris to land; he enters the secret gates in the glory of the lords of eternity, following the one who shines in the horizon, on the ways of Re in the Great Seat.
units.translation: … they turned [his] head in time and brought him to land. He entered the secret gates in the splendour of the lords of eternity, in the steps of the one who shines in the horizon, on the ways of Re in the Great Seat …
units.lacunae: Surface fairly well preserved; minor wear at y≈716–760 (gouge), 990–1040, 2540–2565 and 2695–2730. The right edge of the stone is broken away below y≈2650 but this column is not affected.

units.title: Column 64
units.summary: Final column: Osiris enters the earth in the royal fortress on the north side of the land; his son Horus appears as king of Upper and Lower Egypt in the embrace of his father Osiris, among the gods before and behind him.
units.translation: … and so Osiris came into the earth in the royal fortress, on the north side of this land to which he had come. His son Horus appeared as king of Upper Egypt and appeared as king of Lower Egypt in the arms of his father Osiris, in the presence of the gods who are before him and the gods who are behind him.

Checked the full crop beyond the green estimate; no additional attributable grooves found. The lower carving at y430-486 is neighbouring 14.13 and is excluded. Box encloses surviving cut only.

Domed loaf (x 115-244, y 195-228), larger than and partly left of the green box.

signs.note: leg bone (lens crossed by a stroke); dotted lost area below to the end of 14b

Very worn: a long diagonal back/wing groove from upper right (378,90, above the green box) to lower left (105,290) and a lower horizontal groove at y~298 (x 232-420) are the only traceable parts; head and forked tail not distinguishable.

Very worn. Only a short horizontal groove (likely the base of the ka-arms) at y~250 is visible in relief and native; arms not discernible. Uncertain. The clear U at the far left of this crop belongs to 14.20.

signs.note: twisted wick (ḥ), tall, right of the arms

Ka-arms: clear base groove y~218 (x165-248) and left arm up to y~158; right arm only faintly visible up to y~172.

signs.note: red crown on basket (left of pair); project "?" (pair of crowns/uraei); 14.23's box covers both

Only two horizontal grooves at y~290 are discernible (right one clear x365-505, left one faint x200-288), perhaps the bases of the paired signs; no outlines above them can be separated from the wear. Identity not confirmable. | fixup 2026-11-08: removed the right stroke (FULL x 2815-2861, y~3648): it is the basket of the right crown, Rothoehler R25, traced in 14.R25 (roth-005); only the left crown's base groove remains roth_agrees: the remaining groove sits at the top of his left basket; his crown body above it is not visible (millstone wear).

signs.note: white crown on basket (right of pair); covered by 14.23's box
signs.trace_notes: Right of the crown pair (R24 S4 left, this S2 right). Basket: sunk hollow, rim traced as closed outline (dark upper wall y~297-310, lit floor to y~342, small upturned ends at x~176 and ~327). Crown: worn; only its slanting body survives as a pale ridge from (198,166) down-right to the basket at (248,292), consistent in relief, native and photo (row-peak check), traced as one faint stroke along it; its outline, the knob and the separate shaft lines Rothoehler draws are not separable from the wear. His crown slants the same way (top-left to base-right). OVERLAP: 14.23 (R24) trace's right stroke (its x 365-505, = this kit x 167-307, y~308) lies on this basket; that sid should keep only its left stroke (this kit x 2-90). Not edited.
Heavily pitted/millstone-worn: no coherent groove of an owl can be separated from the pitting in photo, relief or native. Nothing traced.

Heavily pitted; no head outline discernible. The long wavy groove along the bottom of the green box (y~297) is the horned viper 14.26 (its box is misplaced below), not part of this sign. Nothing traced.

Box misplaced: the viper is the long wavy horizontal groove ~80 crop px ABOVE the green box (y~62-99, x95-365; low tail at left, body rising to the right). Head/horns at the right end not discernible. The green box itself holds only diagonal wiping marks.

signs.note: quail chick (left of pair); read before 14.27 (left to right); trace empty
signs.trace_notes: Pitted, criss-crossed by diagonal wiping marks; no quail-chick outline discernible in photo, relief or native. Nothing traced.

signs.note: plant: stem with hooked top and two side leaves; project M17 (ꞽw), trace empty
signs.trace_notes: Pitted area; no reed-leaf outline discernible in or near the green box (also checked ~80 px higher, since the viper 14.26 above sits that much above its box). Nothing traced.
Not discernible: pitted surface, no coherent groove in photo/relief/native. Nothing traced.

signs.note: short horizontal bar; project "?" (small signs); trace empty
signs.trace_notes: Not discernible: pitted surface, no coherent groove inside the box. A horizontal groove at y~97 (x300-500) lies above-right of the box and cannot be tied to this sid. Nothing traced.

signs.note: quail chick, left of Q3; project G5; trace empty

The clear domed sign in the lower half of this box (x230-420, y265-360) is 14.33 (domed ḫꜥ), whose box is misplaced ~50 full px below; not traced here. Nothing traced.
Nothing discernible in or around the green box (pitting only); the grooves at the left edge are 14.33's dome. No stool outline found. Nothing traced.

signs.note: hill with rays (ḫꜥ), domed; project "?" (domed sign); clearly carved, about 50 FULL px above its box

The domed sign (arch over a flat base with an inner slot) is clearly carved ~50 full px higher, at full ≈ x2800-2865, y4314-4346 (inside 14.31's green box). The L-shaped groove in this box (vertical x~120 + horizontal y~152) is a different sign (likely the bar 14.34). Nothing traced here.

signs.note: forearm (L-shape); project "?" (bar); carved just under the dome
signs.trace_notes: Box misplaced: the green box holds only diagonal wiping marks. The bar is the horizontal groove ~135 crop px higher (top edge of crop, y~13, x122-300), directly under the domed sign 14.33 — the same upward shift (~45 full px) seen for 14.33. A short collinear groove at x~380-440 may continue it (not traced). A vertical groove rising from its left end (seen in 14.33's crop) is not included.
No owl outline discernible (pitted, diagonal wiping marks). Only isolated horizontal grooves at y~90 (x150-280) and y~208 (x220-390) that cannot be resolved into an owl. Nothing traced.

signs.note: bird, fragmentary (owl?); he draws only the back and a leg; trace empty
signs.trace_notes: Box area dominated by diagonal wiping marks; no owl/chick outline discernible. Short horizontal grooves at y~403 and y~490 below the box cannot be resolved into this sign. Nothing traced.

Tall narrow sign: a small loop on top (x218-263, y310-362), a vertical stem down to y~560 and a crossbar at y~445 (ankh-like). Box placement roughly right but sign extends ~100 px below it. Worn; all faint.

signs.note: bee (bꞽt), left; he draws the bee LEFT of the sedge; project boxes have L2 right and M23 left; trace empty
signs.trace_notes: No bee discernible: the box is blank/worn except a short horizontal bar at its top (y~170, x165-290), the right one of a side-by-side pair of bars (full y≈4781) that more likely belong to the X1 pair or another sign. Nothing traced.

Very worn. A faint Y-shaped pale form (junction ~(287,352), stem to y~560) was tried but does not sit on real grooves (score <0.95); not traced. The clear horizontal groove in the box (y~210, x200-320) is one of a side-by-side pair of short bars (other at x400-510) whose identity is unclear (possibly the two X1 of 14.40/14.41 or bases of other signs). The loop-topped stem with side shoots traced as 14.36 (full ≈ x2870-2917, y4673-4760) might in fact be this sedge. Nothing traced.

Not found in or near the green box (worn; nothing loaf-shaped there). Candidate t's: a side-by-side pair of short horizontal bars at full y≈4781 (x≈2808-2843 and 2873-2913), ~70-90 full px above the boxes, under the sedge/bee area; or the bar at full ≈(2843-2880, 4923). Attribution too uncertain to trace.

Lung-and-windpipe: windpipe stick x~260 from y~74 down to the heart-shaped lung (x223-302, y278-376); short crossbar at the top (y~70). Sign lies ~70 px right of and well below the green box (box covers only empty stone left of the stick).

Lower of the two long tꜣ bars (second in reading order), y~46, x186-502; ~100 px above the green box (which is on blank stone). Plain bar, no grains visible.

Worn. An arched outline (back/head of the bird, tail at lower left x125, top ~(265,290), front dropping to (335,338)) and a clear horizontal groove at y~384 (x340-452), read as the owl's base/feet. Rest of the owl (breast, head top) not discernible. Low confidence for the arch.

Ladder-form wall: left rail x~205 (faint, vertical) with five rungs at y~159,209,270,319,368 extending right to x~240-290. Occupies the upper part of the green box; the inverted-L groove below (y~430-530) is a different sign (not traced).

Foot/leg: vertical leg groove x~153 (y158-374, faint) and clear horizontal sole y~375-388 running right to the toe at x~300. Fits the green box.

Lung-and-windpipe: clear top crossbar y~156 (x155-240), faint windpipe stick x~200 down to y~345, and one diagonal groove (172,356)-(230,396) from the lung at the bottom; rest of the lung not discernible. Fits the green box.
Upper tꜣ bar (first of the pair), plain long bar y~148, x150-458; fits the box. No grains visible.

Worn owl: long diagonal back line from tail (205,412) up to head (368,190) and a clear base/feet groove y~413 (x315-400). Breast/face not discernible. Low confidence on the reading.

Worn reed leaf: faint left edge (x~145, y200-330), rounded top (y~190) and right edge (x~242, y200-400), visible in relief and native. Somewhat wider than the green box (extends ~15 px right). Bottom/stalk not discernible.

Ring-shaped disk (psd), clear closed groove, centre ~(237,229), r~35 crop px. Fits the green box. No lower crescent/half-obscuring line visible.
Bread loaf: half-dome outline (top arc y~178, flat base y~201), x140-257. Fits the green box.
Foot: vertical leg x~152 (faint, from y~100) and clear sole y~293 running right to toe x~290; sign extends ~50 px right of and above the green box.

signs.note: three nṯr-flags on a common bar; drawn as one connected group
signs.trace_notes: Row of god-flags as a horizontal bar (y~179, x118-392) with three pendant verticals at x~212, 300, 388 down to y~395. The long vertical at x~437 is the column rule, not traced; the L at far left is the foot 15.4.

Cobra (I10) of the dd-mdw group, right-facing, drawn as one long outline: tail at lower left (137,502), rising in an S-curve to the long straight back at y~237 (x 240-430), then a vertical step up at x~436 to the head/hood bar at y~140 (x 440-507). Clear in relief, photo and native along its whole length. Tail end below y~505 not visible. The vertical at x~478 (y 290-545) is the staff 15.7, not traced here; the long vertical at x~570 is the column rule. Rothöhler draws the same sinuous cobra with the head at top right; his head end is a rounded blob where the stone shows a squared step and bar. Lock is moderate because of the steep curve and verticals.

Staff (S43) of the dd-mdw group, right of and under the cobra's head (15.6): one straight, very slightly slanting vertical groove from y~270 to ~507 (full x~2947-2950, y~1685-1764). Clear in photo (pale groove) and relief, weaker in native as usual for verticals. No knob or forked end visible. Rothöhler draws a thin vertical staff at the same place: agrees. The green box was the whole dd-mdw group; real extent is the narrow box given. Low lock is expected for a vertical groove under top light.

Water ripple N35 directly below the dd-mdw group, full x~2847-2970, y~1787-1808: one zigzag groove with 8 peaks across the column, its right end running down steeply to (510,108). Clear in relief, photo and native (the lit lower walls show as pale triangles under each peak). BOX MISPLACED: the green box (y 176-247) is ~120 crop px (~40 full px) too low; it sits on the top of the stool Q3 (15.9). Rothöhler draws a zigzag of about the same width here: agrees.

Stool Q3, cut as a SUNK upright rectangle (sunk, pale floor), full x~2889-2919, y~1837-1900. Traced the rim as a closed outline: top rim under the deep shadowed upper wall (y~42), sides at x~123 and ~212, bottom rim under the lit lower wall (y~222). Top and bottom clear in relief, photo and native; the sides are weaker (vertical edges under top light), the right side lower half is diffuse. The pale diagonal streak inside the hollow is surface texture, not traced. Box: the green box (y 145-358) is ~110 crop px too low; the long groove at y~350 inside it is the viper 15.10. Rothöhler draws an upright rectangle here: agrees (he draws it as an outline).

Horned viper I9 (right-facing), full x~2831-2960, y~1928-1952: long body groove with a low step, tail at left (145,120), rising at x 250-310 to the straight back at y~89 up to x~455. Clear in relief, photo and native. Head/neck rising to the upper right (455,90)->(532,59) is faint: the surface there is a pale broken patch; the upper edge has a groove in relief and native but the head, horns and eye are not resolvable. BOX MISPLACED: the green box (y 174-268) is ~85 crop px too low; it covers empty surface and the top of the reed 15.11. Rothöhler draws a viper here with the head raised at right: agrees.

Reed leaf M17, cut SUNK (pale floor), full x~2904-2921, y~1978-2095. Traced the rim of the tall leaf as a closed outline: pointed tip at top (205,68), widening to the slanted base at y~320-340 (base rim clear: bright lit wall in relief and native), plus the short stem below it at x~187 down to y~412 (faint, a narrow pale groove in photo, weak in relief/native). Sides are weaker under top light, as expected for steep rims. Rothöhler draws a tall shaded leaf with a short stem at the same place: agrees. Green box roughly right but ~70 px too low at the top; the leaf starts at y~68.

Forearm D36 drawn as a long L: short upright at the left end (x~201, from y~138) turning at a rounded corner into the long horizontal arm groove at y~252 running right to x~534 (full x~2861-2972, y~2103-2141). Clear in relief, photo and native. No hand detail (thumb or fingers) visible at either end; a faint pale streak continues the upright up to y~100 but has no groove edge in relief/native, so it is not traced. Rothöhler draws the same L shape here (upright at left, long horizontal arm): agrees.

Quail chick facing right, cut as a SUNK diagonal hollow (head top-right at ~(390,120), body/tail running down-left to the tail tip (140,370)); rim traced as one closed outline. A short horizontal groove at y~480 (x 268-370) is the base/foot line, faint but in relief and native. Legs (Rothoehler: two strokes from the belly to the base) are not distinguishable on the pitted surface between y 380 and 475; not traced. roth.png draws the bird ~25 crop px too low and the head slightly left; by shape and sequence (below R12 forearm, above R14 leg-bone) it is his R13.

Leg-bone: a narrow diagonal oval (clear in photo, relief, native), traced as its two sides meeting at the lower-left end (303,232-245); the upper-right end opens into a faint stroke up-right to (445,148) = one prong of his forked end (second prong not seen; bright spall at (410-450,185-215) is damage). Below it a clear long shallow-curving groove (200,292)-(382,262) is traced as part of this sign: it corresponds to the long tail of his drawing (he draws the tail continuing the oval's axis down-left; on the stone it lies lower and flatter, so it may also be a separate stroke). roth.png sits ~30 crop px lower-left; shape and sequence (R14, last sign of 15a, below the chick R13) agree.

signs.note: Horus falcon on a short base stroke
signs.trace_notes: Very worn falcon (centre of millstone wear), placed where the green box is. Only the long sloping back line survives, in three faint pieces on one curve from the head end at upper right (757,447) down to the tail at lower left (530,713): steep upper part x724-757, middle x684-728, tail x530-582. The gaps between them are abraded. Its size and slope match the col-14 field-1 falcon (14.11) at the left of this crop. Head, breast, legs and the base line can't be made out. The horizontals at y~720 and y~800 are register lines and are not traced. Box placement agrees with the green box.

Small quail chick facing right on a badly damaged surface (deep round hole at (205-300,75-165) just upper-left of it is damage, not traced). Traced: the back as a faint diagonal groove (304,174)-(371,106), the breast/front line from below the head (416,135) down to (342,245), and the clear underside/tail groove (222,280)-(338,252) with the tail at the left. Head top and the legs he draws (down to ~y 355 here) are not distinguishable; the short groove at (270-320,~250) above the tail line may be the wing tip, not traced. roth.png draws the bird ~35 crop px too high; shape and sequence (first sign below the falcon R15, above forearm R17) fit his R16.

Forearm drawn by Rothoehler as an L (short upright at the left = upper arm, long horizontal arm/hand to the right). On the stone: the long horizontal groove is clear (crop x 303-630, y ~307; FULL ~2887-2996, y ~2948), the upright at its left end is faint (x ~302, y 248-305; seen in relief and native, the photo only shows a pale patch there). The hand end at the right is not distinguishable. roth.png draws it ~75 crop px (~25 FULL px) too low; the 1901 green box (y 190-276) lies above the carving, which is at y ~307. Sequence fits: below chick R16, above loaf R18.

Loaf t, cut as a SUNK half-round hollow (domed top, flat base, clear and deep); rim traced as a closed outline. FULL ~2922-2961, y ~2985-2999. roth.png agrees in shape; sequence fits (below forearm R17, above leg-bone R19). Long faint horizontal groove ~110 crop px above (y~55) belongs to forearm R17.

signs.note: leg-bone (oval with forked end); his b-field ends here
signs.trace_notes: Very worn; low confidence. Placement checked: the clear X1 (15.18) sits just above at y~265-295, and the col-14 leg-bone (14.15) is at the same height at the left edge of this crop (x0-250, y460-620). Inside the green box, only a hooked groove survives, faint in both relief and native: a lower-left limb rising from (514,648) to (568,584), then a narrow, near-vertical groove up to (594,484). It reads as the leg-bone lying steeply, lower end at lower left, like 15.14 but steeper. The upper/right outline and the knob end can't be made out. The large pale patch at x600-690, y460-540 looks like a smooth flaked area, not a cut, so it is not traced. The trace_score lock is low for the lower stroke because it is steep and the score favours horizontal grooves; in relief it is a lit wall with a darker area above-left.

signs.note: tall uncertain sign below the leg-bone; he draws nothing here
signs.trace_notes: Stone-only position (Rothoehler draws nothing here: this stretch falls in the gap of his EB 15 label row between 15b and 15c). Surface very rough and pitted. Only two fragments are consistent in relief, native and photo: a short horizontal groove (208-252, y ~384; FULL ~2943-2958, 3237) and a short faint vertical below its left end (x ~206, y 398-455; FULL ~2943, 3242-3261), together an L/hooked fragment. The tall shape the 1901 box suggests (y 145-527) is not visible; the rest of the box is pitting and pale spalls. Identity cannot be determined; it may not be a sign at all (could be damage).

Scarab, worn but recognisable. Traced: the two upper (front) legs as arcs rising from the ends of a clear horizontal groove at y ~350 (left arc clear (300,358)-(258,258); right arc faint (448,343)-(388,222)); together they look like a large ring above the body. Body: faint left side running down from the junction (308,362) to a clear small cup-shaped lower end (345-385, ~495). Lower left leg: clear arc (259,520)-(309,592). Faint short diagonal at (405-458, 395-410) = probably a middle right leg. Not visible: the body's right side, middle left leg and lower right leg (Rothoehler draws all six legs). roth.png draws the sign ~100 crop px (~33 FULL px) too low; shape and sequence (first sign of 15c, above water R22) agree.

Water line n: wavy/zigzag groove across the column (FULL ~2905-3011, y ~3492-3507). Traced along the dark-to-bright upper edge of the cut; the lit band below it is ~25-30 crop px wide, so it may be cut as a shallow sunk zigzag band (its lower edge at y ~215 is not traced). Right half (x 300-512) is clearer than the left (x 195-300), where pale spalls confuse the surface; marked faint overall. Peaks ~(248,178),(322,180),(368,182),(468,182). Fits Rothoehler's N35 (R22) by shape and sequence (below scarab R21, above the long bar R23 at y ~330).

signs.note: long flat bar with a small raised element on top; both unidentified
signs.trace_notes: One long, clear horizontal bar groove, x480-795 at y~494-496, directly below the N35 (15.22) zigzag (y~350-390). It is clear in photo, relief and native. Only one bar is cut: there is no second parallel bar above or below. The sign is about 315 crop px wide, much wider than the typical 143 px. Above the bar's middle (x590-690, y410-480) there is a faint pale ^-shaped area between two dark hollows. It might be a worn sign sitting on the bar (e.g. hills of dw), but it shows no clear groove edges, so it is not traced. The oblique marks below the bar (x560-720, y530-610) are not part of this sign. Placement agrees with the green box (the box was already right).

signs.note: small sign beside the bird on flaked surface; he draws nothing here

signs.note: hook ending in a small ring; project X1; left of the next sign

signs.trace_notes: Nothing traced. The green box and its surroundings are flaked and pitted (the band at 15c ~1790-1960 where Breasted's small signs can't be verified). I see no carved round outline in photo, relief or native. Inside the box there is only a small pale chip at x472-512, y488-505, which looks like a raised flake with no paired groove edge. Below the box, at x490-525, y580-650, there is a deep oval dark pit with no lit lower wall, so it reads as damage, not a cut sign. The domed arc at x240-340, y490-530 lies in the 15.26 X1 box and is not this sign. identity_ok is left true because nothing on the stone contradicts it; the sign simply can't be verified, and its position is unconfirmed.

signs.note: short curved stroke with a dot to its right; dot may be a separate mark
signs.trace_notes: fixup 2026-11-08: RE-CHECKED with the rebuilt kit (15.R29 was marked lost). A short curved groove at kit ~(28-110, 258-283) = FULL ~2933-2961, y 3868-3876, left of and ~70 kit px above the reed R30's stem (15.30), is visible in relief and native (dark upper wall over a lit floor) and as a dark curved band in the photo. By sequence (below N35 R28, above/left of reed R30) it is in the slot of his R29 'short curved stroke', so traced as R29, faint. Doubts: it could be the top of the reed R30 (roth-006), and its curvature (sagging in the middle) does not clearly match his hooked arch; his dot to the right is not visible on the flaked surface. roth.png in this region sits ~50 kit px too high and somewhat left (his reed vs the traced 15.30).

Very uncertain. The surface here is heavily scaled (many short horizontal flake edges). The only candidate for his reed is a narrow dark vertical band at x ~277, y 335-425 (FULL ~2956, 3895-3925), visible in relief and native as a dark vertical without a clear paired lit wall; traced as a faint stem. It lies ~25 crop px right of and ~10 px below roth.png's stem, and in the right place in the sequence (below R29, above the lens R32 at FULL y ~3966). Above it a clear curved groove (230-300, y 270-305; FULL ~2941-2964, 3873-3885) could be the reed's leaf/forked top or Rothoehler's R29 'short curved stroke' (whose roth.png position is ~35 px left, ~50 px higher); not traced here because it cannot be assigned safely. The stem's lower part (y > 430) and the fork are not visible.

signs.note: short vertical stroke; project '?' narrow vertical
signs.trace_notes: Nothing traced. I see no carved narrow vertical sign (no paired groove edges) in or around the green box, in photo, relief or native. The one candidate is a uniformly dark, sausage-shaped hollow at x535-600, y535-625 (about 30 crop px wide, slanting from upper left to lower right). It has no lit lower wall, is as dark as the pit directly below it (x505-560, y635-685), and lines up with the diagonal flaking that runs across this area (upper left to lower right). So I read it as damage, not as an incised stem. If a later reviewer takes it as the stem, its centre line runs (548,540)->(590,618). Breasted's narrow original box (x492-531) has only pits. The D21 lens of 15.32 is clear below, at x290-510, y805-860, which confirms the column position.

signs.note: mouth r (lens); he draws no X1 beside it (15.33)

FULL ~2932-3027, y ~3985-4005. roth.png draws it ~35 crop px too low and ~25 px left; shape and sequence (first lens below the reed R30/stroke R31) agree. The horizontal flake edges above and below (y ~210, ~300) are surface scaling, not traced. Rothoehler draws no X1 beside it; see 15.33.

signs.note: X1 beside the first lens; he draws only the lens

Rothoehler draws no X1 here; I cannot fully rule out that this groove is a long left tail of the lens.

signs.note: mouth r (lens); he draws no X1 beside it (15.35)

FULL ~2949-3027, y ~4038-4054. The groove running on left from the left tip (x <190) is the X1 R35 already traced (15.35), not part of this sign. roth.png draws the lens ~30 crop px too low; shape and sequence (second lens, below R32/R33) agree.

signs.note: X1 beside the second lens; he draws only the lens
signs.trace_notes: Low, flat loaf traced as its single upper groove, x396-508, y~496-509. It runs left from the left tip of the 15.34 D21 lens (lens at x510-700, y480-520), on the lens's axis, and falls slightly at its rounded left end (x396). The loaf's base line isn't visible: a deep pit (x390-450, y510-570) and abrasion lie beneath it. I can't fully rule out that this groove is a long left tail of the D21 lens, though 15.32/15.33 above show the same X1-left-of-D21 arrangement. The real position is about 55 crop px left of the green box and at its lower edge.

signs.note: square head on a long shaft (mace/hammer-like); project O6; not an enclosure in his drawing
signs.trace_notes: Only the SHAFT is traceable: a narrow sunk vertical channel (rim traced, 'sunk') at crop x 196-218, y 300-470 (FULL ~2949-2957, 4126-4183), dark in photo, relief and native, matching Rothoehler's shaft position closely. Sign separated from the loaf R37 (crop x 360-486, y 203-250), which stands to the right of the head level. QA off_cut (lock 0.94) is expected for a narrow steep sunk channel (weak evidence for verticals); the channel is visible in photo, relief and native.

signs.note: loaf t; right of the previous sign

Rim traced as a closed outline. Odd lighting: the loaf area reads PALE in photo/relief/native with a dark shadow under the flat base (y 250-265), unlike a normal sunk hollow; it may be a hollow whose floor is lighter stone, or partly flaked. Shape and position fit X1 well, hence faint not restored. Green 1901 box (x 144-245, y 146-202) is ~20 FULL px too high.

signs.note: falcon (Horus); followed by his stippled lost zone (y 2860-2925)

That line may be the chick's ground line or the top of R4 (15.45), whose box starts at 821. Head-to-body joins and the back of the head are lost. | fixup 2026-11-08: ADDED the base bar (roth-007): a short sunk bar with a lit floor at kit x 234-404, y 510-531 (FULL ~2978-3035, y 4740-4747), clear in relief, photo and native, where Rothoehler draws the chick's base/foot bar; traced as its rim (sunk). X1 loaf at the upper edge of the estimated green box: shallow domed groove and both ends visible in relief and native. A separate basal groove is not distinguishable beneath the broad lit wall; no speculative closing line added. No continuation into adjacent signs.

Foot b, worn but complete as Rothoehler draws it: vertical shin groove (x~177, y 158-375), sole groove along the bottom (y ~375-385, to x~308) and a fainter diagonal from the shin at y~290 down to the sole near x~270, which is the edge of his filled heel triangle (the triangle is not visibly sunk on the photo, only its diagonal edge). signs.note: three nṯr-flags on a common bar; drawn as one connected group

Cobra: body groove clear and deep, from the tail end at (170,525) up in a curve to the long top line ending at x~434 (y~291); the head is the short clear horizontal groove at y~194 (x 447-517), as in Rothoehler's hooded head. Rothoehler continues the tail further down-left to ~(110,590); on the stone the groove ends at ~(170,525) (a bright blob at (110-135,513-534) is a separate pit). The staff R7 (vertical at x~490, y 300-560) is not traced here.

Staff mdw: single straight vertical groove at x~435 from y~286 to ~460 (clear in relief, photo and native), faint to y~490. Rothoehler draws it widening into a thick foot at the bottom; on the stone there is a round pale chip at (418-448, 515-543), just past this kit's bottom edge (513), which looks like flake damage rather than a cut, so it is not traced. Water line, clear: zigzag of ~6 crests from (245,170) to (574,162), both ends turning down. It lies ~40-60 crop px ABOVE the 1901 green box (box y 185-258 is empty stone); Rothoehler's red zigzag in roth.png also sits ~40 crop px too low, matched by sequence (water between the cobra/staff and the first pintail duck R9). Pintail duck G39 facing right, between the N35 zigzags at y~285 (16.8) and y~810 (16.10). Back groove (590-746, y~515-537) and long belly/tail groove from the pointed tail at (474,608) to the breast (746,540): clear. Head/neck at the right lies in a pale flaked patch x735-780, y490-560: no groove can be followed, not traced. Upper edge of the tail (x480-590) not separable from the belly groove. One slanting leg (655,594)-(686,657) and a feet/base groove y~659 (x598-785), both faint; this hooked leg+base is presumably Breasted's B711. Inner wing line not resolved. Box 16.10 N35 is ~100 px too low (zigzag actually at y~795-830).

signs.note: water n; 1901 box ~50 FULL px too low

Pintail duck facing right, ~70-85 crop px higher than roth.png draws it (matched by sequence: second duck after the second water line R10). Traced: small head at the top (x 488-548, y ~85-104), the front of the neck and breast curving down into the belly/underside line to the pointed tail at (229,301) (clear), the back from the tail up to the rear of the neck (faint: worn, partly broken by pits and diagonal scratches), a clear base/foot groove at y ~348 (x 405-555) and one faint leg at x~458 (y 302-345). The bright oval at (465-495,170-185) inside the neck is a pit, not traced.

signs.note: Horus falcon over a small ⊥-shaped stand; the small stand under the tail is counted with the falcon
