Falcon: a sunk diagonal silhouette (head top right at ~(450-485,165), body sloping down-left to the tail at ~(275,375)), traced as its rim in two faint halves (back = upper-left, front = lower-right); pale floor with lit walls in relief and native; no detail of head, wing or legs survives. Stand: a small sunk blob at (380-416, 346-374) under the breast (his top of the stand) and a horizontal groove at y~426 (x 378-522) = his stand bar; the stem joining them is not visible. Rothoehler draws the bird ~25-50 crop px left of the carving and the stand bar ~15 px higher. The long horizontal at y~550 is the register rule; the circle at (510-600, 260-370) right of the bird is surface texture (no consistent groove), not traced.

signs.note: jackal (back outline only) on a standard with a long pole; pole drawn as a separate long vertical through the stippled zone
signs.trace_notes: Standard with animal (E18), very worn, matching Rothoehler's col 48b field 2, which also shows only a fragment: a rising back line, a horizontal platform and a long separate vertical pole. Stone: back line rising from (560,489) to y~462 and running right to (692,455); platform groove y~588 (x485-712); long vertical pole x~680 from y~868 to ~1190 (visible in relief, photo and native, weak by orientation). All faint. The animal's body, head, legs and the short stub under the platform he draws are not visible; a dark smooth patch (x560-640, y540-590) between back and platform may be the worn body, not traced. Box: carving lies in the left-centre of the large green box, x482-715, y450-1195.

signs.note: bird (body outline with one leg stroke), head of 16c; project D21 small arched sign
signs.trace_notes: EMPTY: surface lost. The whole area (this crop and ~300 crop px around it, checked with an extended view) is flaked and pitted with no consistent groove edge. Rothoehler draws a diagonal bird outline (head top right at ~(330,130), body down-left past the crop's lower-left corner, one leg stroke near (220,370)). On the photo only a faint diagonal pale edge runs from ~(226,158) to ~(72,284), roughly parallel to his back line ~60 crop px further up-left; it shows no paired groove walls in relief, nothing in native and no support in the evidence map, so it is not traced. The pale patches at (205-265,140-170), (300-340,290-310) and (230-260,335-355) are flake scars (probably what 1901 read as the small arched D21). No leg stroke visible.

signs.note: diagonal stroke (feather-like); project '?' bars; ~30 FULL px apart
signs.trace_notes: Narrow straight diagonal groove (clear in relief and native) from top right (176,-71) down-left to (90,30), then a fainter, shorter groove turning left along y~26-32 to x~12 (the base of his 'feather'). PAST CROP EDGE: the stroke lies mostly ABOVE this crop (y<0); traced from extended views (work/scratch/roth-009/ext.py) in this kit's frame. The green box (145-263,144-227) holds only flake scars. Rothoehler's narrow diagonal stroke R15 matches in shape and direction (his lower end shows at (110-160,30-50) in roth.png, ~30 crop px right of the carving). Surface around is badly flaked.

signs.note: two short horizontal dashes side by side; below his outline of the lost zone
signs.trace_notes: Uncertain. No long bar is visible in the green box (x450-880). The only cut-like feature in it is a small sunk hollow x774-846, y490-525 (arched dark upper wall, flatter base: sunk; visible in relief and native), traced as a closed rim, faint; it could equally be a pit. A pale flat trapezoid at x590-660, y455-545 to its left looks like a flake surface, not traced. Below, a continuous groove y~590-600 (x550-880, broken into pale segments) lies in 16.18's N35 box and is presumably that water line. Rothoehler col 48c starts below the flaking with two short dashes side by side, then N35: the hollow (and possibly the trapezoid) fits his dashes, so roth_agrees=true with low confidence. roth.png overlay is unreliable here (~300 FULL px off; his F36 sits on this box).

Lung-and-windpipe F36 inside the green box, very worn, the same pale-filled form as 15.47: top crossbar y~580 (x468-580, its left end rising), windpipe stick x~530-535 from y~588 to ~800 (pale band with shadowed right side), and a pale roughly triangular lung x505-600, y808-872 directly under the stick (rough pale patch; its outline is approximate). All faint. Above the box (y220-450) the oblique back and neck of bird 16.19 are visible. Rothoehler col 48c: bird + tall narrow sign, then F36 (T-stick with heart) - agrees in sequence. His roth.png overlay is ~300 FULL px off (it puts his house sign on this box), so it was matched by sequence only.

Almost entirely lost: heavily flaked surface, no head, breast, legs or feet visible. Only one faint diagonal groove survives, from (148,518) up-right to (244,415), soft but present in relief and native (not distinct in the evidence map, so uncertain); it fits the lower back/tail line of Rothoehler's owl (his outline sits ~40 crop px higher: his tail at ~(150-230,440-480)). Rothoehler draws a full bird from head (~(380-440,155-190)) to tail; the rest of it is not visible on the photo. The clear horizontal groove at y~513 (x 320-460) is R23 (his short horizontal stroke), not traced here; R20's lower end lies above y~129.

signs.note: ḥwt enclosure (corner square lower right), holding the next three signs; project '?' large rectangle (House of Ptah)
signs.trace_notes: Large rectangular enclosure (hwt / House of Ptah), fits the green box well: clear top line y~457 (x456-735, turning down at the right end to (752,472)) and clear bottom line y~818 (x461-792, with a small step at x~650); left side faint at x~456-461 (vertical, weak evidence). Right side not visible (no vertical groove at x~750-800). Interior: only scattered short pale marks (e.g. y~600 x620-690, y~735 x650-710, y~690 x500-570) indistinguishable from the surface flecks; the Ptah figure and other contents are not traceable. Rothoehler: in sequence (F36, bird, then a framed hwt with Ptah, ka-arms and corner square, then bird) this is his hwt-Ptah enclosure; agrees on the frame, his interior signs and corner square are not visible on the photo. roth.png overlay is ~350 FULL px off here (it lays his two long bars and curved line, i.e. 16.31-16.33, onto this box); matched by sequence.

signs.note: twisted wick ḥ (inside the enclosure, left); covered by 16.25's box
signs.trace_notes: Worn; only the lower part of the wick survives. Traced: the splayed foot as an inverted V (apex (206,440), legs to (160,473) and (283,482)), faint but present in relief, native and the evidence map, and a faint near-horizontal groove at y~408-412 (x 200-268) just above it, which fits the lowest twist of Rothoehler's wick. The upper twists (his loops up to ~y 235 after his ~45 crop px offset) are not visible: the upper left of the enclosure is a pale flaked patch (150-230, 250-320) with no consistent groove. Separated from neighbours: the enclosure R24's walls (top bar y~185, bottom bar y~545, left wall x~110, right wall x~420) are not traced; the short horizontals at (325-370,~325) and (330-385,~460) on the right half belong to the stool R27 and loaf R28. Rothoehler draws the whole enclosure ~45 crop px higher than the carving.

signs.note: stool p (inside the enclosure, upper right); covered by 16.25's box
signs.trace_notes: Inside the hwt enclosure (16.R24), upper right. Only the BOTTOM edge of Rothoehler's upright rectangle (stool p) is visible: a clear horizontal groove at crop y~291, x 140-199 (FULL x ~3161-3180, y ~4454), in photo, relief and native, matching the base of his rectangle in position and width. Sides and top are not visible (scattered flecks only; native evidence hints at a top edge near y~175 but not convincingly in the photo), so not traced. Separated from R26 (wick, left part of the enclosure, x<~110) and R28 (loaf, ~45 FULL px lower) by position.

signs.note: loaf t (inside the enclosure, lower right); covered by 16.25's box
signs.trace_notes: Loaf (X1) inside the hwt enclosure (16.R24), lower right: one short clear groove crop x 159-221, y ~195-202 (FULL x ~3164-3185, y ~4498-4500), dark upper wall over a bright lit wall, in photo, relief and native; traced as a single slightly domed stroke (as the loaf R30 below). No separate base visible. Matches Rothoehler's flat loaf at the lower right of the enclosure, above his corner square (corner square not visible). Separated from R27 (stool base ~45 FULL px higher) and from the enclosure's bottom frame line (~25 FULL px lower) by position.

Worn bird (G43 type), facing right; matched by sequence (first sign below the hwt enclosure R24, above the loaf R30). Traced: (1) the BACK, a long straight diagonal groove from the nape at crop (470,134) (FULL ~3197,4572) down-left to the tail tip near (156,423); its upper half is visible in relief and photo, its lower half (x<~260) only faintly, parallel to and ~15 crop px left of (2); (2) the TAIL UNDERSIDE, a clear groove from the tail tip (160,436) up-right to an apex at (288,330) (FULL ~3136,4637), with a sharp lit wall in photo, relief and native; (3) from the apex a faint groove down-right to (360,411), the belly/leg line. This inverted-V at the apex matches Rothoehler's underside apex closely (within ~5 FULL px). Not visible: head (only a pale blotch near FULL 3185-3200, 4562-4580), breast line, legs and feet, base. Rothoehler's back line lies ~10 FULL px further left in the upper half; otherwise his shape agrees.

Loaf (X1): one clear, gently arched groove crop x 178-292, y ~147-161 (FULL x ~3121-3159, y ~4694-4699), dark upper wall over a strong bright lit wall, clear in photo, relief and native; the groove evidence is a single dome-shaped band (ends lower than the middle), i.e. the loaf's rounded top. No separate flat base groove is visible (the dark area below, y~175-245, is uncut dark stone), so only the dome is traced. Rothoehler's loaf has the same width and shape but sits ~13 FULL px higher in roth.png (same offset as his ∩ R31 below, whose top bar is the groove at crop y~255 here). Sequence: bird R29 above, ∩ R31 below.

∩-shaped sign, matched by sequence (below the loaf R30, above the two long bars R33/R34); it lies at the TOP of this kit, not in the green box (the 1901 box, FULL y ~4772-4802, is ~40 FULL px too low and covers only flecks). Traced: the top bar, a clear groove crop x 158-316, y ~17 (FULL x ~3106-3158, y ~4729), in photo, relief and native (in kit 16.28 it is the groove at crop y~255; it may start a little further left, near FULL x ~3090), and the right leg, a faint vertical groove at x ~320 from the corner down to y ~88 (FULL 3160, 4732-4752), visible in photo and relief (weak evidence: vertical). Left leg not visible (only short horizontal flecks below the left end). Rothoehler draws a ∩ with two equal legs; it agrees in width and in the right corner; his left leg is not visible on the photo. roth.png places it ~13 FULL px too high (above this crop).

Empty: no carved groove can be followed in or around the green box (x450-573, y452-573) - only pale flat flake surfaces, small dark pits (e.g. (550,545), (500,480)) and a large dark hollow at x600-650,y560-640 (a pit). The box lies at the right edge of column 16, beside X1 16.28 (sunk loaf x175-300, y375-445). Rothoehler draws X1 above a 'Π' sign with a small 'L' sign to its right; this sid presumably corresponds to his 'L' (or 'Π'), but the stone shows nothing here. The 'Π' may be the bar y~475 (x150-300) below the X1 with possible legs at x~175 and ~300 down to y~560 (in 16.30's area / between 16.28 and 16.30; not traced here). roth_agrees=false only because he draws a sign the photo does not show.

First of Rothoehler's two long bars between the ∩ (R31, top bar at FULL y ~4729) and the knob bar R35 (FULL y ~4903-4920); matched by sequence. Note: the 1901 box of 16.31 (FULL y 4847-4859) lies on the SECOND bar (R34, FULL y ~4850), ~30 FULL px lower than this one.

Second of Rothoehler's two long bars (R33 at FULL y ~4818 above, the knob bar R35 below); matched by sequence. The broad pale patch under the left half (y~130-160) is surface wear, not traced. The 1901 box of 16.32 (FULL y 4863-4874) is ~15 FULL px too low and narrower than the carved bar.

signs.note: long bar with raised knob at the right end; cf. 17.10 'bar ending in a ball'

The paler streak at x450-520, y485-520 below the left end is surface wear, not traced. Gardiner not determined (cf. a rope/snake-like sign); identity '?' left as is.

signs.note: loaf t over the bird's back
signs.trace_notes: Loaf (X1) over the bird's back: a clear groove crop x 124-238, y ~106-118 (FULL x ~3115-3153, y ~4954-4957), dark upper wall over a broad bright lit wall (the photo shows a shallow lens-shaped sunk hollow ~8 FULL px tall); traced as one centre line along the upper (dome) edge, as the other loaves of 16c (R28, R30). No separate base groove. In photo, relief and native. Matches Rothoehler's loaf above the bird R38 in shape and place (his is drawn ~5 FULL px lower in the overlay). Sequence: after the knob bar R35, before the bird R38.

signs.note: small sign right of the bird 16.36; he draws nothing there
signs.trace_notes: Stone-only position (Rothoehler draws nothing here). The only feature in and around the green box is a dark, nearly rectangular sunk hollow crop x 152-238, y 142-200 (FULL x ~3208-3236, y ~4941-4961) at the right edge of the column, level with the loaf R36 and the head of the bird R38: straight top edge with a pale lip above it, straight right side, dark smooth floor; visible in photo, relief and native. Rim traced (sunk; edges placed by eye), conf faint because it may be a spall/damage scar rather than a carved sign: its shape is regular but it sits against the column's right edge, it has no incised detail, and Rothoehler omits it. Nothing carved in the lower part of the green box (FULL y ~4965-5003). Identity unknown ('?'); if carved, a small upright/oblong sunk sign.

Worn bird (G43 type), facing right, matched by sequence (after the knob bar R35 and the loaf R36, before the bar R39 at FULL y ~5074). Traced: the BACK, a clear straight diagonal groove from crop (341,242) (FULL ~3170,4999) down-left to the tail tip (175,365) (FULL ~3114,5040), and the BASE line under the feet, a clear horizontal groove crop x 284-504, y ~360 (FULL x ~3151-3224, y ~5038), both in photo, relief and native; Rothoehler draws both (back and base stroke) in the same places. Not visible: head, neck and the upper back above FULL y ~4995 (only pale blotches, a ring-like relief shape near FULL 3180-3210, 4968-4992 is not convincing), breast, underside and legs (a pale vertical streak near crop x 330-345 is not a clear groove). The loaf over the back (R36, FULL y ~4957) and the dark hollow at the column's right edge (R37/16.35, FULL ~3205-3232, 4940-4960) are separate and not traced here.

Plain horizontal bar, clear: groove y~466 (top edge of the pale lit wall), x446-648, filling the green box. A second, shorter bar on nearly the same line lies just right of the box (x680-780, y~462; separated by a ~30 px gap) - not traced here; it may be the other half of a 2-part sign or the end of this bar. Pale wear patch below (x600-760, y500-545) is not a cut. Above, bar y~360 (x555-770) lies under bird 16.36 (its base line?). Rothoehler: no confident counterpart. His col 48c has bird -> U38-like balance group -> bird + tall sign -> bar with crossing, long bar, small 'Z'-like sign + short vertical; the roth.png overlay puts that small sign + vertical on this bar and the right-hand bar, but his overlay in this column is ~300-400 FULL px off elsewhere, and the stone shows two horizontal bars, not a vertical. roth_agrees=false = unresolved, not a definite contradiction.

signs.note: plant with three heads on a ring base; covered by 16.38's box (left half)
signs.trace_notes: Plant with heads on a ring base (left of the balance R41), matched by sequence (after the bar R39 at FULL y ~5074, before the bird R42). Traced: (1) the central head, a clear sunk inverted triangle (umbel) crop x 205-285, top edge y~160, apex (244,222) (FULL ~3127-3154, 5109-5130), rim traced closed; (2) the top edge of the ring base, a clear horizontal groove x 224-294, y~346 (FULL ~5171); (3) its bottom edge, faint, x 234-296, y~442 (FULL ~5203). Not visible: the two side heads, the stem(s) and the sides of the ring (only blotchy texture; vertical edges get weak evidence and none is clear in photo AND native). Rothoehler's three-headed plant agrees in place (central head at the top, ring base at the bottom); his side heads are not visible on the photo. Separated from the balance R41 by x: everything traced here lies at FULL x < ~3157, the balance's post and bars at x > ~3170.

Balance (U38), right of the plant R40, matched by sequence. Traced: the BASE, a clear horizontal groove crop x 447-553, y~491 (FULL ~3189-3224, 5204); the CROSSBAR at y~383 (FULL ~5168), clear on the right (x 525-588) and faint on the left (x 412-492), with no visible groove where it crosses the post; the POST, a faint vertical groove x ~474-494 from y~250 to the base (FULL x ~3198-3205, y ~5123-5201), seen in relief and native and as a pale streak in the photo (steep: weak scorer evidence). Not traced: the top hook. The area above the post (crop x ~400-556, y ~130-200; FULL ~3173-3225, 5083-5107) is a broad pale irregular patch with a strong horizontal edge at its top (y~149) that looks like flaking rather than a cut hook. Rothoehler's small pan ticks on the crossbar are not visible. His balance agrees in place and proportion (post, crossbar, base); his crossbar is narrower than the carved one. The small marks at the foot (old 16.39, phantom) are not separate here.

Worn bird (G43 type), facing right, matched by sequence (after the balance R41, left of the tall narrow sign R43, before the knotted bar R44). Traced: (1) the TAIL/UNDERSIDE line, a clear groove from crop (357,365) (FULL ~3182,5306) down-left to the tail tip near (180,425) (FULL ~3123,5326), in photo, relief and native, matching Rothoehler's underside running from the tail up to the legs; (2) the BASE line under the feet, faint, x 335-457, y ~431 (FULL ~3175-3215, 5328). Not visible: head, back, breast and legs. A large dark wedge-shaped area (crop x ~190-280, y ~180-320; FULL ~3126-3156, 5244-5291) cuts across where the back should run; its lower-right edge (crop ~(246,337)-(331,259)) could be the back but reads as the edge of surface loss, so it is not traced. Bright blobs at the tail end (crop x 110-240, y 430-465) are uncertain and not traced.

Faint. Rothöhler's column strip (col 16 = his 48c) shows a tall narrow sign right of the G43 bird, above the two N16; his overlay in this kit is badly misaligned (~350 FULL px too high: the rect/N35/rect/G43 he draws at y30-920 here are 16.45-16.48), so matched by sequence. On the stone the matching feature is a narrow vertical groove inside the green box: pale band x~515-545 with a dark left edge, y~368-520 (clear in photo, relief and native as a left/right edge pair), fading and drifting slightly left to ~(519,592). Traced as one centre line (w 14); its exact outline (leaf vs simple stroke) is not resolvable. Vertical, so lock is weak. NOT the sign: the deep dark slanted groove at x636-714,y512-925, which lies right of the col 16|17 rule and runs into it lower down (damage; it also appears in 17.25's kit at x300-380,y815-1220).

signs.note: bar with a knot in the middle
signs.trace_notes: N16 bar with knot, sequence-matched: on the stone below bird R42/tall sign R43 (16.41 ends FULL y~5314) come a bar with a knot at FULL y~5360 (this sign), a long plain bar at FULL y~5395 (R45), two short joined bars at FULL y~5447/5459 (R46), then the rectangle R48 (16.45). KIT MISPLACED: the green box (crop y 214-259) lies on R45's bar; R44 is ~95 crop px higher, at crop y~117 inside the orange R42 box (traced there). Bar: clear groove x 258-512 at y~120. Knot: a small loop hanging below the bar at x 363-395 (photo clear, relief/native show its dark hollow at (379,137)); loop outline faint. Rothoehler draws the knot as a small swelling on the bar; here it hangs below it.

Plain bar, sequence-matched (below the knot bar R44 at FULL y~5360, above the short joined bars R46 at FULL y~5447/5459). KIT MISPLACED: the green box (crop y 214-253) lies on R46's short bars; R45 is the long groove ~180 crop px higher at crop y~33, at the very top of this crop (traced there). Long clear groove x 232-598 (relief, photo, native); right end turns slightly up. Above it a dark shadowed band (y ~8-30) suggests the bar may be cut as a broad shallow channel; centre line traced at the dark-to-bright edge. Rothoehler: plain bar at the same place (his slightly shorter on the right).

Two short parallel horizontal bars, sequence-matched as Rothoehler's small two-bar sign R46 (between plain bar R45 at FULL y~5395 and rectangle R48 16.45 at FULL y~5500). KIT MISPLACED: green box (crop y 146-208) lies on blank stone; the sign is ~100 crop px higher, at crop y 44 and 80 (FULL y ~5445 and ~5457), in the upper part of the crop (and inside the orange 16.43 box). Upper bar x 182-299, its right end turns slightly down; lower bar x 180-318. No joining stroke between them is visible (the gap y 60-72 is uncut); a faint pale patch at (315-335, 60-72) right of the bar ends is not a clear groove and is not traced. Rothoehler draws a smaller sign (two bars joined by a short middle neck) ~25 FULL px further left; same place in the sequence, so taken as the same sign; the joint he draws is not visible on the photo.

signs.note: small vertical stroke; right of 16.44; no project sid
signs.trace_notes: Small vertical stroke right of the two-bar sign R46 (16.44), as Rothoehler draws it (his Z1 at the right of the column, slightly higher than R46). On the stone: a narrow pale vertical groove at x~200-203, y~152-211 (FULL x~3222, y~5443-5462), clear in photo, faint in relief, barely in native; vertical, so the scorer's evidence is weak. Its position (right of R46's bar ends at crop x~96 here, level with R46) matches his. The kit green box (x 144-171) is ~30-40 crop px too far left. Faint: could be a worn stroke; nothing else in the area is a candidate.

signs.note: upright rectangle (stool p); project '?' small upright rectangle
signs.trace_notes: Upright rectangle clearly carved, sitting in the upper part of the green box (y 387-538, green box ran to 615): top groove y~392, bottom groove y~531 (bright lit lower wall below it), side grooves x~469 and ~566 (seen in photo/relief/native, weak in the scorer as they are vertical). Interior floor reads paler than the surface, so it may be cut as a shallow sunk rectangle; outline traced at the groove/rim line. Pale diagonal streak at (440-480, 440-480) is a wipe, not a cut. Box essentially correct (≈-60 px top shift). Rothöhler (col 16 strip, matched by sequence: ¤|, rect, N35, rect, G43) draws an upright rectangle here; his overlay in this kit is ~350 FULL px too high (his column end falls at y~265), so roth.png position is unusable.

Water line N35, sequence-matched (below rectangle R48 = 16.45, above rectangle R50 = 16.47). Long shallow wavy groove x 164-444 at y~168-195 (FULL y ~5586-5595), clear in relief, photo and native; left end rises to the upper left, a distinct peak at x~327, otherwise only low ripples (no sharp zigzag teeth resolvable). Green box correct. Right of x~445 a groove continues steeply down-right to ~(478,227): probably a crack / the column edge, not traced (it may be the water line's downturned end). Rothoehler draws a regular toothed water line at the same place; the teeth are not resolvable on the photo.

signs.note: upright rectangle (stool p); project '?' small upright rectangle
signs.trace_notes: Upright rectangle (Q3 per Rothoehler), sequence-matched (below the water line R49 = 16.46, above the bird R51 = 16.48). Top groove y~143-148 and bottom groove y~262 (bright lit lower wall below it) clear in relief, photo and native; side grooves x~158-162 and ~236 only faint (vertical, weak light pairing). Interior reads paler and rough in the photo, like R48 (16.45): possibly a shallow sunk rectangle; outline traced at the groove/rim line. Somewhat smaller than R48 (about 26x40 FULL px vs 35x50), as in Rothoehler. Green box roughly right (sign ~10 px left, box ran ~35 px too low).

Bird (G43 per Rothoehler), last sign of col 16, sequence-matched (below rectangle R50 = 16.47, whose bottom groove is the short bar at crop (264-341, ~128) here: not traced). Traced: the head as a thick sunk diagonal hollow (372,246)-(418,206) (clear, all three layers); two parallel diagonals running down-left from it, the back (upper, faint-to-clear) to the tail tip ~(190,393) and the front/breast line (lower, clear) to (268,393); the tail/underside horizontal groove x 176-268 at y~397 (clear); the base line x 238-434 at y~507 (clear, right end turning slightly down). Not traced: the legs Rothoehler draws between body and base (x~265-300): no consistent vertical groove, only pitted surface; a sloping groove right of the body, (372,395)-(485,423), which he does not draw (crack or wiping mark? it is not part of his bird). roth.png in this kit is ~65 crop px too far left and ~60 too low (his rectangle R50 lands at y 55-185 vs 0-120 on the stone); after that shift his head, back, tail and base match.

Goose (G38) facing right, in the green box (shared with 17.2 N9 disk at x~720-810,y~500-590, not traced). Body cut deep and wide (near-sunk): back groove (452,668)->(652,606) under a heavy shadow band; breast edge (652,606)->(603,695) and belly (452,670)->(603,696) are the edges of the pale cut floor (faint). Short inner line (565-610,~651) = wing edge, faint. Neck and head: hooked groove rising from the breast (650,600) to the head top (640-705, ~506); the front of the neck/beak underside not visible. Legs/feet not visible (surface below y~700 shows only the separate stroke at x545-665,y~730, which belongs to the sign below). Same layout as the geese in cols 16 and 18. Rothöhler draws the same goose (neck rising from the breast, head turned right) with short legs on a base line and X1 below-right; the legs/base are not visible on the photo, so not traced.

signs.note: disk psḏ; 1901 box also covers the goose
signs.trace_notes: Disk N9: a clear incised ring (crop x ~438-512, y ~198-268), right of the goose R1 and above the loaf R3, as Rothoehler draws it (his circle sits within ~5-10 crop px). The lower half of the ring is cut broader/deeper than the top; a small notch/pit on the inner right side at y~240. The ring interior is not sunk. Separated from the goose by clear stone between them (x ~400-435).

Loaf X1, sunk: a half-round hollow with a deep shadowed upper wall and a pale flat floor (crop x ~162-258, y ~137-179); rim traced as a closed outline (the lower edge placed by eye at the floor's lower limit). Lies below the disk R2, as Rothoehler draws it (his loaf ~10-15 crop px higher, same x).

Foot D58 facing right: a long narrow vertical groove (leg, x ~186-191, y ~166-378, clear in relief and native) ending in a sunk wedge-shaped foot pointing right (x ~192-274, y ~366-422; deep shadowed upper wall, pale floor), rim traced as a closed outline. Matches Rothoehler's L-shaped foot; his drawing sits ~15-20 crop px higher and ~5 px left. Not to be confused with the long vertical grooves left of it (x ~60 and ~120), which are the column rule and a sign of the neighbouring column.

signs.note: three nṯr-flags on a common bar; drawn as one connected group
signs.trace_notes: Row of nṯr-flags as Rothöhler draws it (col 17 strip: a long bar with three pendant poles, D58 'L' to its left): bar groove clear at y~480, x463-700; first pole x~537 (y500-635) and second pole x~613 (y495-595) faint but visible in photo, relief and native as pale bands with paired left/right edges (vertical, so scorer evidence is weak). Rothöhler's third pole would fall at x~700-710: only an ambiguous pale spot at (690-700, 560-620), crossed by a diagonal scratch (640,590)->(950,710); not traced. Lower ends of the poles lost. Roth overlay is ~110 FULL px high and ~35 FULL px left here; matched by shape/sequence.

Cobra I10 facing right: body = long horizontal groove at y ~289 (x ~260-421, clear: deep shadowed upper wall), bending down-left into the tail (x ~196-255, y ~290-392); the tail below y ~340 is faint and stops ~y 392 (Rothoehler sweeps it further down-left to ~(120,465); not visible on the photo). Neck rises at x ~424 (faint vertical, relief+native) to a sunk head/hood x ~416-496, y ~194-222 (rim traced closed). Rothoehler's drawing sits ~15-20 crop px higher; shape agrees. The pale smooth area right of/below the tail is surface, not cut.

EMPTY: surface lost. Rothoehler draws a short vertical staff right of the cobra's tail (R6) and above the bird's head (R8); on the stone that place (expected crop x ~140-185, y ~90-300, i.e. his position shifted ~+40 crop px down, as for R6 and R8) is rough, flaked surface with no groove edge in photo, relief or native. A weak vertical edge at x ~172, y ~300-400 (photo gradient only) is too low, close above the bird's head (y ~455), and has no native support; not traced. Box given = expected place.

Standing bird facing right, worn. Traced: long diagonal back from the tail tip (183,386) up to the neck (402,205), clear; neck and head top up to ~(452,137), faint (sunk pale head x ~410-452, y ~135-155); a second, lower diagonal from the tail tip to (330,330) = belly/wing line, faint; two legs (x ~266 and ~300-310, y ~402-494), faint but visible in photo and relief; long horizontal base/foot groove y ~495 (x 268-445), clear. Breast line from neck to legs not traceable (no consistent groove). Rothoehler's bird has the same layout; roth.png draws it ~40-50 crop px too HIGH and ~25 px left (his foot line y~450, stone ~495; his head ~(400,115), stone ~(430,140)).

Horns (F13) as a wide U, opening up, clear in photo, relief and native: long left arm from (527,452) down to the bottom (~y605, x620-725), shorter right arm up to (815,515) (its tip merges into a pale flaked patch at x790-830,y500-560). Two short faint strokes hang from the bottom (to (668,640) and (732,634)): the small stand Rothöhler draws under his U. Rothöhler (col 17 strip, below the G43 bird 17.8) draws the same U with a stub; his overlay in this kit is misaligned and shows nothing at this spot. Green box essentially right (sign ~+40 px right).

signs.note: bar ending in an oval knob (ḫt)
signs.trace_notes: Horizontal bar (x ~172-352, y ~189, deep and clear) ending on the right in an elongated oval knob (x ~352-488, y ~158-212), as Rothoehler draws it (his drawing ~10-25 crop px higher). Inside the oval the surface is rough; a further short horizontal line under the oval at y ~222 (x ~370-470) shows in photo but is weak in relief/native, and Rothoehler does not draw it: not traced (probably the oval's lower wall/damage).

signs.note: short vertical stroke; left of X1 17.11; no project sid
signs.trace_notes: Short vertical stroke Z1 (x ~203-207, y ~196-282), worn but visible as a pale vertical groove in photo, relief and native. Located from Rothoehler's plate: his Z1 stands ~28 plate px left of the loaf R12 with its foot level with the loaf's base; the loaf is carved at FULL ~3234-3275, 2148-2165 (R12 kit), which puts Z1 at this crop x ~200, y ~190-285: exactly this groove. roth.png draws it ~50 px left and ~40 px high (x ~155, y 150-235). New sign: not covered by any neighbour's traced box; the R10 bar ends at this crop y ~15 above it, the loaf R12 is right of the crop (x ~366+).

Loaf X1, sunk: half-round hollow with a deep shadowed upper wall and pale floor (x ~148-266, y ~165-210); rim traced as a closed outline, lower edge by eye. The pale flakes just below-left (x ~120-155, y ~200-226) are surface damage, not part of the sign. Rothoehler's loaf (with Z1 R11 to its left) matches; roth.png draws it ~35 crop px high and ~40 px left.

signs.note: Horus falcon on a short base stroke
signs.trace_notes: Falcon on a base stroke, facing right, badly worn. Traced: long diagonal back/tail line from (230,436) up to (360,353), clear; the neck/back of the head rising from (373,300) to the head top ~(442,208), and a short front (breast) line down from the head to ~(440,275), both faint (a narrow pale elongated shape in photo, outlined in relief); the short horizontal base stroke x ~390-490, y ~463, faint. A deep round pit at (360-410, 330-395) interrupts the body between back and neck (damage, not traced). Legs and the inner details Rothoehler draws (leg down to the base) are not traceable. Same layout as Rothoehler's falcon; roth.png sits ~25-30 crop px too high.

signs.note: horns wp; stone shows a pit here
signs.trace_notes: Nothing traced: surface lost. The sign's place (between the G5 falcon above and the N31 road below, whose two long grooves are clear at y~790-840, x520-850) is taken by a round ground pit/cup, rim x~435-785, y~385-650, centre ~(610,515), with radial striations inside. The bright strokes inside it ((530-580,540-590) and the lower-right rim (650-760,580-620)) are the pit's own walls and flakes, not a U-shaped groove. Rothöhler draws horns F13 (U) here in his column sequence; not visible on the photo. His overlay in this kit is far off (col 17 drawn ~300 px right, ~750 px high). The green box (452-733, 450-672) sits on the pit, so the 1901 position is consistent with the sequence.

Road N31: two long parallel horizontal grooves, upper y ~250-256 (x ~182-490), lower y ~290-298 (x ~190-508), clear in photo, relief and native. Rothoehler draws the two lines closed at both ends, with shrub tufts rising from both ends and a small hump below the lower line; on the stone the ends are not closed visibly and the tufts are not traceable (rough surface above the upper line). A small cluster of short pale marks below the lower line at ~(330-360, 340-375) may be his hump but has no clear groove edge; not traced. roth.png sits ~35 crop px high.

signs.note: three vertical plural strokes; project Z2; he draws them left of the X1
signs.trace_notes: Z3, three plural strokes LEFT of the loaf R17 (Rothoehler), not below it as the 1901 copy has it (its Z2 box below-right of the loaf shows no strokes). PAST CROP EDGE: this kit (FULL x from 3240) starts right of the strokes; traced in kit coords from extended views (work/scratch/roth-012/ext.py, fullv.py). Only the rightmost stroke is discernible: a faint vertical groove at FULL x ~3234, y ~2942-2963 (kit x ~-19, y 48-112), visible as a pale vertical line in photo, relief and native, ~10 FULL px left of the loaf's left tip, exactly where Rothoehler's rightmost stroke falls once his drawing is shifted onto the loaf. The other two strokes (expected at FULL x ~3219 and ~3204) are not distinguishable from the flaked, pitted surface there (a pale flake at kit x ~-86..-58, y 76-104 is damage). Not traced: two of three strokes.

Loaf X1, sunk: half-round hollow, deep shadowed upper wall and pale floor (x ~160-260, y ~158-198), rim traced closed, lower edge by eye. Rothoehler's R17 (his order: Z3 R16 left, then this loaf); the plural strokes stand LEFT of it (see 17.16), not below. roth.png draws the loaf ~12 crop px high and ~25 px left.

signs.note: jackal (neck/back curve and one leg only)
signs.trace_notes: Very worn; only fragments, all faint (edge seen in photo AND native). Read as the jackal facing right: back groove (552-643, ~544), a short stroke at the upper right (692-768, ~486) where the raised head/snout should be, and base strokes at y~701-705 (x435-555 and 680-730) = feet/standard line. Legs, ears, tail and the head outline are not visible (surface pitted). Shape is NOT demonstrable from the stone; position follows the column sequence (N31 road y~60-120, X1 17.15 at (700-815,~345), jackal below). Rothöhler's strip shows a jackal (back, raised head, hanging legs) after 'III X1' in col 17; consistent with these fragments. His overlay in this kit is misaligned (the outline at (300-600,650-930) belongs to another column). Note: no 'III' (Z2) strokes are visible at the 1901 Z2 box (777-860,409-484).

signs.note: water n; first sign of his 17c, below the stippled lost zone; stacked above X1 (1901 puts them side by side)
signs.trace_notes: Very worn. A single faint horizontal groove (FULL ~3272-3352, y ~4731-4741), sagging slightly to the right, ~37 FULL px above the traced loaf R21 (X1): visible in relief and native evidence as one continuous band. Rothoehler draws a zigzag water line N35 stacked above the X1, the same width; no zigzag teeth are visible on the stone, so only the line is traced (roth_agrees false only for the zigzag). Taken as R20 by sequence (first sign of 17c, directly above X1). The green box (1901: side by side with X1, y~4771-4789) is ~35 FULL px too low; roth.png here is a whole sign off (it shows Q1 over this crop).

Uncertain, faint. Surface here is badly worn (millstone area). The one coherent cut near the 1901 boxes: a short sunk bar at x~290-396, y~503-549 (dark shadowed top wall over a pale floor/lower wall, seen in photo, relief and native), the same look as the clear X1 loaves higher in this column (e.g. 17.3), so read as X1 (sunk; rim traced, low lock expected for a rim). It lies ~160 crop px LEFT of the green box and overlaps the right half of the 1901 N35 box (17.20); the green box itself has only pits and a large hollow above it. Rothöhler's col 17 sequence has N35 directly ABOVE X1 (not side by side as in 1901); no N35 is visible above this loaf. His overlay in this kit is far off (it shows his D4/G17/O6 here). If a reviewer reads the bar as an N35 fragment, it belongs to 17.20 instead.

Only the base of the sign survives: one clear, deep horizontal groove (FULL ~3301-3351, y ~4928), the strongest cut between R21 (X1, y~4782) and the eye R23 (y~5000), which by sequence is the foot of Rothoehler's tall narrow Q1. His vertical back and the narrow rectangle above the foot are not visible: the surface above (crop y 0-250) is pitted; a dark elongated hollow at FULL ~3288-3294, 4860-4890 (crop x ~117-135, y ~66-156) has no lit wall and looks like damage, not traced. The base is ~50 FULL px long, wider than his foot (~30). roth.png is ~100 FULL px too high here (it draws the eye over this crop); matched by sequence.

Eye, worn. Lower lid clear: one long sagging groove FULL ~3262-3358, y ~5006-5012 (crop x 146-434). Upper lid only on the right half (crop x 300-414, y ~162-175), faint but in relief and native; its left half, the corners and Rothoehler's pupil are not visible (pitted surface). Shape and width (~95 FULL px) fit his D4. Identified by sequence: next sign after the Q1 base (y~4928) and above the owl. Green box roughly right (lower lid inside it); roth.png ~100 FULL px too high in this part.

Owl very worn; only one long diagonal groove survives, running from upper right down-left (crop (405,302) -> (135,571), FULL ~3361,5077 -> 3261,5166), faint but in relief AND native (lower half strong: evidence ~3x texture; upper half broken). It matches Rothoehler's long back/tail line of G17, which he draws running from the head down-left out of the column. Head, breast, legs and base are not visible (pitted surface; large damage hollow at crop 400-560, 520-600 = FULL ~3350-3400, 5150-5176). Identified by sequence between the eye R23 (y~5008) and the O6 rectangle R25 (top y~5215). The green box is about right; roth.png ~100 FULL px too high here.

Tall upright rectangle, clear: top groove y~597, bottom groove y~897 (both crisp dark-over-bright), side grooves x~460 and ~537 (vertical, weaker but continuous in relief and native). Matches Rothöhler's col 17 sequence (D4, G17, tall rectangle, X1, ...); his overlay here is ~1000 crop px off vertically, so matched by sequence. Green box right on (sign ~150 px taller downward). The bottom bar at y~897 could be read as the top of X1 (17.26, 1901 box 447-584,898-985), but the side grooves run down into it, so it is taken as this rectangle's base; X1 would then be the dark hollow just below (460-540, 915-985), unconfirmed. The long dark groove at x300-380, y815-1220 left of the column is the same damage groove seen in 16.41's kit (not a sign).

Loaf X1 cut as a short, deep, slightly domed groove (FULL ~3319-3360, y ~5385), clear in relief, native and photo; no separate dome outline. Identified by sequence: Rothoehler draws X1 ~80 FULL px below the O6 base (R25, y~5315), and this is the only cut there; the bar at crop y~148 (FULL 5317) is R25's base, and the dark hollow under it (crop 170-230, 160-200) is a pit, not the loaf. KIT: the green box (1901, FULL 5316-5345) is ~45 FULL px too high; the sign lies at the bottom edge of this crop (y 338-352 of 375), near but inside the edge.

Bracket sign, PAST CROP EDGE: it lies at the bottom of this kit (FULL ~3313-3365, y ~5445-5484; crop y 327-445 of 393), traced from an extended crop with the same origin/scale (work/scratch/roth-013/mkext.py). Clear: a long top bar (crop x 214-358) and a short bottom bar at the left (x 209-262); faint: the lower part of the left upright (x ~210, y 396-436) joining the bottom bar. This is Rothoehler's bracket open to the RIGHT ('[', top, left side, shorter bottom), not open at the bottom as his list's description says. A thin dark line at x ~347, y 360-425 (right side) has no lit wall (crack?) and is not traced; the bottom bar may continue faintly to x ~300 (weak). Identified by sequence: after the loaf R26 (y~5385), before the long O34 bar (y~5537). The green box (1901, FULL 5384-5420) is ~45 FULL px too high (it reaches up to R26).

Bolt O34: a long straight horizontal bar, clear (FULL ~3293-3393, y ~5535), slightly weaker in its left-middle (x 130-230). Near the middle, just under the bar, a short oblique edge (crop (238,356)->(258,372), FULL ~3348-3354, 5536-5541) forms a small wedge: the central knot Rothoehler draws; only its right flank is visible, so only that is traced (faint). Identified by sequence after the bracket R27 (y ~5445-5484) and before the basket R29 (y ~5590). The green box (1901, FULL 5479-5499) is ~40-55 FULL px too high; the sign lies near the bottom of this crop (inside).

Read by Rothöhler's col 17 sequence (⊏⊐ 17.27, O34 17.28 '—+—', V31 17.29 '⏝', D21 17.30, A40 17.31; his overlay here is ~900 crop px off, so matched by sequence). Stone features down the column: an open-bottomed rectangle (⊏⊐) at x530-690, y195-310; a long straight groove x455-770, y~465 with a small peg/knob at x~640-660 = O34 bolt; then this shallow curved groove (474,617)->(560,652)->(715,642) = the rounded bottom of the basket (clear in photo, relief, native); then the clear D21 lens at x480-780, y790-840 and A40 below. The basket's flat top/rim line (expected ~y610-625) and the handle are not visible. So the sign lies ~170 px BELOW the green box; the green box sits on the O34 bolt. Alternative (less likely): 1901's reading with the y465 line as V31 would leave the lens at y815 unaccounted for.

Mouth r (D21): crisp lens outline (FULL ~3296-3399, y ~5644-5663), both outlines meeting in a pointed tail at each tip, clear in relief, native and photo. Upper outline arches higher at its right half, as in Rothoehler's lens. Below the basket R29 (traced, y~5590) and above the seated god R31; sequence agrees. The green box (1901, FULL 5601-5635) is ~40 FULL px too high and overlaps R29's trace.

Seated god facing right, clear and well preserved (FULL ~3315-3371, 5719-5799). Traced: the head as an inverted V (back of wig rising from (182,350), flat top, face/beard line descending right to (322,315)), the short horizontal arm/hand (y~367), the long thigh/knee diagonal from (340,381) down-left to (245,428), and the base line (y~475). The broad pale patch between the strokes (crop x 215-270, y 320-460: the body, worn smooth) has no separate groove edges except a small blob at (225-250, 315-335), not traced. Matches Rothoehler's A40 in sequence (last sign of column 17, after the lens R30) and in overall shape; green box about right.

Goose (G38) facing right, in the green box; cut broad/near-sunk like the geese of cols 16-17. Back/wing top groove (448,575)->(652,518) clear; belly = lower rim of the pale cut body at y~600 (bright->dark, sunk rim, faint). Neck and head: left edge of a pale cut block at x~650 rising to a head top at y~422 (x650-715), faint; beak tip not resolved. Two short legs (x~563, ~605, y600-633) faint, standing on a clear base groove y~637 (x540-670). Disk N9 (18.2) is the ring at (740-830,420-500) and X1 (18.3) the bar at (735-830,~625): not traced. Rothöhler draws the same goose with legs on a base line; agrees.

Incised ring (disk), slightly polygonal, with a dark worn hollow inside; traced as a closed ellipse on the groove (dark->bright boundary top, inner shadow->lit wall bottom). Right of the goose R1, above the loaf R3. Rothoehler draws the same ring (his roth.png sits on it within ~5 crop px). No inner crescent visible.

Sunk loaf (rim traced as a closed outline): low dome/rounded-rectangle hollow with shadowed top wall and flat lit floor, below the disk R2. Rothoehler draws the same dome with flat base at the same place (his top is slightly more domed). Bottom edge placed by eye (sunk shape).

Only the horizontal sole of the L-shaped foot is visible: a clear groove (shadowed upper wall, lit lower wall) running slightly downhill from (168,356) to (298,377), ending just left of the R5 flags. Rothoehler draws an L with a vertical stem rising from the left end at crop x~200 up to y~180; no vertical groove is visible there or anywhere near x 150-215 in photo, relief or native (surface pitted and cracked; the diagonal dark gash at (115-165,315-375) is damage, not a cut). Stem not traced: not visible. roth.png alignment checked against the traced R5 bar/pole 1 (agrees within ~5 crop px).

signs.note: three nṯr-flags on a common bar
signs.trace_notes: Row of nṯr-flags, clear and well preserved, in the green box: horizontal bar y~503 (x452-698) with three poles hanging from it (x~517, ~599, ~693; y515-735, the third ends ~700). Two short faint diagonal strokes right of poles 1 and 2 ((553,640)->(580,693) and (605,615)->(640,675)) look like the cloth lobes of the flags; seen in photo and relief, weak in native; no matching lobe visible right of pole 3 (close to the column rule at x~740). Rothöhler draws bar + three plain poles; agrees (he omits the lobes). Vertical poles give weak scorer evidence.

Cobra body: long clear horizontal groove (crop y~258-262, x 205-428) curving down-left at its left end; the descent continues faintly (relief + native, worn, pitted beside a round pit at ~(157,305)) to ~(159,395), lower part lost in pitting. Rothoehler draws the same S-shaped body, with the tail running further down to ~(131,482), and a raised head hook at the right end (~438,219): on the stone the right end of the groove stops at x~430 and the area above/right of it is a pale spall (435-470,195-230), no head cut visible; not traced. The staff R7 (separate kit 18.7) stands to the right, not traced here.

Staff: a single worn vertical groove at crop x~427-433, y~292-522, right of the cobra R6 (whose body groove lies at y~207 in this frame) and left of the column rule (x~525). Otherwise agrees.

Upright rectangle (Q3 stool as drawn in this inscription), clear and complete, in the green box: grooves top y~450, bottom y~620, sides x~465 / ~551 (sides weaker in the scorer, clear in photo/relief/native). Three fox skins, clear: two crossed short strokes at the top (left one (163,160)->(232,203) with a rounded lobe end, right one from (284,143)), meeting at (232,~205); from there three hanging skins: left one curving out and down to (165,488), middle one straight down at x~235 to y~494, right one curving down to ~(287,468) (lower part fainter; the pale patch at (275-300,410-435) is a flake). Very worn bird (G43 type), most of the outline lost to pitting and flaking. signs.note: Horus falcon on a base stroke

A short groove crosses the back down-right at (646-712,632-671), in all three images: wing/body detail, faint. Rothöhler's head, breast, legs and base line are not visible on the photo (surface pitted; pale horizontal streaks at y~720-800 have no groove edge). Sign lies in the upper-left part of the green box.

EMPTY: surface lost. Between the falcon R13 (base ~crop y 40 in this frame) and the U-shaped horns R15 (stone U top ~crop y 595 in this frame) the stone is spalled and pitted; no hanging fox-skin tails or crossed top can be made out in photo, relief or native. Features present: a short bright bar (150-300, y 250-285) with a small upturned hook at its right end, and a rough ring-shaped rim (x~146-323, y~343-520) around a dark spalled hollow with a pale lump; the ring closes at the bottom, so it reads as the edge of a spall, not as skins. A template of the clear skins of R11 (18.11) laid over these features does not fit (lock 0.95). Rothoehler draws three fox skins here (his drawing in this region sits ~30 FULL px too low, judged from his U R15).

Wide U-shaped groove (horns drawn as a U), clear: bottom clear in all layers, arms fainter toward their tips (left tip ~(250,238), right tip ~(547,245)). Rothoehler draws the same U; his roth.png sits ~30 FULL px too low and a little right here. The pale lump inside the U at (370-420,240-300) is a surface feature, not a cut.

signs.note: two pairs of short parallel dashes side by side (remains of the road sign?); last thing he draws above the stippled lost zone
signs.trace_notes: Very damaged zone just above the lost area. Visible in relief and native: an upper row of short horizontal grooves at y~205-212 (left dash (188-266), right dash (300-440)) and a lower one at y~248-253 (275-393), ~45 px apart, i.e. two parallel dash rows; traced faint. Separating dashes from the broken edges is uncertain: the surface between and below is flaked. A further groove segment at (455-520, y~204) continues the upper row past the column's right edge (FULL x ~3446-3467, beyond the U R15's right tip at 3449) and was not traced. Rothoehler draws a single '=' (two short stacked dashes) here; his roth.png sits ~90 crop px too low (cf. R15); shifted up, his pair falls on the right upper dash and the lower dash. roth_agrees false: I see a longer upper row (left dash extra) than his pair.

signs.note: small L-shape; 18.17's trace (narrow sunk upright wedge) sits above the LEFT bar, where his L is; matched by position
signs.trace_notes: fixup 2026-11-08: RE-TRACED (decided together with 18.18). Rothoehler's 18c strip, scaled to the stone by his '- -' (R19/R20, FULL y~5495), owl and djeds (~0.52 FULL px per strip px), puts the foot of his small L (R17) at FULL y~5440, x~3439-3472, and the base of his pillar (R18) at the same height on the right. Exactly there the stone has a pale sunk bar pair (roth-015): LEFT bar FULL ~3429-3474, y 5437-5444 = this sign's foot, traced as its rim (sunk, clear in relief, photo and native); RIGHT bar (FULL ~3499-3532) = R18, traced in 18.18. The L's upright stem is not visible (worn/flaked surface). The old trace (a narrow sunk wedge, FULL ~3466-3485 x 5455-5508) was removed: it lies between the two bar pairs in the middle of the column, where he draws nothing, and with the pale triangular hollow beside it (FULL ~3438-3468, 5456-5481) it reads as a spall, not as his L or T. Uncertain identification: the bar pair also looks like a second '- -', but nothing else is cut in his L/T row. | previous notes: Very uncertain. Inside the green box nothing is cut: the only candidate there, a diffuse dark patch at ~(520-590,710-810) beside a pale chip, has no groove walls. Rothöhler (whose drawing is misaligned by ~380 FULL px here: his bird and two R11 lie ~1150 crop px above the carved ones, which are in 18.21's kit) has, in sequence, a small L + an upright T side by side, then a pair of short bars '- -', then the bird and two R11. His '- -' match the two pale bars at y~1130 (x 520-610, 740-840; 18.20's box). The one upright feature just above/beside them is a narrow sunk wedge, traced here as its open rim: apex (619,1012), widening down to ~(606-664,1170), with sharp edges in photo and a dark band in relief and native, below the green box and partly inside 18.20's box. It may be his T (traced faint as a sunk upright), but its shape (pointed top, wide base, pale chip beside it) also fits spall damage, and his solid T-top is not visible. His small L is not identifiable on the photo. Short pale bars at y~965 (x 510-630, 720-800) not traced. Low lock (0.88) is expected: it is the rim of a sunk, near-vertical wedge with weak top-light evidence. Treat it as a candidate only.

signs.note: upright narrow pillar with a solid top bar, hanging from the edge of the lost zone; above the right bar; project box lies above/right of 18.17
signs.trace_notes: fixup 2026-11-08: RE-CHECKED (was marked lost), decided together with 18.17. Traced: (1) the RIGHT bar of the pale sunk bar pair at FULL ~3499-3532, y 5438-5442 (kit 75-175, y 489-503), clear in relief, photo and native, at the height where Rothoehler's strip (scaled by his '- -', owl and djeds) puts the foot of his pillar R18, beside the L R17 (= the left bar, 18.17); rim of a sunk bar. (2) faint: a short horizontal groove ~25 FULL px higher, FULL ~3509-3536, y~5365 (kit 106-186, y~272; dark wall over a pale floor, strong in the evidence map), which may be his solid top bar at the edge of the lost zone. The pillar shaft between them is not distinguishable (only a pale vertical streak at kit x~160, y 330-390 and a pale mound at kit 100-150, 440-470, neither a clear groove). roth_agrees false: the bar is wider than his pillar and the shaft is missing; identification by position only, uncertain.

signs.note: short flat bar (left); his '- -' pair = the two pale bars in 18.20's box
signs.trace_notes: Left of the two short flat bars ('- -'): a shallow sunk lens-shaped bar, rim traced as a closed outline (sunk; lower rim placed by eye), x 114-219, y ~176-200. Its right end abuts the dark sunk wedge traced as R17 (18.17). The right bar (his R20, no kit of its own; ~x 290-375, y ~170-192 here) not traced. roth.png is badly misaligned here (it draws the owl R21 over these bars, ~380 FULL px off, cf. 18.17 notes); matched by sequence: L/T pair, then '- -', then owl.

signs.note: short flat bar (right); covered by 18.20's box
signs.trace_notes: Short flat bar, the RIGHT bar of Rothoehler's '- -' pair (R19 left, R20 right), matched by sequence: below the damaged L/T row, above the owl R21 (top ~FULL y 5537). On the stone it is a narrow sunk lens-shaped bar, pale with a dark centre line in photo, bright in relief and native, FULL x 3512-3547, y 5492-5497; rim traced as a closed outline (sunk). PAST CROP EDGE: the kit's green box and roth.png sit ~85 FULL px (~255 crop px) too HIGH (his bar drawn at crop y~165); the bar lies at crop y ~415-433, below this crop (height 333); traced in kit coordinates from full-frame views (work/scratch/roth-015/fv.py). Separated from R19 (the left bar, FULL x ~3415-3450, same row) by the gap at x~3450-3510. A similar pale pair ~57 FULL px higher (y~5440; right bar x~3497-3530, which is what the kit's crop shows at y~260) was not taken: its spacing to the owl fits his L/T row, not his '- -' (his '- -' sit ~25 plate units above the owl top). Lock score is not meaningful for an out-of-crop trace.

Owl, worn, cut as a shallow sunk silhouette (pale field in photo) facing right. Traced: flat head top (408-455, y~139, clear), the breast/front edge straight down x~455 to y~300 (faint, photo clearest), the back running down-left from the head to the tail tip ~(152,452) (faint, dark-above-bright edge in relief and native), and the foot/base bar at y~456, x 366-512 (clear, sunk pale bar). Not traced: legs and the lower breast (a pale vertical strip at x~385-420, y 365-450 at the left end of the foot bar may be the legs, photo only); ear tufts/face details not visible. Matched by sequence: one bird between the '- -' pair (R19/R20, FULL y~5495) and the two djed pillars (crossbars from FULL y~5705). roth.png is ~130-150 crop px (~45-50 FULL px) too HIGH here (his feet bar drawn at y~325); shapes agree after that shift. 18.21's old box covers this bird's head (no separate sign). Low lock is expected: sunk/pale silhouette edges and a sunk bar centre line, not top-lit grooves.

Djed pillar, LEFT of the pair (R22). Four crossbars (pale sunk bars) at y~210, 240, 262, 300 (x ~150-290; the third is short and faint) and the shaft at x~216 from the lowest bar down to a slightly flared foot at y~515 (pale in photo, bright in relief and native; upper shaft faint). Shaft not visible between the crossbars. Separated from R23 (right djed, its bars start at FULL x~3501 = this crop x~330) by the gap at x~290-330; the long vertical at x~100 is the column rule, not traced. roth.png draws the pair ~35 FULL px too far left and ~23 FULL px too high, with wider spacing; matched by sequence (two djeds side by side after the owl), shapes agree.

Djed pillar, RIGHT of the pair (R23); separated from R22 (left djed, bars end at FULL x~3488 = this crop x~117) by the gap at FULL x~3488-3501. Four crossbars (pale sunk bars): y~221 (long, x 158-324), y~248 (x 182-258 clear, plus a faint piece at x 305-330, middle not visible), y~276 (faint), y~304 (x 198-337); shaft at x~280 from the lowest bar to a flared foot at y~520 (clear in photo, relief and native). The shaft sits right of the bars' centre (bars reach further left than right). The vertical at crop x~380 is the column rule, not traced. roth.png draws it ~25-35 FULL px too far left and ~23 FULL px too high; matched by sequence, shapes agree.

N35 zigzag clearly cut just under the line-divider, x 409-858. Left end is a long down-slanting lead-in stroke (to y~566), the same style as the N35A rows below (19.3), traced as a separate stroke. Teeth 440-800 clear; the right end (800-858, at the column rule) is worn and flatter. Green box was about right; real box is a little lower and extends left.

signs.note: whip mḥ (bar with knobbed right end, long tail curving down at left); its tail runs down beside the N35A
signs.trace_notes: V22 whip, clear. Long bar (groove centre FULL y~1454, x 3489-3597) with a small round sunk knob at the right end (traced as a small closed rim, FULL ~3588-3600, 1446-1458), turning at the left end into the long tail that runs straight down beside the N35A (19.R3) to FULL y~1550. PAST CROP EDGE: the tail continues below this kit's bottom edge (crop y 438 = FULL 1537); points to crop y~477 are outside the image. Matches Rothoehler (bar thickening to the right with knob, tail curving down at left).

signs.note: three water lines; three rows, one sign
signs.trace_notes: N35A, three zigzag water lines, all clear (FULL rows at y~1504-1521, 1543-1561, 1583-1601, x 3484-3602). Each row starts with a longer down-slanting lead-in at the left, like 19.1. Six teeth per row; tooth positions placed by eye on relief/native, individual teeth approximate. The whip tail (19.R2) runs down left of the rows and is not traced here.

signs.note: floating (drowned) man, horizontal, head right (det. of mḥ 'drown'); same sign as 19.22

The gap at FULL x 3505-3526 on the lower line is damaged. Rothoehler's small round head at the far right is not clearly cut: a round bright pit at FULL ~(3591,1628) may be damage, not traced. roth.png is drawn ~15-20 FULL px too high here (his N37 lies over the N35 lines).

N37 pool: long rounded-rectangle outline, x 404-840, top groove ~y467 (rising slightly to ~460 at the right), bottom groove ~y505-518. Both long sides clear in relief and native; the left end is clear, the right end (790-840, beside the column rule) is worn and less certain. Green box was about right but the sign starts ~45 px further left and sits ~30 px higher.
N35 water line, clear (FULL x 3475-3616, peaks y~1765, troughs ~1773). Seven teeth, positions approximate. Matches Rothoehler.

Q1 seat, tall narrow form, cut as a SUNK silhouette: traced the rim as one closed outline. Narrow upper post (FULL x~3528-3536, y 1813-1852), stepping out to a wider lower part (x~3531-3548, y 1852-1904), and a foot extending right at the bottom (FULL x 3521-3579, y~1904-1921). Clear in photo, relief and native. Matches Rothoehler's L-shaped tall seat with the narrow upper part. Lock is modest because it is a sunk rim.

D4 eye: upper lid arc and lower lid, meeting in long pointed tips (FULL x 3489-3613, y 1961-1986), clear. The central pupil is a raised/pale blob in the middle (FULL ~3547-3566, 1963-1981); its outline traced as faint. Matches Rothoehler's eye (his pupil is drawn filled at the top centre).

signs.note: small frontal head (round, with ears and neck)
signs.trace_notes: D2 face, heavily worn. Three parts are visible in relief and native: a rounded top (forehead/crown arc, x 470-546, top ~y461), and two lower sides converging in a V to a chin at ~(525,594). The upper ends of the V (438,530) and (576,516) don't visibly join the arc; that link is lost, so it is not restored. Traced as the sign below the eye D4 (19.8) and above N35A (19.10), consistent with the reading order. Isolated bright pit at (510,655) not traced. The sign sits in the upper-left part of the green box.

N35A, three zigzag lines, very worn: FULL rows at y~2134-2146, 2174-2183, 2221-2234, x ~3490-3615. Rows are visible as wavy groove evidence in relief and native (row 1 clearest); tooth positions are approximate (phase fitted by eye/evidence map), so all marked faint. Matches Rothoehler's three rows.

signs.note: horned viper f (long rising stroke, forked head right)
signs.trace_notes: I9 horned viper: long groove rising from left (FULL 3482,2302) to the right (3610,2272), clear in relief, photo and native. At the right end a short branch goes back up-left (FULL 3590-3610, 2263-2272), traced faint; this is Rothoehler's forked head. Matches his drawing.

U1 sickle: one continuous groove: top part coming down at right (FULL ~3551,2349 to 3549,2373), bending left (to ~3504,2388), then the long blade sweeping down-right to FULL (3603,2446). Clear in relief and native; the link from the bend to the left corner (FULL x 3504-3528) is weaker. Matches Rothoehler's sickle; roth.png draws it ~20-30 FULL px too low.

signs.note: long-necked bird; left of the X1; read before it (1901 order puts X1 first)
signs.trace_notes: R13 long-necked bird (G1 label), worn. Traced the long neck/back line from the head (FULL ~3602,2466) down-left to the tail tip (3484,2562), the front/breast line from the throat (3606,2472) curving down and back to the tail along the belly (y~2557-2562), a tiny faint beak stub at the head, and a faint ground/foot line FULL x 3500-3560, y~2598 (level with the bottom of Rothoehler's feet, just below the X1 19.13). Legs not visible (surface worn); not restored. The neck/body reads partly as a sunk band between the two lines. X1 19.13 to the right not traced.

X1 loaf right of the bird G1 (19.14), in the green box. Cut as one sunk dome-shaped hollow (shadowed top ~y462-488, lit floor/lower wall ~y495-522), not as separate outline grooves; traced the rim of the hollow as a closed outline like the other sunk loaves (10.26, 10.31). The lock score is modest (1.06) because a sunk shape's rim isn't a dark-to-bright groove centre; the shape itself is clear in photo, relief and native. Small bright chip at (475,483) inside the left part is surface damage.

signs.note: loaf t (left); side by side with Q1, read first
signs.trace_notes: R15 X1 loaf (left of the Q1, read first). Very worn: a small dome-shaped sunk hollow at FULL x 3503-3541, y 2686-2699 (shadowed top arc, lit floor), visible in photo, relief and native but faint; rim traced as a closed outline. It sits where Rothoehler and the 1901 box put the left X1. Separated from Q1 (R16): Q1's only surviving part is the foot groove ~40 FULL px lower and to the right.

R16 Q1 seat (right of the X1). Only the FOOT survives: a clear horizontal groove FULL x 3586-3619, y~2737 (dark wall above, lit below, in relief/photo/native), with a faint continuation left to FULL ~3557. Its level matches the bottom of Rothoehler's Q1 and his foot extends right from the post as here. The tall post above it is not visible (surface pitted and worn; maybe faint traces at FULL x~3565, 2640-2690, not convincing); not restored. roth.png draws his Q1/X1 ~50 FULL px too low here and ~20 px left.

signs.note: short horizontal groove ~85 FULL px below Q1 19.15/X1 19.16 (traced); he draws only stipple (lost) here
signs.trace_notes: Unidentified ('?'). One short, slightly sagging horizontal groove, x 418-522, y ~556-572, visible in photo, relief and native; it sits at the lower-left edge of the green box (the box's upper/right part holds only pits and texture). A thin wiggly line continues up-left from its left end toward (380,525) and looks more like a vein than a cut, so it is not traced; nor are the diagonal pale streak at (560-660, 590-660) or the pits at (640,450-470). Too little survives to identify the sign; nothing restored.

signs.note: thin plain horizontal stroke at the edge of the lost zone; project O34; he draws only a plain stroke (no knot), probably the foot of a lost sign
signs.trace_notes: R18 thin plain horizontal stroke: clear horizontal groove at FULL x 3587-3709, y~5358-5360, right under the big lost area (edge of the lost zone), visible in photo, relief and native; right end turns slightly up. Left part (FULL x 3587-3615) fainter. It lies above the N35 19.19 (R19). Matches Rothoehler's plain stroke; nothing else of a sign survives above it.

N35 water line, worn: one shallow groove with a few broad undulations (teeth worn to gentle waves), visible in relief, photo (pale band) and native. Rothoehler draws the same line with fine teeth ~15-25 crop px higher and ~20-50 px further left (roth.png drift). Separated from R18 (stroke at y~165) and R20 (whip bar at y~465).

signs.note: whip mḥ (bar, tail curving down at left)
signs.trace_notes: V22 whip: long straight bar (clear, deep, x 278-555), at its left end turning down into the tail that curves down-left (clear to y~300), then continues as a faint steep groove to y~396 (visible in relief and photo, weak in native as expected for a steep groove). No knob at the right end is visible; the bar simply ends at x~555. Rothoehler draws the same shape (bar + tail curving down at left, tail ~160 crop px long) ~50 crop px higher and ~40 px left (roth.png drift). The short diagonal pale streak at (300-350, 330-345) inside the curve is not a cut (not in native).

N35A: three worn, low-amplitude water lines inside the green box, about 130 crop px apart: row 1 y~493-510 (x 520-780), row 2 y~622-650 (x 498-786, with a short lead-in from lower left and the right end dipping down), row 3 y~759-792 (x 490-790, with a long rising lead-in from lower left, as on the N35 rows of 19.1/19.3). The teeth are mostly worn to gentle undulations, so they are traced as seen, not as sharp zigzags. All three rows are visible in photo, relief and native (faint). The small I9 box (19.24) at the lower right is not touched.

signs.note: floating (drowned) man, horizontal, head right; repeats the group N35 V22 N35A + this sign + N37 of the upper part
signs.trace_notes: Horizontal figure, head end at right, read with Rothoehler as the floating (drowned) man. Traced three clear grooves: (1) the long upper line from the far left (x~172) rising to the right toward the head end (475,171); (2) a second trailing line (lower left) that runs up-right and merges into line 1 at ~(312,227) (the two legs trailing left); (3) the lower body line from (344,278) rising to the head end at (491,213). The head itself is not traced: the smooth pale oval at x 498-545, y 162-183 (bright in relief and native) sits where Rothoehler draws the round head, but it looks like the pale surface flakes nearby (e.g. x 420-470, y 150-170) and shows no groove edge; it may be the head hollow, but is left out. Rothoehler's drawing here is ~90 crop px too high and ~60-90 px too far left; matched by sequence (between N35A R21 above and the pool R23 below). Separated from the pool R23 (two long lines y~370-430) and the N35A row 3 (above y~50).

N37 pool: two long parallel horizontal grooves, ~46 crop px apart, both clear in relief, photo and native; the lower one runs ~30 px further right (to x~655) than the upper (ends x~624). The short vertical end caps Rothoehler draws at both ends are not visible: on the left the surface between the lines is pale/flaked, on the right nothing is cut between the line ends. The steep groove at x~680-690 (y 250-335) to the right is the column rule, and the vertical at x~207 on the left is the left column rule/edge; neither traced. Rothoehler's pool is ~90 crop px too high and ~60 px left in roth.png; matched by sequence (below the drowned man R22, above the viper R24).

signs.note: horned viper f; matched by sequence: the 1901 box sits right of the N35A (19.21), his I9 is below N37
