Column 21 here lies between rules at x~345 and x~740; from y~250 down its right half is deeply flaked, and the green box (451-603, 450-768) shows only pitting, pale spalls and short random edges in relief, photo and native (the evidence map is uniform noise). No tall narrow reed leaf is visible anywhere in x 345-740, y 300-880. The first coherent cuts below are two long horizontal bars at y~893 and ~947 (x ~450-720), in 21.10's D54 box: not traced here. Rothöhler (overlay roughly +170,+355 crop px off, judged from the cobra 21.5) has no reed at this point in the sequence; his sign in this slot is a rectangle with a hooked arm, which is not visible on the photo either. 21.9's M17 is therefore unconfirmed and may be a 1901 misreading.

signs.note: long horizontal bar with pointed left end; covered by 21.10's box; drawn joined to the walking legs below
signs.trace_notes: Long horizontal bar with pointed left end, ~FULL x 3817-3928, y 1972-1993: two long parallel grooves (upper y ~260, lower y ~318 in 21.10 crop terms) closing at a pointed left tip; clear in relief, photo and native. At the left the outline forms a lens-like end (tip at x ~153 here); its upper line breaks off at x ~213 and a diagonal groove runs from there down-right to meet the lower line (x ~305), while the long upper line starts again at x ~298 and runs right; the stretch between (x ~213-298 at the top) is a pitted, bright patch, no groove visible, so not joined. Right end open (lines end at x ~480-485). Rothoehler draws the same: a lens-shaped left end continued by two long lines. Legs below are 21.R14 (not traced here). roth.png is ~30 FULL px too high in this area; matched by sequence (bar above the legs, above the N35).

signs.note: walking legs under the bar; 21.10's box covers bar + legs; matched to the legs by identity, not to the first sign
signs.trace_notes: Walking legs (D54) under the long bar 21.R13: an inverted V with a flat narrow top (x 386-414, y ~357, just ~12 FULL px under the bar's lower line), the left leg nearly vertical down to (369,448) (photo and relief, faint in native), the right leg slanting down-right to (455,464) (clear in photo and relief, visible in native) and a short foot running right from its end to x ~508 (faint). Matches Rothoehler's legs (vertical left leg, slanting right leg, foot to the right); he joins them to the bar, on the stone there is a small gap. roth.png is ~90 crop px (~30 FULL) too high here (his bar at y ~200 vs the stone's ~265-322). The green box covers the bar (21.R13), not the legs; the legs lie below it.

Water ripple N35 across the column, x ~295-645 (FULL ~3809-3926, y ~2083-2095): a zigzag groove with a shadowed upper wall and bright lit triangular teeth below, clear in relief, photo and native from x ~480 to 645 (four regular teeth) and at the left end (x 295-360); the middle stretch x ~360-470 is worn flat, the zigzag there is not distinct (traced as the smooth groove line the evidence shows). In the green box. Rothoehler's N35 matches in sequence (below the bar+legs, above V30 21.R16); roth.png is ~110 crop px (~35 FULL) too high here.

signs.note: flat-topped basket (half-round below); 1901 N35; he draws a basket/bowl shape, not a ripple
signs.trace_notes: Sunk flat-topped basket under the ripple (21.R15? N35 at FULL y~2100) and above the bird 21.13: rim traced as closed outline. Flat top (deep shadowed upper wall, crop y~155) from x~238 to ~486; half-round underside = lower edge of the lit floor band, lowest ~y 234 at x~360. Worn/flaked, so conf faint; visible in relief and native. Rothoehler draws a small hook at the left end; on the stone only a pale smudge at x~230-250, y~175-200, not traced. roth.png sits ~60-70 crop px (~20 FULL px) too high; matched by sequence (ripple -> basket -> bird). Sunk rim: trace_score lock low (0.85) as expected.

signs.note: bird (long body, tail down-left; G1/G43 type); project V13; he draws a bird (cf. opus_findings)
signs.trace_notes: A long, narrow, diagonal U-shaped outline, clear in photo, relief and native: the upper-left line (straight, dark shadowed wall) runs from ~(566,580) down-left to (452,712), turns round a closed lower-left end, and the right line curves back up to ~(680,450); open at the top (the upper end of the left line fades out; a deep pit/spall at (560-640,450-500) sits between the two upper ends). Short cross-hatching inside is texture, not traced. It is not an oval loop with a tail (V13): the outline is a bird's body seen obliquely, back on the upper left and belly/breast on the right, converging at the tail, as on other oblique birds of this stone. Rothöhler draws a bird here (his overlay ~150 px left, ~100 px up), so identity_ok false: read a bird (G43/G1-type, code to confirm), not V13. Head (in or beyond the pit) and legs not visible: surface lost. Box: carving sits in the left-centre of the green box. The right line shows mainly as one pale lit wall with a weak shadow on its upper-left side; the centre line is placed on that dark/bright boundary, hence the modest lock (~1.0).

signs.note: bird in outline at the column foot (below the lost zone), tail to lower left; project '?'; species not certain (owl G17 per 1901)
signs.trace_notes: Only the tail / lower back line of the bird survives: one diagonal groove from the tail tip (112,522) up-right to (226,360), lit lower-right wall clear in relief and native (FULL ~3924,5802 -> 3962,5748). This matches Rothoehler's thick tail-to-back stroke at the lower left of his bird. Rest not visible: upper back and head (he puts the head ~90 FULL px right/100 up of the tail tip, i.e. near crop (380,230)), breast line and feet. The bright splash with dark notches at crop (470-580,150-270) is surface damage (pale flaking), not the head; not traced. Species not decidable from the stone. roth.png agrees closely here (his tail tip ~10 crop px lower-left of mine).

signs.note: crenellated enclosure (fortress) with a standing man holding a staff inside; the figure inside is drawn as part of the enclosure group; counted as one sign
signs.trace_notes: Crenellated enclosure (fortress), clear. Traced as cut: the top line (y~527, only x 552-776 visible; its left part and the top-left corner are lost in a worn patch), the right wall (x~737, y 535-952) with 7 clear crenellation teeth on its outer side (y 574, 640, 697, 750, 806, 855, 912; positions agree in relief and native), the bottom line (y~956, x 402-776), and a fainter left wall (x~408) with 6 teeth outside it (y 608, 680, 737, 800, 865, 925). Teeth along the top, which Rothöhler draws, are not resolvable (only dark pits above the top line). The inner sign is traced as the faint strokes actually visible: a clear horizontal bar (y~805, x 440-600), a vertical at x~477 above it, a V at (553-620, 652-698), two short verticals (x~507, ~547, y 838-920) on a base line y~920, and a long upright at x~652-672 on the right. Rothöhler draws the inner sign as a standing man holding a tall staff (his overlay ~-320,+245 px off); the stone's upright on the right fits his staff and the two short verticals his legs, but the bar at y~805 and the V do not clearly match a human figure, so the inner strokes are given as seen, not as a man. Box: carving x 346-794, y 500-962, roughly the green box shifted ~100 px left; the column rule at x~818 is not part of the sign.

signs.note: large falcon/bird, tail to lower left, on a base line; 1901 Aa13 (horizontal bars); he draws a big bird here. Match by sequence (plate->photo drift is large in this column)
signs.trace_notes: Large bird facing right, matched to Rothoehler's G5 by sequence (enclosure 22.R1 above, his base line and the long bar 22.R3 below) and by geometry: scaling his plate drawing on his base line puts his head top at crop ~(478,101) and tail tip ~(197,441), exactly where the stone has them. Traced: flat head top (clear, x 480-542, y~92); the long back line from the head down-left to the tail tip (205,447) (clear, deep, in relief/photo/native); the front/breast line from the head down to ~(515,235) (faint: right edge of a pale band below the head); a faint line (300,430)->(385,331) parallel to the back, probably the tail underside running up to the leg notch (his underside starts at the tail tip; the stone line is ~70 px further right, uncertain); and the base/foot line (clear, x 478-582, y~404). Not visible: the rest of the breast and the leg (y 240-400 on the right is plain), and the left end of the tail underside. The 1901 'Aa13 bars' are this sign's base line and the head-top groove. roth.png for this kit is badly misplaced (shows the enclosure figure); compared directly with his plate.

signs.note: long horizontal bar with rounded right end, at the edge of the lost zone; 1901/project X1 'short t'; his bar is long
signs.trace_notes: Long sunk bar with a rounded, slightly down-turned right end, directly under the bird 22.R2's base line (FULL ~4017-4092, y 1721-1744): rim traced as closed outline (sunk; top rim = shadowed upper wall, bottom = lower edge of the lit floor). The right end (x>400) runs PAST CROP EDGE (crop width 402); traced in kit coordinates from an extended view (work/scratch/roth-020/ext.py). Matches Rothoehler's long bar with rounded right end; the 1901 'short t' X1 box covers only its left half. Conf faint because the lower edge at the left is blurred by flaking. Below it (y>150) is the lost/flaked zone; his small mark under the bar (22.4 phantom) not traced.

Water ripple, clear in relief, photo and native: a zigzag of 4 peaks (x~510, 572, 639, 700 at y~445), starting at the lower left (476,484) and ending in a longer down-stroke to (740,502). The centre line is on the dark/bright boundary (upper side of the lit band). It is shorter than a typical N35 (about 275 px) and fills the green box. Rothöhler draws N35 at the head of his column 41 (= unit 23), overlay offset ~(-280,+230) px; his drawing agrees.

Sunk mouth/bar: rim traced as closed outline (sunk). Pointed left tip at (148,193), top rim rising to a low hump over the left half (y~152 at x~240, as in Rothoehler's drawing, whose bar is thicker at top-left) and running nearly straight to the blunt right end (441,192); bottom rim = lower edge of the lit lower wall (y~215-220). A pale flake lies inside the upper left part of the hollow (x 185-350, y 158-186); not a separate cut. Clear in relief, photo and native. roth.png renders his drawing with very thick strokes and his mouth ~40 crop px low, so it is hard to read; matched with his plate by sequence (ripple 23.1 above, pot 23.4 below, Z1 23.3 at the right edge).

signs.note: vertical stroke at the right edge
signs.trace_notes: Vertical stroke at the right edge of column 23, ~20 FULL px right of the mouth 23.R2's right end (mouth tip visible at crop (90,200)). Steep groove: a pale vertical groove floor (photo) with weak edges in relief from y~140 to ~330 (FULL 1442-1505), continuing fainter (relief + native) down to ~425, i.e. from the mouth's level to below the pot 23.R4, as Rothoehler draws his tall Z1 wedge. Lower end uncertain (round pit at (178,390) beside it, not traced). The pale vertical band at x~255-270 is the column rule between 23 and 24, not traced. Steep stroke: low trace_score lock expected.

signs.note: small round pot (nw); project X1; he draws a small pot
signs.trace_notes: Small sunk pot (nw), both parts traced as rims of sunk hollows: a wide flat lip (clear; dark upper wall + lit lower wall, x 114-212, y 144-182) and below it a narrow-necked, round-bottomed body (faint but clear in relief/photo/native as a pale lit floor, x 127-175, y 186-288). Matches Rothoehler's small pot with a flat lip, not the 1901 X1 't'. Sits under the left half of the mouth 23.R2 and left of the Z1 23.R3; the bright spot at (230,200) right of the lip is a pale chip, not traced. roth.png (very thick strokes) puts his pot ~20 crop px right of the stone pot; agrees by shape and sequence.

signs.note: old-form qd: frame with crenellated right wall and slanting leg; project '?'; Rothöhler's reading qd (cf. opus_findings)
signs.trace_notes: Old-form qd (Sethe): long upper groove 470-745 sloping up to the right with a short inner lens/bar groove under it (548-668, y~525); below it a ⊓-frame: left leg x~477 and right leg x~695 running down to ~770 (faint, visible mainly in native/relief as vertical edges; steep strokes score weakly); two short horizontal cuts at the foot of the left side (452-482 y786, 505-565 y777) taken as feet/base. Sign sits in the green box; no box shift needed. Rothöhler (overlay offset about -330 x, +290 y crop px; his drawing sits in the next column at ~790-1100 x 185-475; strip roth_col24 is this column) draws A35: a standing man on the left, a slanting top bar, and a crenellated wall on the right; this matches the stone's long top groove, left vertical (= the man's body; no head/arms visible) and right vertical (= wall; no crenellations visible). Note roth_col<unit> strips appear shifted by one here: roth_col24.png shows column 23's sequence (bar, t, stroke, qd, wall).

signs.note: crenellated enclosure with a small standing man inside; lower part runs into the lost zone
signs.trace_notes: Enclosure under the qd-frame 23.R5. Traced: the long top line (clear, FULL y~1721, x 4130-4248; crop y~186, x 111-465), the left wall (faint, a pale vertical groove at crop x~147-153 from the top line down to y~480, i.e. FULL x~4142; NOT the column rule, which is the longer straight line ~30 FULL px further left at FULL x~4113 and is not traced), and inside, centred under the top line, a sunk rounded hollow with a straight top edge (crop x 222-352, y 302-452), traced as its rim (faint). Rothoehler draws the top and left walls with crenellations (teeth) and a small standing man inside; on the stone no teeth are distinguishable (small dark notches just above the top line at FULL y~1710 are not clearly cut) and the inner figure shows only as this rounded hollow, no head/legs separable, so its identity as his man is uncertain (it is wider and rounder than his figure). No right wall visible; below y~480 the surface runs into the flaked/lost zone. roth.png: his drawing here is badly misplaced (thick strokes); matched by sequence with his plate (ripple, mouth+Z1, pot, qd frame, enclosure).

Goose (Rothöhler draws the same G38 goose: lens body, neck rising at the front, head/beak to the right, two legs and a foot line). Stone: long lens body 528-790 x 609-690 (outlines merge at both tips), neck as a curved groove from the front tip (faint, steep, ~760-790 x 500-613), head a short groove at 755-812 y~488. Legs not visible (surface pitted; steep strokes give little evidence). A clear horizontal cut at y~750 (632-712 and 724-805, in photo AND native) sits where Rothöhler's foot line is: traced as the feet (faint). A shorter cut below it at 668-720 y~787 left untraced (could be part of the feet or of the I10 below at ~650-830 x 880-940). Rothöhler overlay is offset about -345 x, +180 y crop px here (his goose drawn at ~880-1170 x 295-530).

signs.note: L-shaped sign (vertical with foot turned right; seat/foot-like), left; project S43; he draws an L (like his Q1/D58 L-signs elsewhere), not a curved-top staff; position matches 24.3
signs.trace_notes: L-shaped sign at the left of the column under the goose 24.R1, left of the bird on a standard 24.R3. Traced: the foot as a sunk triangular wedge (clear in relief/photo/native: dark diagonal upper wall from (247,245) down-right to the tip (362,312), lit flat bottom y~320-333; rim traced as closed outline, sunk), exactly like Rothoehler's filled triangular foot turned right; and the vertical shaft rising from its left end (faint: a narrow pale groove at crop x~242-247, visible in photo and weakly in relief/native from y~75 to the foot; FULL x~4302, y 1525-1582). Its top is not distinct (fades at y~75, about the level of the bird's head as in his drawing). Not a curved-top S43 staff: no curve visible at the top. Q1 vs D58 not decidable from the stone. roth.png draws the L at the same x but ~70 crop px (~23 FULL) lower; agrees by shape and sequence.

signs.note: bird (ibis?) on a standard, right; project I10 cobra at this place; he draws a bird on a stand
signs.trace_notes: Bird on a standard, right of the L-sign 24.R2, under the goose's foot line (24.R1, the two sunk bars at crop y~90-100, not traced here). Cut as sunk parts, rims traced: the small head (clear, sunk hollow at x 226-286, y 110-157, FULL ~4356-4376, 1494-1509), a faint beak/neck groove running down-left from under the head to (170,186) (as in Rothoehler's long down-left beak), and the horizontal body with its pointed tail to the right (clear, x 209-388, y 232-298; FULL ~4351-4410, 1534-1556). Not visible: the neck curve between head and body, the legs and the standard/base (surface below y~300 shows no consistent cuts; left part there belongs to the L 24.R2's foot wedge at x<370 in that kit). Head/body proportions fit his G26-like bird; species not decidable. 1901 read a cobra I10 here; the cobra is lower (24.R4). roth.png draws this bird ~70 crop px lower than the stone.

signs.note: cobra, head at upper right, body curving down to the left; project '?' (long horizontal); he draws the cobra here
signs.trace_notes: Cobra, matched by sequence: the only carving below the bird-on-standard 24.R3 and the L-foot wedge 24.R2 before the flaked zone. Traced: the horizontal body groove (clear, FULL ~4347-4391, y~1673; crop x 395-528, y~221) = the 1901 '?' long horizontal, and a faint groove curving up-right from its right end towards the head (to (586,165), FULL ~4410,1654), visible in relief/photo/native as a weak dark arc. Head blob not separable. Rothoehler's tail curving down-left from the left end is not traceable: only scattered small marks at crop (335-455, 265-315), no continuous groove. Position: his cobra head is level with the L's foot; on the stone the body lies ~60 FULL px below the foot wedge (his plate compresses this stretch); in kits 24.2/24.3 roth.png draws this unit ~70 crop px too low.

signs.note: cobra body curve (rising from lower left to a horizontal top), small detached head mark at upper right; project '?'; 25.1's cuts and 25.2's curved outline both lie on this curve
signs.trace_notes: Badly worn surface (millstone area). Only two short horizontal cuts are supported in photo, relief AND native inside the green box: one at 500-632 y~507 and one at 666-765 y~603; traced as faint fragments, sign not identifiable (consistent with the tracer's 'group of short cut strokes', possibly part of the dd-mdw heading). Not traced: the pale ledge running diagonally 590-750 x 385-425 (reversed polarity, reads as a break edge of the worn zone, not a groove) and isolated pits/blobs lower down (e.g. 525-565 y~668, weak). Neighbour 25.2's box (445-730 x 475-724) covers the same area; the lower cut (y~603) could belong to 25.2 instead. Rothöhler draws no signs here, only lacuna outlines (his column strip for this area is empty); the two cuts are real in photo and native but he did not record them.

signs.note: cobra body curve with detached head mark at upper right; project '?' (curved outline)
signs.trace_notes: Surface lost (millstone wear). No coherent carved sign inside or near the green box: the bright diagonal in relief at ~550-630 x 470-525 is the edge of a pale broken flake (photo), not a cut. Only candidate: a straight horizontal edge at 605-850 y~435 (top edge of the box) with groove-like polarity in relief and native; in the photo it is the lower border of a rough, darker worn band (y 380-430), and a similar edge continues at the same full height in column 25 (here 80-280 x 430-470; in the 25.1 kit at 590-750 x 385-425), so it reads as a break/wear edge (or ruling), not this sign. Not traced. If 26.1 is a horizontal sign at the head of 26b, that edge (full ~4678-4759, y~3567) is where to look. Empty trace; estimated box kept. Rothöhler also draws only lacuna outlines here; one of his lacuna lines runs across the crop at y~360-430, consistent with the y~435 edge being a break edge.

signs.note: short vertical stroke right of the cobra (ḏd-mdw stroke)
signs.trace_notes: EMPTY: not identifiable on the stone (millstone-worn surface; no anchoring trace nearby, 26.R1 cobra is also empty). Rothoehler's Z1 (roth.png) lies at FULL ~4734-4742, 3604-3657 (crop ~150-175, 150-310): no groove there. Candidate, not traced: a narrow near-vertical dark band with a lit right side ~25 FULL px further right and lower, crop [[223, 300], [229, 340], [234, 390], [239, 445]] (FULL ~4758-4764, 3654-3702), weak in relief and native (trace_score lock 0.93, support 0.12 when tried) and continued upward by a hairline crack to FULL ~3612; it may be his stroke displaced by this group's poor alignment, or a crack.

signs.note: tall narrow pointed leaf (reed) with a side tick; project Z1 (narrow vertical); he draws a reed-leaf shape
signs.trace_notes: Very worn (millstone surface). Traced only a faint, diffuse near-vertical groove at crop x~196-203, y~45-275 (FULL ~4710-4713, 3657-3734), a dark band with a lighter right side in relief and native and a darker streak in the photo; it is where the 1901 copy put its 'narrow vertical' (Z1) box and where the top of Rothoehler's reed should be in y (his apex at FULL ~3655). Low evidence (trace_score lock 0.93; steep stroke), so conf faint and provisional. Rothoehler draws a tall narrow leaf (vertical left edge, diagonal right edge, side tick at the lower right, then a stem down to FULL ~3799); roth.png puts it ~20-25 FULL px further left (FULL x ~4665-4692). Only one line is visible on the stone: no second edge, no tick, no stem below y~275 (pale flakes and pits at x 60-180 are breaks, not cuts). So the stone neither confirms the leaf shape nor the 1901 Z1; roth_agrees false (shape not confirmed).

signs.note: crisp horizontal bar in 26b (photo y≈4300); lies in his stippled/lost zone, he draws nothing
signs.trace_notes: Doubtful sign. A horizontal bar-like feature at crop x 252-388, y ~145-178 (FULL ~4706-4751, 4290-4301): lit lower band (strong in relief, present in native) with a shadowed band above it, clearest on the right half; centre line traced, conf faint. In the photo the lit band is a pale, broken flat surface in two segments, much like the laminar flake ledges around it in this spalled zone (e.g. crop (0-60, 230-280), (250-300, 250-260)), so it may be a ledge rather than a cut; no sign shape can be read. Rothoehler draws nothing here (stippled/lost zone of his plate), so roth_agrees false; kept as a faint trace so it can be judged later rather than lost.

signs.note: small dome/half-disc, left; project '?' (traced as a small dome, X1-like, ~110 crop px above its box)
signs.trace_notes: The curved stroke named in the tracer note (x 2410-2440 half-px) is a clear arch 354-500 x 319-343 (photo, relief and native agree), with a short faint bar under it at 410-476 y~384; together they look like a small dome/half-disc sign (X1-like), traced as such. This lies ~110 crop px ABOVE and left of the green box (box misplaced; real box 350-504 x 314-389), just below/right of 27.3's estimated box. Rothöhler draws a small half-disc at about this place in his sequence (his overlay drawing at 720-815 x 60-95 here; his overlay runs ~one column right and ~60 full px high in this area), so roth_agrees=true (weak). Inside the green box (450-575 x 450-710) and below it there is only a vertical run of short horizontal nicks at x~490-555 (y~545, ~625, ~745, ~850; the last is the clearest) that do not form a recognisable sign; not traced. Rothöhler's lacuna line crosses at y~650-780.

signs.note: L-sign: tall vertical with block and foot to the right; project '?' (curved stroke + two bars); match by sequence only
signs.trace_notes: Worn surface. Three short cuts supported in photo AND native (evidence maps agree): a curved stroke descending from 496,483 into a near-horizontal run to 606,513 (the clearest), a short bar 427-467 y~506 to its left, and a short bar 488-547 y~550 below. Sign not identifiable; the curve-into-horizontal could be the lower part of a d-cobra hook (I10, as at the head of other b-lines), but that is a guess. Rothöhler here draws a small standing man with round head over a small loaf, near 620-745 x 190-600 in this overlay (overlay offset uncertain, possibly a column off as in cols 23/24); his drawing does not match these cuts, so roth_agrees=false. The pale broken area above (350-650 x 150-300) is damage, not traced. Box: traced extent. || fixup 2026-11-08: re-traced. The three old cuts (FULL x ~4861-4921, y ~3555-3578) lie ~110 FULL px above the dome R1 and do not fit his L-sign standing beside R1; removed (unassigned, see findings fix-F2). R2 is now the crisp sunk bar FULL x ~4884-4935, y ~3699-3708 (rim traced as a closed outline; sunk: dark upper wall over lit floor), just below and right of R1's base: his L-sign's foot, which in his strip runs right from the bottom of the upright, below the level of the dome. The upright and the grey block are not visible (above the bar's left end only mottled surface and a diagonal pale wiping streak 4855,3640->4885,3670). PAST CROP EDGE: the bar is at kit y ~595-622, below this crop (height 390); kit should be re-cut ~150 FULL px lower.

signs.note: small standing figure with round head and two legs; project '?' (narrow sign)
small dome at the foot of the group (edge of the lost zone); project '?' (crisp short horizontal bar)
signs.trace_notes: PAST CROP EDGE: traced in kit coordinates at crop y 726-766, far below this crop (height 354), from extended views. Sunk small dome (X1), crisp: arched shadowed upper wall over a lit flat floor, rim traced as closed outline (FULL ~4862-4904, 3884-3897). It lies at the upper edge of the dark lost zone, as Rothoehler says ('small dome at the foot of the group, edge of the lost zone'). Sequence: his R1 dome = traced 27.5 (FULL y ~3680), his overlay for unit 27 is ~55 FULL px too high, and with that shift his R4 lands on this dome. NOT traced: the crisp sunk bar inside the green box (crop x 100-245, y 170-200; FULL 4885-4934, 3699-3709), the old 1901 '27.4'; by position it fits the foot of his L-sign R2 (or another sign of the group), not R4.

signs.note: L-sign with grey inner block (seat-like), top left; project Z1 (short vertical); the tracer also noted his isolated vertical above-left of the loaf
signs.trace_notes: Short vertical stroke (Z1) at x~459, y 238-334, seen as a pale vertical band in photo and a bright vertical in relief AND native; ~110-200 crop px ABOVE the green box (box misplaced up/left; real box 452-466 x 234-338). It does not continue above or below (checked the whole crop height), so it is not the column rule. Steep stroke: weak trace_score evidence is expected. Inside the green box (452-553 x 452-629) there is only broken, flaked surface with no vertical groove. Rothöhler draws a short isolated vertical stroke above-left of his small loaf (= 28.2's crisp bar at 580-740 y~715), which matches this stroke's role; his overlay places it ~270 px left and ~100 px lower (overlay offset unreliable here).

Sunk elongated hollow (rim traced as closed outline): flat top edge, wider rounded left end, x 168-325, y 170-204 crop. Crisp in photo, relief and native. Rothoehler's small loaf/dome (X1) under the L-sign; on the stone it reads more as a flat sunk bar than a domed loaf, but it is his sign by sequence (first of the two bars; the second bar 28.R3 lies ~90 crop px lower).

signs.note: second crisp bar just under 28.2; he draws only one small loaf here

Not traced: (a) the thin bright line running from the right end up to (730,330) is a pale ridge in the photo (it could be a viper head/neck but is not a clear groove); (b) the two thin parallel lines inside the green box (y~465-500) are, in the photo, the edges of pale stepped flakes. They do show in the evidence maps, so they COULD be what Breasted drew as I9. Caveat: the 47.4 tracer_note calls a 'deep modern-looking pit' near here and gives W24 as a rounded outline at y~159-363. If this lens is in fact the base of W24 or a pit, I9 would be the lines at y~465-500. I judge the lens to be carved, because it matches the sunk lens grooves in the 48-52 block, and Rothöhler's spacing and length favour it as I9. No horns or head visible. Rothöhler draws a plain bar here, consistent.

signs.note: god-flag 1; trace on the first flag top
signs.trace_notes: First (leftmost) of the three god-flags at the head of the 48-52 block. The block is retrograde: the 1901 numbering runs left to right, R8 R8 R8 L1 D21 G17 ? Q3 X1 V28 = nṯrw ḫpr m Ptḥ. Only the flag top is traced: a crisp, slightly wedge-shaped sunk groove at x 498-608, y~468-478, deepest at its right end. It is clear in photo, relief and native. The pole is not traced: below the left end (x~505-520, y 520-830) relief shows only scattered pale flecks, with no paired edge in evidence_sign or native ('pole worn; not visible'). The other two flag tops (not traced here) are at x 665-750, y~465 and x 800-890, y~470. The 1901 boxes are off: 48-52.2's box (426-588) overlaps this one, and 48-52.3's box (661-977) covers BOTH the 2nd and 3rd flags. So the 2nd flag = 665-750 and the 3rd = 800-890. Rothöhler draws three Г-flags (pole at left, cloth to the right) in the same row, his first at x~200-330 in roth.png (~-300 px from the carving). Same sign, same order; his full-length poles are not visible on the photo.

signs.note: god-flag 2; 1901 box overlaps flag 1; per 48-52.1 kit flag 2 is at crop x 665-750
signs.trace_notes: Second god-flag (R8), the middle one of three, left to right: flag 1 (R1, traced as 48-52.1) at crop x 189-300 here, this flag at x 351-457, flag 3 beyond the crop (48-52.1 frame x ~800-895). Traced the flag top only: a crisp sunk wedge-shaped groove, higher at its left (pole) end (y ~163) and stepping down to y ~178-185 at the cloth end, deepest at the right; clear in photo, relief and native, same form as flag 1. PAST CROP EDGE: the right end (x 450-457) lies just beyond this crop (width 450); positions taken from the wider 48-52.1 kit (offset: this crop = 48-52.1 crop - (309,303)). The pole is not traced: under the left end a line of pale flecks runs down at x ~345-357, y ~260-500 (48-52.1 frame x ~653-666, y 560-800), consistent in photo, relief and native and in line with Rothoehler's pole, but it shows no paired groove edges, so it is not reliable enough to trace (same judgement as for flag 1). Rothoehler draws full-height poles. KIT: the green box (x 145-307) sits on flag 1, not this flag.

signs.note: god-flag 3; 1901 box covers flags 2 and 3 on the stone
signs.trace_notes: Third (rightmost) god-flag R8, read left to right after flag 1 (48-52.1) and flag 2 (48-52.R2, in this crop x ~141-246; flag 1 at x ~0-90). Traced the flag top only: a crisp sunk groove x 279-376, y ~183 at the left (pole) end sloping to ~199 at the right, deepest along x 300-375; clear in photo, relief and native, same form as flags 1 and 2. Pole not traced: under the left end (x ~265-280, y 280-500; 48-52.1 frame x ~785-800) there are only scattered pale flecks with no consistent groove edges. Rothoehler draws a full-height pole. KIT: the green box (x 145-461) is too wide and its left part covers flag 2; flag 3 lies in its right half. The scarab R4 starts right of x ~400.

Scarab, cut as two SUNK hollows, worn and damaged in between. Traced: (1) the lower hollow (abdomen/elytra) as a closed rim x 153-348, y 448-551, clear in photo, relief and native (bottom arc strongest); (2) the upper hollow (head/thorax) as a faint closed rim x 173-352, y 210-330: top arc and left side clear, right side weak (steep), lower edge along a groove at y ~320-330. Between them (y 335-445) the surface is broken: a pale diagonal ridge from (146,404) to (274,354) and short edges, not traced. Legs not traceable: the arc from (303,211) to (410,283) right of the head could be a right foreleg, but it is isolated and partly runs into the lost area towards the lens R5; not traced. Rothoehler draws an outlined scarab with an oval body over crop y ~300-513 (narrower, x 216-336) and six legs; the stone's overall extent (y 210-551) agrees, but the stone shows two large sunk sections rather than his single oval, and his legs are not visible, so roth_agrees=false on form (identity agrees). Neighbours: lens R5 above right (x 464+), small bird R6 to the right.

signs.note: mouth r (lens above the small bird)
signs.trace_notes: D21 r of ḫpr: a large, crisp lens at x 398-618, y 407-472. Its upper and lower outlines merge at the left tip (398,448) and the right tip (618,440); from the right tip a single tail groove runs on to (685,440). Clear in photo, relief and native, and evidence_sign shows the full outline. The green box (y 452-548) is ~40 px too low and too far right: it catches only the lower outline. Below and right of the lens is the G17/bird area: a diagonal back at x 420-560, y 600-740, and the long diagonal at x 730-940, y 560-800, which Rothöhler shows as the second, bigger bird. Rothöhler draws an oval over the small bird, right of the scarab (roth.png x 60-290, y 320-390, ~+360/+90 from the carving). Same sign and place; he draws no tail.

signs.note: small bird (quail chick w of ḫprw?); project G17; 48-52.6's box covers both birds, matched to the first (small) one
signs.trace_notes: Small bird (Rothoehler's G43, first of the two birds; read left to right before the owl R7). Traced: (1) the back, a deep diagonal groove from the tail end (138,362) up to (233,266), continuing less steeply as a dark wedge to the head end (305,233); clear in photo, relief and native; (2) a short horizontal base/foot groove x 262-352, y ~449 (dark over lit floor, clear in photo, weaker in native), where Rothoehler puts the foot. Not traced: head detail, breast/front line and leg (no consistent groove; the pale pieces at x 200-240, y 330-420 are flakes), and the parallel pale band right of the back. Rothoehler's bird has the same slant and sits ~50 crop px left/~30 high of the carving. Separated from neighbours: the lens R5 above (y 45-123), the scarab R4 to the left, the owl R7's long diagonal starts right of x ~450. KIT: the green box (x 186-639) also covers the owl's diagonal; this sid takes only the small bird.

signs.note: large bird with long diagonal body (owl m); project '?' (scraps); its box sits on this bird's upright front; the owl's long diagonal lies inside 48-52.6's box
signs.trace_notes: Owl (Rothoehler's G17, the large bird with the long diagonal body, second bird of the pair, left to right after the small bird R6). Traced: (1) the long diagonal back groove from the tail end at lower left (17,555) up to the head end (247,268), deep and clear in photo, relief and native (placed just lower-right of the darkest line, at the dark/bright boundary; the lowest part x 17-35 is fainter); (2) the horizontal base/foot groove x 210-358, y ~522 with a short upturn at its left end, clear. Not traced: the head/face (a pale bulge at x 255-300, y 205-330 with no groove outline), the front/breast line and the leg (no consistent edges; Rothoehler draws a front line from the head down and a leg rising from the base to x ~250). The pale striated band parallel to and right of the back (x 50-200) is the body surface, not a cut. Rothoehler's bird matches in slant, length and base position. KIT: the green box (x 173-406) sits on the owl's front/base area; the diagonal back lies left of it, mostly inside R6's 1901 box. The star-shaped feature at x ~420-520, y 430-560 belongs to the wick R8.

Twisted wick V28, worn; all strokes faint. On the stone the sign is a vertical chain on axis x ~255-275: an upper loop (pale ring around a dark hollow, x 230-283, y 325-408) and a lower loop (x 248-298, y 458-510) from whose bottom two strands splay down-left to (214,568) and down-right to (305,573), giving an X-like lower end; this matches Rothoehler's wick with forked foot (his drawing ~20 crop px left). Strands placed at the dark/bright boundary of the sunk diagonal grooves. Not traced: the top of the wick (y 210-320) and the link between the two loops (y 410-455): only pits and flecks, no groove edges. Lock is low (~0.9): loops are rims of small hollows and the strands are steep, so evidence is weak; all are visible in photo, relief and native. Neighbours: owl R7's base ends at x ~150 (left); stool R9 and loaf R10 to the right (x 384+).

Sunk rectangle (stool p), rim traced as closed outline: deep shadowed top wall at y~180, bright lit bottom wall at y~370, side walls faint but visible in photo and native. Pale streak at upper left (x 140-180, y 215-260) is a surface patch, not a cut. Rothoehler draws the same tall rectangle, ~25 crop px further right and ~10 px lower.

X1 t of Ptḥ, under the Q3 rectangle (x 480-580, y 150-340) at the right end of the top line. A SUNK loaf: the dome rim is crisp (dark over bright) from (460,492) over (530,463) to (595,494). The flat base is placed by eye along the lower edge of the lit floor, y~506 (faint: the lower edge of a sunk shape reads bright to dark, so trace_score's lock is low there). The green box fits (shifted slightly left). Rothöhler draws Q3 over a small dome just left of the column rule (roth.png x 70-165, y 320-365, ~+410/+110 from the carving). Same sign and arrangement.

V28 ḥ of Ptḥ at the head of col 49a. Only the TOP loop of the twisted wick is traced: a small loop at x 458-523, y 438-512. Its rounded top is crisp (dark over bright) and its pointed V-shaped lower end is at (492,511). Visible in photo, relief, native and both evidence maps. Below it (y 520-760) the rest of the wick, the lower loops and the forked foot, cannot be made out: only scattered flecks, with no coherent outline in evidence or native ('lower loops not visible: surface worn'). The bright arm running up-right from the V to (550,475) may be the start of the crossing strand but is too short to trace with confidence. Placement: carved Q3 rectangle at x 650-740, y 440-615 (11:Q3 box) and X1 dome at x 640-760, y 750-800 (12:X1 box) lie to its right, as in Rothöhler (his V28 + Q3 + X1 at roth.png ~-307/-200 from the carving). The green box (450-560 x 450-850) is right for the column but its top should be ~15 px higher.

Sunk rectangle (stool p), worn; rim traced in four parts. Top wall (deep shadow y~80-105, x 165-260) and lit bottom wall (bright bar y~270-290, x 158-248) are clear in relief and native; the side walls are only faintly seen (sunk floor patchy), drawn faint at the extent of the top/bottom walls. Tops of R11 wick (left, y~104) and this stool line up, the dome R13 sits below at y~420-450, matching his sequence. The green box covered only the lower middle. roth.png drifts here: it draws the dome R13 over this stool (stool ~250 crop px higher in his overlay).

Sunk dome (t), rim traced as closed outline: arched top wall in deep shadow, flat lit base. Clear in relief, photo and native. Directly below the stool R12 and above the Q1/D2 pair, as in his strip. roth.png drifts: it draws D2 (R15) over this dome; matched by sequence.

signs.note: tall seat st (left); side by side with D2, read left first
signs.trace_notes: Very worn. Only the foot of the seat survives: a clear horizontal base groove at y~488 (x 118-204; dark above, lit wall below, in relief and native) and a short dark vertical wall at x~142 rising from it to y~425 (photo clear, relief/native faint), bounding a shallow sunk pocket to its right (x 142-200, y 425-485), i.e. the low seat part of his L-shaped Q1 at the foot of the back. The tall back above (his drawing: narrow upright on the left, up to ~y 235) is not traceable: no consistent groove edges, surface pitted; a pale diagonal streak at (200,255)-(280,350) is a wiping mark, not a cut. Read left of D2 (R15), which lies higher, to the right (x~280-400, y~195-340).

Only one groove survives: a deep horizontal groove at y~143-157 (x 165-300), dipping slightly at x~232, clear in relief, photo and native, ~45 crop px below the dome R13's base and right of/above the Q1 foot (R14), where his D2 lies in sequence. Read as the top edge of his pointed oval/face; the rest of the oval (his lateral points, lower outline and short tail below) is not traceable: the surface below (x 150-300, y 165-320) is worn smooth with only pits; the pale diagonal (110,200)-(210,290) is a wiping streak. Rothoehler draws a complete oval ~120 crop px wide; only its top agrees in position (roth_agrees false because the trace is a fragment of uncertain fit).

Swallow facing right, worn. Traced: the long back line rising from the tail tip at lower left (212,318) to (360,217); the head/neck line (366,188)-(478,151) rising to the beak at upper right (clear dark groove, in relief and native; the round dark spot at ~(470,145) may be a pit at the beak); the base/belly line from the tail (215,320) to (378,282), faint, diverging from the back at the tail as in his drawing. Not traceable: the breast/front between base end and head (his right side, ~x 430-470) - the area is a pale smooth patch (440,250-300) with no groove edge; the step between back and neck at x~360 is not clear. Rothoehler's outline agrees in shape and lies within ~10-20 crop px.

signs.note: short flat bar t; traced as flat bar ~70-100 FULL px below the 1901 box
signs.trace_notes: Seed-box move. The green box (x 440-520, y 450-550) is NOT X1. It holds a dark pit at (445,520) and part of the long diagonal groove (345,555)-(520,490), which belongs to the G36 bird / Q1 group above. By Rothöhler's col 49a order (V28 Q3 X1 | D2 Q1 | bird | SHORT BAR | lens | dome), the t of wrt is the short bar between the swallow and the D21 lens. On the stone the swallow sits at x ~200-470, y 520-700 and the D21 lens at x 200-470, y 850-900. Mapped with the same offset (~+250 x / +310 y crop px), his bar falls at x ~350-430, y ~740. There the stone has a flat, shallow horizontal groove, x 352-478 at y~759 (dark band above, lit band below). It shows in photo, relief and native evidence. Traced as faint: it is shallow and its ends are vague. Its shape is a plain bar, not a dome. 'X1' fits as a flat t (Rothöhler draws a short flat stroke, not a loaf); identity kept. The tracer_note's 'box lies on worn surface' is correct for the 1901 box.

Lens (D21), long oval with pointed tips, left tip lower than the right. Upper outline clear (dark groove y~238-250, strongest on the right half x 330-430); lower outline and left tip fainter but visible in photo and native; the darker pocket inside (250-310, 278-290) is the hollow interior. Pale smooth diagonal patch at (360-420, 265-310) is not a cut; the dark blob at (300-330, 190-220) above is a pit. Rothoehler's oval matches in shape, ~40 crop px lower in roth.png; his small bar R17 above is the bar traced at 48-52.17.

CRITIQUE: A's base line ran through the middle of the lit band (y~140), about 8 px below the groove centre, which is the dark-to-bright boundary at y~123-135 per relief, native and photo. C moves it there. The base has strong evidence across the hollow (x94-169, clear). The leftward extension to x48 (outside the green box, no dome above it) also has a real groove edge, but it is kept as a separate faint stroke because it is unclear whether it belongs to this loaf or is a longer N35-like line. The dome is kept as A drew it: it marks the top edge of the dark sunk hollow, clear in all three images. It is an edge of the cut, not a paired groove, so its lock stays ~1.0 by construction. The bright blob at (130-165,75-100) is a pale spot, not a cut, and stays untraced. X1 is still preferred: the dome is a true half-disc and there is no zigzag. The sign sits in the left part of the green box.

Shrine (C20), only the arch of the roof survives: a long groove from (148,165) rising to a flat crown at y~124 (x 280-340) and turning down at the right to (448,192), clear in relief, photo and native. It matches his arch trace in shape (his falls on the right too). The figure traces he draws below (a short diagonal and a curved left stroke) are not identifiable on the photo: the area below the arch (y 200-750) is pitted, with a darker stained patch at (90-200, 540-700) but no groove edges; not traced. roth.png sits ~240 crop px too LOW here (his arch drawn at y 365-430) and ~70 px right; placed by sequence: the arch lies ~110 crop px below the dome R19, as his strip spacing predicts.

Twisted wick, left sign of the 50a top row (read before the stool R22 to its right). Traced: the top loop (sunk oval hollow, rim clear in all views), and the splayed foot as an inverted V (apex (213,478), legs to y~546, clear). The middle twist (y 270-460) is badly worn and crossed by a large dark pit at (150-190, 280-330) and a pale flake at (140-200, 340-380): only fragments are traced, faint: a horizontal crossing at y~342 and the right/lower curve of the lowest loop (208,370)-(190,440). Rothoehler draws three loops above the splayed foot; the overall height (~360 crop px) and positions agree. A diagonal edge (220,300)-(314,331) is not part of the wick (runs out of the sign's width).

Sunk rectangle (stool p), right sign of the 50a top row, read after the wick R21 on its left. Rim in four parts: top wall (deep shadow y~135-147, x 225-305) and lit bottom wall (bright y~300-325, x 208-305) clear in relief, photo and native; side walls faint (right wall shadow seen at x~300-310, y 165-220; left wall only implied). Interior is broken by flakes (the diagonal pale/dark streak at (235-275, 195-235) is damage). The dome R23 lies below at y~460-510 (traced at 48-52.22); the dark hole at (240-300, 345-375) and pale lump below the stool are a flake/pit, not part of it. Rothoehler's stool agrees in shape and sequence.

X1 t of Ptḥ in col 50a: the sunk loaf under the Q3 (21:Q3 box x 430-570, y 125-310), right of the V28 (x 280-370). The green box is correct. Traced: the dome rim, crisp dark over bright from (462,483) over (518,460) to (573,479), in photo, relief and both evidence maps. The flat base is not traced: the lit floor fades out at y~500-510 with no edge in evidence or native ('base not visible'). Rothöhler (his col 50a sits ~-300 x from the carving in roth.png) draws V28 | Q3 over a dome, then three nw pots and the N36 bar. The spacing matches the carving (pots at y~630-745, N36 at y~800-890), so he agrees. The bright lump at x 510-600, y 345-395, between Q3 and the dome, is a flake, not a sign.

signs.note: nw pot (left); traced at the left pot of the row; 1901 box was inside N36
signs.trace_notes: Uncertain. The 1901 box (inside the N36 box, x 450-550, y 450-555) holds only the left end of the N36 groove (y~483) and a bright crystal sliver at (465-495, 495-530). No pot there. Rothöhler draws Nwn in col 50a as THREE nw pots side by side in one row, between the X1 dome and the N36 bar. On the stone that row is y ~290-400 (X1 at y 120-190, N36 groove at y 483). Its left end, matching the 1901 box's x-range, has a pale, rounded, sunk-looking oblong at x 480-530, y 296-388 (narrow top, rounded base). It shows in photo, relief and native, and I trace its rim as a faint closed outline (sunk; rim placed by eye). Evidence is weak (support 0.29). This could equally be a lit flake, so treat the outline as provisional. A similar pale form at x 725-790, y 300-400 fits as the rightmost pot (the 1901 25:W24 box is at 645-735). The middle position (~x 600-660) has only a diagonal pale streak. Box correction: 48-52.26 belongs in the pot row at y~295-390, not in the N36 box. The 1901 split of 24/25 above and 26 below is wrong per Rothöhler.

EMPTY: surface lost. The middle nw pot of his three-pot row (between the N36 bar and the dome R23) should lie at about x 210-275, y 95-235 here (row: left pot R24 body at x~91-139, right pot R26 body at x~343-404, y 140-250; rim bars at y~100 above both). At that place the stone shows only a long pale diagonal streak (268,115)-(228,175) (wiping mark), small pits, and a vague pale smear at (205-255, 205-225) with no groove edge in close-up relief, photo or native. Rothoehler draws all three pots complete; the middle one is not verifiable on the photo.

Right nw pot of the three-pot row (rightmost in reading order L->R). Traced: the rim bar, a short horizontal groove at y~100 (x 237-276; dark above, lit slab below), and the body as a sunk oval hollow (pale lit floor x 228-302, y 150-248, shadowed top wall with two dark pockets at y~130-150), rim placed by eye: sunk, faint. The neck between bar and body and his inner dot are not visible. The pale oval blob at (305-331, 73-110) to the upper right is a flake, not part of the pot. Matches the left pot R24 (traced at 48-52.26, same pale-body form) and his drawing (bar over a rounded body).

Canal bar N36 under the three pots: long deep horizontal groove from (178,238) to (503,219), rising slightly to the right, clear in all views; both ends turn down as in his drawing: the left leg (x~180, to y~322) and the right leg (x~505, to y~300) are faint (vertical, weak evidence; left leg runs beside a pale crystal sliver at (180-210, 230-330), which is not a cut). A dark diagonal wedge rising from the bar's right end to (575,178) is a break/flake edge, not traced. Rothoehler agrees in shape and position (his bar is the line under the W24 row).

C20 shrine of 50a, very worn (FULL ~8381-8544, 2127-2476). Traced: the arch, left part clear (dark->bright edge from (92,198) up to the apex at ~(345,110), which is where Rothoehler puts his apex), right part faint, descending to meet the 51a shrine's arch at (570,198); the right wall as a long faint vertical at x~570 from the arch end down to y~1000 (clear in relief, pale line in photo); a short inner parallel groove at x~536, y 790-950 (Rothoehler's inner right line); a long faint inner vertical at x~452 (y 400-1140; his inner vertical, which he draws only y~600-970 and ~60 crop px further left); and the base line at y~1146 (x 100-425, clear). Not traced: a left wall (no groove; Rothoehler also draws none, only a separate vertical further left), the standing figure and the small inner signs he draws (o, hook, C, =): nothing distinguishable from the pitting. A second, lower horizontal at y~1225 runs under the whole width and joins the 51a shrine's base via a diagonal crack at x~430-500; not traced here (probably R39's base or a ruling). roth.png sits ~45 crop px too far left and the base ~25 px too high; matched by sequence and shape.

X1 t of 50a (left of the reed R30), under the R28 shrine base (FULL ~8407-8447, 2545-2559). Sunk low dome: dark upper wall (y~150-165) over a lit flat floor ending at y~190, clear in photo, relief and native; rim traced as a closed outline ('sunk', so lock is low as expected). Separated from the large bright flake below-left (x 190-250, y 200-260), which is a pale break, not carving. Rothoehler draws his dome ~110 crop px higher (roth.png drift); matched by sequence: first sign after the shrine, on the left.

M17 reed of 50a (right of the dome R29), very worn; surface broken here. Traced only one faint near-vertical groove (FULL ~8480-8483, 2516-2565): a thin dark line in the photo with a weak matching vertical shading in relief and native, at the place where Rothoehler's reed stands once his drift is removed (his dome is ~37 FULL px too high here, so his reed maps to ~FULL 8486-8508, 2540-2633). Read as the left edge/stem of the reed; uncertain (could be a crack). Not visible: the leaf outline to the right, the foot. The pale diagonal bar at (180-250, 300-340) below is a raised ridge, not a groove; the dark pit at (190,360) is damage. roth_agrees=false because only this fragment can be matched to his outline. Steep stroke: low lock expected.

U15 sledge of 50a (FULL ~8405-8507, 2694-2729). Traced: the long runner, a crisp straight groove at y~213 (x 228-433) whose right end turns up to the right to (533,144) (clear in photo, relief, native, evidence), and a shorter upper line (faint) running parallel above it from (356,166) and also turning up at the right to (490,115): together the two lines with the upturned front, Rothoehler's '=<' drawn with the front at the right. His forked crossing at the very front is not separately visible. roth.png sits ~40 FULL px too high in this part of 50a (his sledge ~2668-2690, stone 2694-2729); matched by sequence: shrine base, dome + reed, sledge, stroke.

signs.note: tall vertical stroke; no project sid
signs.trace_notes: EMPTY: surface illegible. Rothoehler draws a tall single vertical stroke under the sledge R31. The sledge's runner is at crop y~150 here (FULL 2731), but his sledge in roth.png sits ~120 crop px (~40 FULL) higher, so his stroke maps to about crop x 150-240, y 265-520 (FULL ~8432-8462, 2770-2855). On the photo this area is a granular, pitted surface with only pale flakes and a damage pit at (205-235, 340-370); no vertical groove edge in relief, native or the evidence map. Nothing traced.

V28 twisted wick, first sign of 51a (FULL ~8559-8600, 1594-1715). Three stacked loops traced as closed rims (top loop crisp in relief, native and evidence; the loops narrow to waists at y~199 and ~296), and the two splayed legs from the lowest waist (~190,392) down-left to (136,466) and down-right to (248,452), faint but visible in relief and native. Rothoehler's drawing agrees in shape; his roth.png overlay sits ~10-20 crop px left/high. Right of it the Q3 (R34) and the dome R35; below, the W24 pot (R36).

Q3 stool p of 51a, right of the V28 (R33) and above the sunk dome R35 (traced 48-52.34). Sunk rectangle, rim traced as closed outline (FULL ~8646-8669, 1600-1651): top edge crisp (deep shadow), right wall clear as a dark shadow band, bottom edge at y~296 in relief, native and evidence; the left wall is weak (steep, vertical) but the lit interior ends there. A broad bright band at the bottom continues left of the rectangle to x~150 (stone texture or wear, not traced). The green box sits ~45 crop px too far left. Rothoehler agrees (tall rectangle).

X1 t of Ptḥ in col 51a: a SUNK loaf directly under the Q3 rectangle (33:Q3 box, x 435-525, y 175-365), right of the V28 (x 240-340). The green box fits but is ~35 px too narrow on the left. Traced: the dome rim from the left foot (420,509) over (480,468) to the right foot (554,506), crisp dark over bright in photo, relief and both evidence maps. signs.note: long-legged bird with slender neck; 1901 G17; opus_findings: possibly not an owl
signs.trace_notes: Seed. Sunk bird: rim of the pale sunk silhouette traced as a closed outline (small head at top right crop ~735-785,626-660; long body running down-left to the tail at ~538,860; FULL ~9110-9194, 4181-4260). Below it a sunk leg strip, its two edges traced faint (x~595-601 and ~641-648, y 868-944; seen as a pale strip in photo with paired edges in relief and native), standing on a clear short base groove (crop 598-765, y~946, FULL ~4288) which 1901 boxes as 55.53 'N35'. The three N35 lines below are the long rising grooves at crop y~1000-1020, 1060-1080, 1120-1140, not the 1901 boxes at 878/956/1075.

Upright rectangle, worn; probably sunk (pale floor with horizontal striations in the photo, deep shadow above the top edge), rim traced as a closed outline at FULL ~9196-9217, 4217-4257. Top edge clear, sides and bottom faint but present in relief and native. Right of the long-legged bird R56 (55.50), above the three bars. Rothoehler's rectangle (roth.png ~30 crop px left and ~40 high) has the same proportions; agrees by sequence. The 1901 green box sits ~25 crop px higher and is narrower.

signs.note: bar 1 of three stacked lines; opus_findings: lines at FULL y≈4314/4333/4351
signs.trace_notes: Bar 1 (top) of the three stacked long bars, FULL x ~9105-9213, y ~4313 at the left rising to ~4296 at the right end (the bars curve up to the right, as Rothoehler draws them). Clear in relief, native and photo. The short bar above it (FULL y ~4288, x 9140-9195) is the long-legged bird's foot line (traced in 55.50), not a bar: his strip shows the bird's foot separate from three bars. Bar 2 (55.53) at FULL y ~4331, bar 3 (55.54) at ~4350. KIT: the 1901 green box (FULL y 4261-4270) lies on the bird's legs, ~45 FULL px above this bar.

Bar 2 (middle) of the three stacked long bars, FULL x ~9106-9212, y ~4330 at the left, curving up to ~4311 at the right end (the right part is chipped along its edge in the photo but the groove is continuous in relief and native). Bar 1 (55.52) lies ~18 FULL px above, bar 3 (55.54) ~18 below. Rothoehler agrees (three bars curving up to the right). KIT: 1901 green box (FULL y 4287-4296) is ~40 FULL px too high.

Seed. Traced the third (lowest) of three long parallel grooves that rise to the right (Rothoehler draws three slightly curved slanted lines here; N35 as straight/slanted strokes, no ripple visible): crop 442-797, y 525 at left rising to 436 at right (FULL ~9105-9224, 4351-4321). The other two: line 1 crop ~445-760, y~415->360 (FULL ~4314-4296) and line 2 crop ~445-790, y~470->405 (FULL ~4333-4311) - these should be 55.52 and 55.53. The 1901 boxes are spread too far apart: 55.52's box (y~256-282) holds only the leg of bird 55.50, 55.53's box (y~337-358) holds the short straight base groove under that bird's feet (crop 520-680, y~340), and this sid's green box sits on line 2. Sequence (Rothoehler col 55): bird + rectangle (55.50, 55.51) / three slanted lines / small rectangle, dash and tall stroke (55.55-55.57). Right end of the line rises more steeply after x~700. Ripples not visible; straight lines.

Sunk upright rectangle: rim traced as a closed outline (deep shadow along the top wall at y 152-167, pale floor, bright lit bottom wall at y 275-293; sides soft, faint in relief and native). FULL ~9125-9147, 4366-4414. Left of the tall rounded sign R62 (55.56) and directly above the loaf R63 (55.57, FULL y ~4434). Rothoehler's rectangle has the same shape; roth.png draws it ~55 crop px (~18 FULL) higher. The 1901 green box fits. trace_score lock <1 is expected for a sunk rim (the scorer looks for the dark->bright groove pair inside the hollow).

Tall narrow sign with a rounded top: the arch (FULL ~9188-9209, top y ~4372) is visible in relief, native and photo (bright lit arc with a dark hollow below); the left side runs down to y ~290 crop (FULL ~4407) as a faint diagonal pale band; the right side only weakly (traced faint to y 300). Below ~y 300 the surface is pitted; Rothoehler's long legs (left to ~FULL 4435, right to ~4470) are not visible on the photo and are not traced. Right of the rectangle R61 (55.55); roth.png ~55 crop px higher, same sign by sequence. The pale blob right of the arch at (281-311, 210-225) is surface, not traced.

Sunk loaf (X1): rim traced as a closed outline, domed top (deep shadow of the upper wall, y 157-179) over a flat bright base (lit lower wall, y 179-196). FULL ~9118-9153, 4425-4439. Below the rectangle R61 (55.55), above the arm R64 (55.58). Rothoehler draws the same domed loaf ~55 crop px (~18 FULL) higher; agrees by sequence. trace_score lock <1 is expected for a sunk rim (the scorer looks for the dark->bright groove pair inside the hollow).

Seed. Sequence (Rothoehler col 55): three slanted lines (55.52-55.54) / small rectangle + tall stroke (55.55, 55.56) / dash (55.57) / THIS sign: a long groove with a forked left end, running right and then curving down to the lower right / lens (55.59 D21, crop ~440-640,590-630) / bird (55.60). Traced: main groove crop 466-738 (top at y~463, FULL ~9094-9185, 4458-4499), descending right part to ~(738,586); a short lower prong under its left end (crop 498-556, y~493-499), giving the forked 'hand' end. The descending part ends where the head of bird 55.60 begins (~(740-760,600-615)); the boundary between the two is not sharp. A pale streak above the left end (crop ~510-560, y~445) is not traced. Box: inside and below the 1901 box, which it overlaps well.

Lens/mouth D21, outline groove clear in relief, native and photo: upper and lower outlines merging into a single tail at each tip (left tip FULL ~(9084,4511), right tip ~(9151,4507)); dark interior. FULL ~9083-9152, 4500-4514. Left of the bird R66 (55.60), below the arm R64 (55.58). A pale streak continues ~8 FULL px right of the right tip toward the bird; not clearly a cut, not traced. Rothoehler's lens matches in shape; roth.png ~50 crop px (~17 FULL) higher.

Rothoehler's R66 long-necked bird, partial. signs.note: small upright rectangle at the lacuna edge; seed note: this sid = the rectangle below the bird

signs.note: curved sickle-like hook with a small tick at top; his form is only loosely a sickle

signs.note: figure-8 double loop, right; project F20 (uncertain on the stone)

signs.note: slim bird with small beaked head; project G17; he draws a slim bird, not his owl type

signs.note: small lens right of the bird

signs.note: shield with crossed arrows (hmswt emblem) 1; project '?' (same sign, no code)

signs.note: faint dome-like mark left of/above the loaf 58.9 (seed finding: two domes on the stone); he draws only the right one

Sunk: rim placed by eye. | closeup: the close-up shows the same peaked pale shape (apex ~150,202, left flank a defined pale edge down to ~(90,320), right flank weaker, broad pale floor below y~250 with no base line); it does not decide between a sunk loaf and a damage hollow, so the open faint outline stays as it was.

signs.note: bread loaf; he draws one plain loaf, the right of the two dome marks on the stone (58.9's trace); not F51
signs.trace_notes: A flat dome-shaped sign sits just right of centre between the D36 forearm (y~410) and the V30 basket (y~640-740), probably sunk. Its domed top is clear, with a dark rim above a bright fill. The base at y~603 is faint, seen as the lower rim in native. The shape reads as a loaf/dome (X1) rather than a fleshy F51. Rothöhler (his col 58, matched by sequence D36 > dome > V30) draws exactly one small dome here, in this position, and only damage dots to its left. The stone also shows a second, peaked dome-like shape at the left, x~310-420, y~500-610: this is presumably Breasted's 58.8 X1. Not traced. So the labels have two signs where Rothöhler has one, and 'F51' is doubtful. | closeup: the close-up shows a crisp sunk dome: a dark arched upper wall over a pale floor, base clearer than in the photo (the close-up sits ~10 px higher than photo.png here; positions taken from the photo). The domed top was traced on the lower edge of the shadow; moved up 5-8 px to the rim. Base unchanged. Its neighbour R7 (58.8) at left is a much vaguer pale patch.

Basket, sunk: a half-lens hollow with a straight top (FULL y~1822-1828, x 9659-9765) and a rounded bottom down to y~1852. Rim traced as a closed outline; top edge is the start of the deep shadow, bottom edge the lower end of the lit floor (placed by eye). Clear in relief, photo and native. Matches Rothoehler's basket (R9). | closeup: the close-up shows the sunk basket crisply: straight top under a deep shadow and a pale rounded floor whose lower rim follows the traced outline within a few px. No change.

Loaf, sunk dome (left of pair): domed top FULL x 9654-9700, top y~1892; flat base at y~1915. Rim traced as closed outline; domed top clear (deep shadow), base placed by eye at the lower end of the lit floor (clearer in photo than in relief). Matches Rothoehler's small loaf left of the ring. | closeup: the close-up shows the sunk loaf clearly (domed shadowed top, pale floor to y~200); the brownish patch at its right (x 270-320) is a stone inclusion, not carving. Rim already fits; no change.

Ring (Aa1 as Rothoehler reads it), right of the loaf R10. A clear incised oval ring, groove centre FULL x 9724-9756, y 1876-1908, with a slightly raised, pitted centre. Clear in relief, photo and native. No internal hatching visible (the pits inside are damage). | closeup: the close-up shows the ring as a pale incised oval (x~128-225, y~230-325) around a pitted centre, exactly on the trace; no internal hatching. No change.

signs.note: horned viper (horizontal snake); drawn the same as n=14

Two short pale diagonal streaks rise from it ((724,512)-(747,535) and (751,543)-(781,505)) and could be the horns, but they are not clearly grooves, so they stay untraced.

Long-legged bird facing right, worn. Traced: head top and the back of the neck (FULL ~9712-9733, 1990-2018; faint), the back running down-left to the tail point (~9655,2061; clear, deep shadow), the lower tail/wing line converging at the tail (faint), one upright leg/rear-body line at x~9689 (2057-2087; faint, steep: weak lock) and the ground line at y~2089 (x 9676-9727; clear). signs.note: tongue (ns); whole tongue = 58.33's trace; 58.34 (F20) box covers the same sign, listed as phantom

On the stone it leaves the line ~12 FULL px short of the left end rather than at a sharp corner. The crop coordinates in the older note predate the kit rebuild.

signs.note: short vertical stroke; drawn vertical, under F39

The surface here is pitted and crossed by diagonal scratches; the only vertical feature at Rothoehler's position is a soft light vertical band with a dark edge on its right at x~334-342, y 145-218, seen in relief, photo and native but without a crisp groove edge (vertical grooves get weak evidence; scorer support is patchy). The green 1901 box (x 145-506) is far wider than the sign.

Water N35 cut as a SUNK zigzag band (rim traced as one closed outline): teeth along the top edge (peaks at x ~247, 300, 342, 402, 447, 493; y ~265-276), a nearly straight lower edge at y ~312-320, left end at x~215, right end tapering to x~548.
