Rothoehler draws a 6-peak zigzag line here; his roth.png sits ~45 crop px high. Separated from the Z1 R37 above (y<222) and the loaf/ring pair R39/R40 below.

Sunk loaf (X1), the dome left of the Aa1 circle 58.44 under the N35 water line; traced rim of the hollow (flat base + domed top, peak slightly left of centre). Rothöhler draws X1 left of Aa1 in the same position in the sequence (his column labelled 58 is in strip roth_col59.png). roth.png overlay is offset by ~700 crop px.

Ring (Aa1) right of the loaf R39: incised circular outline, slightly wider than tall, clear in relief, photo and native. No internal hatching visible. A short bright streak running down-left from the ring's lower-left (to ~(180,232)) looks like surface damage, not traced; Rothoehler draws a plain ring.

Basket (V30), sunk: a hollow with a nearly straight top (deep shadow along its upper wall) and a curved bowl bottom (lit lower wall), crop x 160-435, y ~170-258; rim traced as a closed outline. The bottom is deepest slightly left of centre (~x 300) and the right end rises a little. Lies under the loaf R39 / ring R40 pair and above the scarab R42. trace_score lock is low (off_cut) as expected for a sunk rim.

signs.note: scarab (ḫpr); he draws a full scarab amid dotted (damaged) surface
cobra (ḏ); head at top right, body curving down-left
signs.trace_notes: Only the cobra's body survives: one long groove rising from the tail at lower left (430,770) and running level to x~650 (full ~9600-9672, y~3580-3607). The head/hood should be at the right end (x~680-730, y~700-790) but that patch is broken (pits and flakes); not traced. Rothöhler (his col. 58 = strip roth_col59.png, sequence ...L1 N35 I10 D46 D4 D21 U15) draws I10 with the same rising tail at left and level body; the eye D4 lies just below at full y~3640-3655, consistent. The 1901 box covers I10 and D46 together; the area above (y 380-650) is heavily damaged and holds nothing traceable. roth.png overlay is offset by several hundred crop px.

signs.note: hand (d); under the cobra; 58.49/58.50 boxes identical in 1901
signs.trace_notes: Hand (D46) under the cobra R44, cut sunk in two parts: an upper short hollow (thumb / back of the hand, crop x 268-432, y 471-527) above a long lower hollow (palm and fingers, x 220-488, y 530-572); both rims traced as closed outlines (shadowed upper walls, lit lower walls in photo, relief and native). Matches Rothoehler's two-tier hand, which roth.png draws ~55 crop px too high and ~40 px too far left. The cobra arc traced in 58.49 lies at y ~345-400; the bright pit at (290-320, 575-600) below the hand is damage, not traced.

Eye (D4) under the hand R45: upper lid rising steeply from the left tip (140,236) and running across the top, lower lid nearly straight at y ~246 (its groove runs on left to x ~100, past the front corner), the two meeting at the pointed right tip (386,232); pupil as a small sunk hollow at (205-268, 207-228). Upper lid's right half is worn (fainter between x 280 and 330). Rothoehler's eye matches in shape; roth.png draws it ~55 crop px too high. The sunk loaf R47 below (y ~320-355) not traced here.

signs.note: bread loaf (small, filled); small sunk loaf under the eye where 1901 has D21
signs.trace_notes: Small sunk loaf (X1) under the eye R46, between the eye and the sledge R48: a low domed hollow (dome x ~308-393, shadowed top) on a wider flat base (x ~273-423, y ~317-336); rim traced as a closed outline. PAST CROP EDGE: the loaf lies at the bottom/right edge of this kit (only its top is inside the 399x321 crop); traced from the 58.51 kit (offset x+108, y-21 from 58.51 crop to this kit) with points beyond y=321. Rothoehler's small filled loaf under the eye matches; roth.png draws it ~60 crop px too high and slightly left. 1901's D21 label here is wrong (Rothoehler relabel confirmed).

Sledge U15 (tm of ꞽtm): two long parallel grooves ~10 full px apart, the upper one turning up at its right end (front of the runner) at (692,558); a deep shadowed hollow lies above the upper groove at x 560-690. No struts visible. Identified by sequence on the stone below I10 (58.49 arc), the flat sign at full y~3640 (D46), the eye at full y~3690 (D4) and a small sunk sign at full y~3730 (D21), and above the long single bar at crop y~735 (O34, 58.54); matches Rothöhler's col. 58 (strip roth_col59.png): I10 D46 D4 D21 U15 O34 L1. Rothöhler draws the hook rising from the runner; stone shows it on the upper groove. 1901 box is close (slightly higher/taller).

Bolt (O34): a long horizontal sunk bar (left half x 250-356 thicker, right half x 460-570 thinner, both clear, traced as centre lines with groove width) with a small lozenge in the middle (x 415-462, y 221-264, slightly tilted, visible in photo, relief and native). Between the left half and the lozenge (x 356-415) the bar is worn (faint). Under the sledge R48 (traced in 58.53); the line at crop y ~128 just under the sledge's traced strokes is not part of this sign. Rothoehler's bolt matches; roth.png draws it ~55 crop px too high.

signs.note: scarab (ḫpr); 58.56 box falls inside the scarab, listed as phantom
signs.trace_notes: Scarab (L1) between the bolt R49 (bar at crop y ~243 here) and the three flags (top bars at y ~720): the surface is badly worn and crossed by many horizontal tooling/grinding streaks, so only two fragments are traceable, both faint but visible in relief, native and the groove-evidence map: the upper-right front-leg arc (240,299)-(334,342) and the lower part of the left hind leg (114,586)-(200,660). Body, head and the other legs not distinguishable from the damage; not traced. These fragments fit Rothoehler's full scarab (which he draws amid dotted damaged surface) when his drawing is moved ~55 crop px down. Box = extent of the two fragments; the sign occupies roughly x 100-345, y 290-670.

LEFT flag (first in reading order) of the three ntr flags cut side by side above the large mouth 58.60: top bar/cloth x527-618 at y~494 (clear, dark-over-bright groove) and the pole down its left end, x~525-527 from the bar to y~768 (faint: a steep groove, seen as a lit band x507-527 in relief, photo and native, strongest at y700-765; weak scorer evidence is expected for a vertical). The cloth's hanging end is not visible. Rothöhler draws three flags here in a row (Gamma-shaped: pole on the left, bar to the right); his left flag's pole merges with his column line. Other two flags (crop px): middle bar x~635-740,y~496 with pole x~635-645; right bar x~757-847,y~494 with pole x~760-767 (traced earlier, kept as trace_wrongflag.json). The 1901 boxes 58.58 (x626-724) and 58.59 (x735-845) fit the middle and right flags; this sign's green box (x452-606) is about right but the bar runs to x~618.

Middle flag of three (R51/R52/R53, read left to right). Traced: the flag's top bar (crop x 143-226, y ~237, clear) and its pole (x ~140-143, y 238-495), faint and worn but visible as a pale vertical groove in photo and native. Separated from neighbours: left flag R51 (traced in 58.57) has its pole at crop x ~33 and bar x 40-120; right flag R53 has its pole at crop x ~265 here (FULL ~9658) and its bar at x 275-355. A sharp diagonal line from (250,240) down-left to (180,285) between the middle and right bars looks like a scratch; not traced (Rothoehler has nothing there). Flag cloth drawn as a plain Gamma, as in Rothoehler.

Right (third) flag of R51/R52/R53. Top bar clear (crop x 172-262, y ~258); pole worn, visible as a pale vertical groove in photo, relief and native at x ~167-172 down to y ~512 (FULL ~4054), level with the other two poles' ends. Separated from the middle flag R52 (pole at FULL ~9618, bar ending FULL ~9646) by the gap at crop x ~140-170 here. Gamma shape as Rothoehler draws it.

Mouth (D21): incised lens outline, clear in relief, photo and native; upper outline arched, lower outline flatter, pointed right tip (longer) and blunter left tip. Lies under the three flags and above the wick R55 / stool R56.

signs.note: wick (ḥ); tall sign at left (Ptḥ group)
signs.trace_notes: Wick (V28) as a chain of four stacked loops. Loop 1 (top, y 197-261) clear in relief, photo and native. Loops 2-4 worn: their lower edges / junctions are clear at y ~334, ~416 and ~500 (groove evidence in relief and native), their sides only faint; the bottom loop drifts left (centre x ~207). Rothoehler's crossed tail at the foot is not distinguishable from the worn surface around y 500-530; not traced. Separated from the stool R56 (traced, to the right at crop x >378) and the N16 bar R58 below (y ~590).

Sunk upright rectangle (Q3 p of Ptḥ) at full x~9632-9665, y~4119-4172: shadowed top rim at y~448, lit bottom wall at y~600-605; the vertical sides are weak (steep walls, light from above) and placed by the edges of the pale floor, hence 'faint'. Right of the ḥ chain V28 (loops at full x~9570-9590), above the sunk loaf X1 58.62 (crop y~730-765) and the long N16 bar. Matches Rothöhler's col. 58 (roth_col59.png): D21, then V28 left with Q3 over X1 at right. Box agrees with the 1901 box to within ~15 px in y, ~50 px in x (1901 box sits at x 450-515, sign is 403-505).

signs.note: bread loaf; right stack, under Q3
signs.trace_notes: Bread loaf (X1), sunk: a low flat-bottomed hollow (shadowed upper wall, pale floor) at crop x 125-247, y 185-221; rim traced as a closed outline. Right stack under the stool R56 (traced, above), right of the wick R55; the N16 bar R58 lies ~90 crop px lower.

signs.note: land (flat bar); drawn as a plain thick bar
signs.trace_notes: Land sign N16 as a plain long bar (as Rothoehler draws it), cut as a sunk flat-bottomed groove: shadowed upper wall, pale floor; rim traced as a closed outline (crop x 274-575, y 226-258). The pale nick just above it at (350-395, 195-220) is a separate small damage/hollow, not part of the bar; not traced. Lies under the wick R55 and loaf R57, above the god A40 (R59).

Very worn seated figure under the N16 bar (crop y~400), full x~9577-9627, y~4315-4413. The figure reads as a pale silhouette: traced the base/seat line (y~845), the lap/thigh rising to the knee at right (602,803)->(692,751), a short horizontal at y~571 (arm or held object) and, faintly, the back (x~551-560). Head and tall plumes (expected at y~460-550) are not distinguishable from the pitted surface; not traced. Rothöhler's col. 58 (roth_col59.png) has the seated god A40 between N16 and the bird/M17 group, as here; his figure has the same lap diagonal and base. roth.png overlay is ~240 crop px too high here.

signs.note: quail chick; left of the group
signs.trace_notes: Quail chick facing right, worn; drawn as Rothoehler's elongated diagonal body. The body is a pale, shallow lens-shaped band from the tail tip (222,391) up to the head (438,190); traced its back (upper-left edge) and belly (lower-right edge, with a narrow lit wall in the photo at (320-400, 300-385)) meeting at both tips. The tail's lower edge is a clear short horizontal groove at y~390 (x 222-298). Base/foot groove clear at y~472 (x 278-430), where Rothoehler draws the foot. The leg (Rothoehler: vertical from the belly to the foot near x~310) is only a faint pale streak at x~330-335; drawn faint. Head details (eye, beak) not distinguishable. The square R61 at (395-460, 345-445) is not traced here. roth.png sits ~5-10 crop px left of the carving.

signs.note: small square; small square tucked under the chick's head, between chick and reed; no project sid
signs.trace_notes: Small upright rectangle under the chick's head, between the chick's body and the reed leaf, as Rothoehler draws it. On the stone a pale rectangular patch with a clear lit lower wall (bottom groove y~246, x 148-212) and a top groove at y~157 (x 148-215, clear in the evidence map and native); the left (x~148) and right (x~213) sides are steep and weak, seen as dark/pale boundaries in photo and relief. Could be a shallow sunk square rather than an outline; traced as its rim. Separated from the chick: the chick's belly line passes left/above it (ends near crop (100,160)) and the chick's foot groove lies lower (y~287 here). Rothoehler's square sits within ~5 crop px.

signs.note: reed leaf; right of the group
signs.trace_notes: Reed leaf, right of the chick/square group. On the stone a pale elongated leaf (x 178-230, y 148-350) with a rounded top (top groove clear at y~148) tapering into a narrow stalk (x~206) that ends at y~448, as Rothoehler draws it (his leaf is a narrow open outline; the carved leaf is slightly wider, ~50 crop px). Long vertical sides are steep, so the evidence map is weak there; the edges are seen as pale/dark boundaries in photo, relief and native. Traced as leaf outline + stalk.

signs.note: three fox skins (ms); clear ms with knot and three strands
signs.trace_notes: ms (three fox skins): an X-shaped knot at the top (crossing at ~(240,229)); the long arm from upper right (290,197) down-left is the clearest groove and runs on into the LEFT strand; the upper-left arm (184,203) is clear, the lower-right arm into the RIGHT strand is fainter. Three strands hang down at x ~183, ~239 and ~296 to y ~450-465, visible as pale grooves in photo, relief and native (steep, so weak in the evidence map). Rothoehler's small tick on top of the knot (~(240,185)) is not visible separately. Matches his drawing in shape; his strands sit ~5-10 crop px closer together. Strands are steep, so trace_score's lock is low (~1.0); they are visible in relief AND native.

LEFT flag (first in the left-to-right reading order of retrograde columns) of the three nTr flags at full y~4685-4775, below F31 and above O1: top bar x~458-555 y~453 and pole down its left end (x~462-467) to y~718. The pole is a steep groove (weak light pairing). The other flags (crop coords): middle top bar ~575-645 y~455, pole x~578 to ~710; right top bar ~696-795 y~459, pole x~699. Rothöhler col. 58 shows the three flags in this place.

MIDDLE flag (second, left to right) of the three nTr flags. Traced its top bar/cloth (clear groove, y~164, x 290-384) and the pole down its left end (x~290, pale steep groove in photo, relief and native) to a bright foot at y~411, where Rothoehler ends it. The bar's lit lower wall is broad (y 170-190) and may be a short sunk cloth; traced the groove centre. Separated from the left flag (R64, 58.69: bar x 164-261, pole x~170) and the right flag (R66: bar x~403-500, pole x~408, both crop coords here) by the gaps between the bars at x~270-290 and ~385-400. Pole is steep, so the evidence lock is low.

RIGHT flag (third, left to right) of the three nTr flags. Traced its top bar/cloth (clear groove, y~156, x 178-272) and the pole down its left end (x~179-181) to y~404; the pole is clearest in the photo from the bar down to y~280, fainter below, with a bright patch at its foot (~y 390-410). Rothoehler draws the pole a little longer (to ~y 430 here); not visible below ~410. Separated from the middle flag (R65, bar ending at x~156 in this kit, pole x~62) by the gap at x~157-175.

House pr: rectangle open at the bottom middle (door gap x~218-272), top bar y~141 (x 184-314, clear), sides at x~180 and ~315 (steep, fainter), bottom returns at y~244 (left x 180-218, right x 272-315, clear lit lower walls). Matches Rothoehler's shape; roth.png draws it ~40 crop px too LOW (his top bar at y~185 here) - matched by sequence (the only house between the flags and the mouth D21).

Mouth/lens D21, clear, between the house O1 58.72 (x500-700,y265-375) and the water line 58.74 (y~650-700), as in Rothöhler (O1, lens, water, loaf+circle, basket). Upper outline starts at ~x484 with a short inner spur (x486-529,y477-485, a re-cut or the lip line); outlines merge at the right (~x704,y478) into a tail to x~776; the lower outline runs on as a left tail to x~414. A short stray groove leaves the lower outline at ~x655,y515 down to ~x665,y538 (visible in all three images; not in Rothöhler; not traced, probably not part of the sign). Box about right; tails run ~35 px left of the green box and ~25 px right.

Water line: a broad worn zigzag band (x 185-525, y ~180-244), clearest at the left (three sharp peaks at x~225, ~294, ~362) and flatter/blurred on the right; the right end is a bright lit wall at (492-525, 227-240). The band is wide and shallow, so its single centre line is traced; individual peaks on the right half are not separable (Rothoehler draws ~9 even peaks). roth.png draws it ~45 crop px too LOW (his zigzag at y~230-290 here); matched by sequence (between the mouth D21 above and the loaf/ring pair below). Wide shallow band, so trace_score's lock is low (~1.0).

signs.note: bread loaf; left of pair; 58.76 box sits on the basket's left half
signs.trace_notes: Loaf X1, LEFT of the loaf/ring pair: a shallow sunk dome (rim traced, sunk), pale in the photo at x 160-270, y 40-80, with a groove/shadow along the top (y~40-50) and a clear lit wall along the flat base (y~55-80, x 190-268). Rothoehler's flat-bottomed loaf, but on the stone it sits ~60-70 crop px HIGHER than roth.png and the green box (which lie on the basket R72's left half, as the inventory says); the ring R71 is to its right at crop ~(310-425, -30-100). Edges are soft, so drawn faint.

Ring Aa1, RIGHT of the loaf/ring pair: a clear circular groove, centre ~(226,124), ~106x100 crop px, upper rim and the lit lower wall (y~155-180) clearest; the interior is pale and slightly sunk. Matches Rothoehler's open circle; roth.png sits ~10-20 crop px lower. The loaf R70 is to its left (crop x ~11-122 here); the basket R72 lies below (y>~250). The disc reads partly as a shallow sunk hollow (pale interior), so the rim is traced and trace_score's lock is low (~0.93); the rim is plain in relief, photo and native.

Basket V30, cut SUNK as a shallow crescent hollow x505-776, y357-413 (thickest ~x600-700); traced its rim as a closed outline (top rim at the dark-to-bright edge, lower rim at the bright-to-dark edge, placed by eye). A dark hairline inside the hollow at ~x620-690,y393-398 is probably a crack. BOX MISPLACED: the green box (x451-785,y452-565) is empty stone; the basket lies ~90 px higher, inside the 1901 box 76:X1 (x515-664,y346-425) and extending right of it. Rothöhler's order here is water line 58.74, loaf (left, stone ~x520-620,y~260) + circle Aa1 (right, ~x680-790,y180-300), BASKET (=this, 4th after the water line counting the pair), then bird (left) + reed M17 (right).

Owl, LEFT of the owl/reed pair, worn, strongly slanted as Rothoehler draws it. Traced: the head block (x 416-461, y 30-88: top and front edges faint), the back line running from the head down-left along the upper-left edge of the pale body to the tail tip (~(207,325); upper part clear in the evidence map, lower part faint), and the clear horizontal foot/base groove at y~292 (x 362-470). The front/breast line, the inner belly line and the leg (Rothoehler) are not distinguishable on the photo. roth.png draws the owl ~100 crop px (~33 FULL px) too LOW (his foot bar at y~395, tail at y~430 here) - matched by sequence (owl before the viper R75 and the second owl R76).

Reed leaf, RIGHT of the owl/reed pair: a pale, narrow, upright leaf (x ~229-267, y ~258-473) with a pointed top, widening downwards; outline traced on the pale/dark boundaries (steep edges, weak evidence lock expected; bright lit lower end at y~445-470 in relief and native). Rothoehler's leaf is similar; his tick/stalk details at the base are not distinguishable. Separated from the owl's head (x<~200 here) by a dark gap. roth.png is ~100 crop px too low here, as for the owl.

signs.note: horned viper; between the two owls; 58.80 box ~60 FULL px low
signs.trace_notes: Horned viper: a long horizontal body groove (clear lit wall, y~92-95 from x~300 to 455), the tail running down-left to ~(190,130), and at the right end the neck/head rising steeply up-right to ~(500,30) (bright diagonal in relief and photo). Horns and the head's outline are not separable from the worn patch at (460-515, 25-80). Rothoehler draws the same shape (tail left, head raised at right); roth.png and the 58.80 green box sit ~100 crop px (~33 FULL px) LOW - matched by sequence (between the owl R73 and the owl R76).

Bird (G17 position after the viper 80:I9, before cobra 83:I10, as in Rothöhler), very worn and cut/worn as a broad SUNK silhouette: head as a bright knob at ~x530-575,y405-445, back running diagonally down-left to the tail at ~x292,y668, breast/front edge coming down from the head to a near-vertical edge at x~515 (y520-645), and a clear feet/base groove x460-590,y~670. Back and breast are rims of the worn hollow placed by eye (faint; low trace_score lock is expected for a sunk rim). Legs, eye and wing detail not distinguishable (a dark pit at ~x440,y555 is a hole, not traced). Most of the sign lies LEFT of the green box (box x451-629: only head, breast and base fall in it); the tail reaches x~290 and overlaps 1901's orange 80:I9 box only at its lower-right corner. Rothöhler's bird in roth.png is drawn ~200 px right and ~170 px higher (mid-column drift) but has the same shape: head top right, long back diagonal to lower-left tail, base at the right. QA 'absorbs:58.80' = only the head knob touches the orange 80:I9 box; the viper itself is probably the horizontal groove x300-555,y~275-310 higher up (inside 1901's 79:G17 box), so the 1901 boxes 79/80 here look shifted.

Cobra facing right, left sub-column top. Body: clear groove rising slightly to the right (crop 232-369, y 112-84), its right end turning up into the neck; head: short clear horizontal groove at crop (372-420, ~50) above the neck end (the neck between y 84 and 52 is not visible). Tail: from the body's left end a faint groove curves down the left side to ~(191,285) (relief and native), as Rothoehler draws it (his cobra hangs its tail down the left edge). Shape agrees with Rothoehler; roth.png is ~55-57 FULL px too LOW and ~13 too far right here (his loaf on mat lands on the cobra body). Green box (1901) sat lower, on the viper R78 and loaf X1; the sign is above it. Short grooves under the body at (240-265,~140) and (220-245,~150) are not traced (damage or a hood detail Rothoehler does not draw). Loaf on mat R80 (right) and viper R78 (below) not traced here.

Horned viper facing right, left sub-column under the cobra R77: clear body groove (crop 240-366, rising gently to the right, FULL ~9487-9529, y ~5513-5502) and the raised head at its right end, a faint groove rising up-right to (392,40) (photo and relief show a pale raised blob there). Horns as separate strokes not distinguishable. Agrees with Rothoehler's flat viper with raised head; roth.png ~55 FULL px too low. The 1901 green box was near the right place. Groove at (410-440, ~100) right of the head is the traced X1 R81, not part of the viper.

signs.note: quail chick (w); left sub-column, standing on a ground line
signs.trace_notes: Quail chick facing right, left sub-column, very worn. Traced: the top of the head (faint arc, crop 500-555, y~207-224, directly above the stool R82, where Rothoehler puts the head), the back line from the nape down-left to the tail tip (faint, (492,289)->(290,440); lit wall visible in relief and native, a pale wedge in the photo), a short fragment of the underside/leg top at (424-458, ~422), and the clear ground line (343-540, y~527, FULL ~9500-9565, 5648). Breast, face, legs and feet not traceable: the area right of the back line is pitted and mottled with no consistent groove edge. The ground line is the 1901 '58.88' (phantom per inventory), drawn by Rothoehler as part of this bird. Shape and sequence agree with Rothoehler (chick under the viper R78, stool R82 at its right, owl R83 below); roth.png sits ~50 FULL px too low.

signs.note: loaf on mat (ḥtp); right sub-column (ḥtp), top; loaf and mat drawn as two pieces
signs.trace_notes: Loaf on mat, right sub-column top. Mat: clear horizontal groove (FULL ~9531-9594, y~5456). Loaf: worn sunk vertical oval above the mat's right half (FULL ~9561-9575, 5430-5452), only a soft hollow in relief/native and a pale patch in the photo; rim traced as faint, sunk. The short clear horizontal groove at crop (148-175, ~180) is NOT the loaf: it is the head of the cobra R77 (traced in 58.82), where Rothoehler draws the cobra's hooked head. Rothoehler's loaf/mat agree in shape; roth.png sits ~55 FULL px too low here. The loaf hollow gives almost no groove evidence (sunk, worn); it is the least certain part.

Loaf X1, cut SUNK as a small flat-bottomed half-oval x369-456, y467-492 (rim traced as closed outline, lower edge placed by eye). BOX MISPLACED: the green box (x450-534) is ~80 px too far right and holds only the loaf's tapering right tip and worn stone; the loaf lies immediately left of it, at the right of a worn horizontal stroke x190-310,y~480 on the same level. Reading with Rothöhler (whose drawing here sits ~220 px right and ~170 px higher than the stone, the same drift as at 58.81): after the bird 58.81 he has a tall hooked sign with a small oval and a bar to its right (stone: hook top ~x200-370,y205-255; bar = long stroke x310-520,y~318, which 1901 boxes as 83:I10), then a horizontal snake with a LOAF to its right (stone: stroke x190-310,y~480 + this loaf), then bird + tall rectangle. So this is Rothöhler's loaf; his group count (5 signs) is one more than 1901's 82-85, so the exact positional match is likely but not certain. QA weak_native: expected for a small sunk rim; the loaf is plainly visible as a bright solid shape in relief, photo and native.

Stool Q3, upright: sunk upright rectangle (rim traced, sunk), right sub-column right of the chick R79, FULL ~9559-9583 x 5589-5628. The rectangle is clear in photo, relief and native (lit floor at the bottom, strong top edge). PAST CROP EDGE: the kit's green box (1901) is ~70 FULL px too low (on blank stone above the owl R83); the sign lies at the TOP of this kit, its upper part above the crop (y<0); traced in kit coordinates from views of the 58.87 kit. Agrees with Rothoehler's upright rectangle right of the chick's legs.

Loaf/upright still not visible. | tracer: Fragmentary horizontal mat groove, compatible with R4, survives in relief and native on either side of a broad worn central break. The bright lower lip is not a separate stroke; no restoration or neighbouring signs are included.

CRITIQUE: agree, conservative: upper groove fragments sit on dark/bright boundary (y~92); a pale right edge near x~195 may be the loaf's descent but lacks a clear groove pair, left untraced. | tracer: Partial presumed X1: rising upper groove along the lower lip of the dark recess and a short lower horizontal groove above the bright lip. Both are softened in native relief, so marked faint. Right descent and right continuation of base cannot be separated reliably from wear and are omitted; the sharper small central kink in the enhanced photo is not reconstructed. Box encloses only surviving traced fragments, shallower and slightly higher than the supplied box. Identity is compatible but the incomplete outline does not independently confirm it. No restored segments. | closeup: close-up shows the same dark upper slot (x~137-171, y~80-89) with the traced rising groove on its lower lip and a pale worn floor below; a second, smaller dark slot right of it (photo x~186-222, y~88-100) could be the loaf's right descent or a pit; not traced. No change.

CRITIQUE: agree with caution: base groove (y~208) coincides with a long horizontal ledge that runs across the neighbouring crops (full-res y~1682), so the base may be partly that feature; sides and top faint but present. | tracer: Worn rectangular Q3 outline in the lower part of the supplied box. Bottom and lower left groove are clearest; top and right survive faintly in relief and native. Upper-left interruption left open; no restoration. Excluded the diagonal scar below the base and adjacent signs.

CRITIQUE: weak: fragments are tiny and native support <1.0; the strong dark/bright edge at y~185 is a long ledge shared with 59.6's crop, not this sign. Identity unverifiable; kept tracer's minimal fragments. | tracer: Extremely worn possible X1 near the lower-right of the proposed box. Traced only a short rising/flattening upper-edge fragment and a short lower-edge fragment faintly supported by relief and native. The descending right curve and the connections are not sufficiently supported and remain untraced. X1 is compatible but not independently secure; the box encloses surviving traced fragments, not a reconstructed loaf. No restoration. Broad damaged ledge below the green box excluded.

CRITIQUE: foot groove was drawn ~40px too low (in flat stone below); relief/photo/native put the foot groove dark/bright boundary at y~429, moved it there. No change.

CRITIQUE: agree: rim on dark/bright boundary, bowl contour on outer edge of the lit wall; tips meet. | tracer: V30 basket: strong upper rim and worn curved bowl, both supported by native relief. The bowl extends below the supplied green box. Lower contour marked faint; no interior texture or neighbouring signs traced. No restoration.

CRITIQUE: agree: low loaf outline, tips converge, both edges on the groove edges. | tracer: Worn low X1 loaf outline. D21 mouth, 13th sign of col 59, directly in the green box: lens outline (x 500-645) with single tail grooves at both tips (left to 453, right to ~712). The same groove line continues right to ~805 at y~497 and crosses the faint vertical stick at x~755 that runs down to the heart blob at (755,740); that part is taken as 59.14 F35's crossbar and not traced here (it could also be an over-long mouth tail). Rothöhler: lens with the nfr to its right, matches.

signs.note: heart and windpipe (nfr); right of pair
signs.trace_notes: Heart and windpipe, right of the mouth R13. Heart: sunk oval (rim traced, sunk), clear in photo/relief/native, its rim ragged with small damage notches (crop 164-228 x 368-481, FULL ~9890-9911 x 2090-2127). Windpipe: faint narrow vertical groove from the heart's top up to the level of the mouth's right end (x~197, y 368->195), pale line in the photo, weak in relief/native (vertical, low lock expected). Crossbar: a faint groove at the stem's top (160-240, y ~191->178) continuing the line of the mouth's upper outline to the right; I take it as Rothoehler's crossbar of F35 because the mouth 59.13 trace ends at x~156 here, but it may be the mouth's tail. The 'rosette' look of the heart in the photo is damage around a sunk oval. Agrees with Rothoehler's F35 (stem with crossbar, oval heart at the bottom, level with the loaf R15).

Bread loaf: sunk half-oval (dome up, flat base), rim traced as closed outline (sunk). Clear in photo, relief and native (FULL ~9818-9859, 2097-2115). Left of the heart of F35 R14 and under the mouth R13, as Rothoehler draws it (his small loaf left of the F35 heart). The green box was close.

signs.note: quail chick; left of pair; 59.17's trace is on the reed, so the chick takes 59.16
signs.trace_notes: Quail chick facing right, left of the reed R17. Traced: flat head top (clear, FULL ~9853-9871, y~2148), back of head and the long back line down-left to the tail tip (clear, (346,216)->(132,463)), the underside from the tail to (275,436) (faint), an inner wing line parallel to the back (faint), the front of the head/breast (faint, x~400, y 208-340), and the left half of a clear horizontal bar under the bird at y~556 (FULL ~9819-9851, 2263), taken as the foot/ground line where Rothoehler draws the chick's feet. Legs not traceable (a pale diagonal band (270,520)-(330,400) may be them, no groove edges). Not traced: the right half of that bar (350-420, ~548) and a short stem going DOWN from its middle (x~340-345, 560-600), forming a T; they are not in Rothoehler's drawing and lie between the reed's foot and the ibis head R18 (see findings). The reed R17 (59.17 trace) right of the head is not traced here. roth.png fits the head within ~10 crop px; his body is narrower than the carved one.

signs.note: reed leaf (hooked, with crossbar); right of pair = 59.17's trace; Breasted's cross/ankh-like form
signs.trace_notes: Positional: the 17th sign of col 59 is the RIGHT member of the bird+reed pair (read left to right), i.e. the reed leaf M17; the bird G43 to its left (x~410-660, y~465-815) is the 16th. The 1901 labels 59.16=M17 / 59.17=G43 are swapped. Traced: the stem at x~717 (faint vertical groove, relief and native) from y~800 up to a hooked top bending right to (806,470) (top clear in evidence), and a horizontal cross-stroke at y~638 from x~655 to 810 that Rothöhler also draws crossing the stem. The left end of that cross-stroke (x 625-690) lies close to the bird's breast and may partly belong to it. Diagonal pale streaks around (650-830, 640-720) are wiping marks, not traced. Rothöhler's foot/branch details at the stem bottom not visible. QA 'absorbs:59.16' is expected: the 1901 59.16 (M17) box is this reed.

signs.note: ibis (gm); standing free on a ground line; 59.19 = that ground line, phantom
signs.trace_notes: Ibis facing right, standing on a ground line. Traced: back line from the tail tip up to the nape, the back of the neck, head top and the long down-curved beak (one clear groove, (118,381)->(522,268)); the lower body/breast line from the tail up to the front of the neck (clear; its last rise (430-458, 314-248) weaker); one leg (faint, vertical, x~321, y 355-486; low lock expected for a vertical groove); and the clear ground line (268-475, y~486; FULL ~9826-9895, 2385), which is the 1901 phantom 59.19 that Rothoehler draws as part of this bird. Second leg and feet not visible. Agrees with Rothoehler's G28 (his body is shorter; the carved tail reaches nearly to the column rule). The T-shaped bar above the head (FULL ~9817-9877, 2258-2280) is not part of the ibis (see 59.16 notes and findings).

signs.note: flat striped box with an oblique stick; left of pair (the 'box/mat' of the 59.21 trace notes)
signs.trace_notes: Flat striped box, left of the tall loop R20: three clear horizontal grooves (top, crop 131-358 y~350->334 with a small step up right of x~230; middle 131-347 y~393->376; bottom 169-342 y~420->411; FULL ~9786-9862 x 2481-2510) and a clear short diagonal groove (176,388)->(228,353) linking the middle line to the top line inside the box. Box ends (short verticals) not distinguishable from the bar ends. Rothoehler draws a closed rectangle with one inner stripe and an oblique stick rising up-left from the box top; on the stone there is no groove above the box, only a broad pale streak (crop ~205-265 x 210-330) with no groove edges, which I did not trace; the carved diagonal lies INSIDE the box (roth_agrees false for the stick). roth.png sits ~50 crop px too high here.

signs.note: tall narrow loop (folded cloth?); right of pair = 59.21's trace; same form as his S29 in ms (n=53); project S32
signs.trace_notes: S32-like tall narrow loop (rounded top, two legs, open bottom), right of the box-with-stick group; read L-R this is the 3rd sign after the ibis 59.18 (stick 59.19?, box/mat 59.20?, this 59.21), and before the vulture G1 59.22 below (x~540-820, y~700-960). Worn: rounded top clear, legs faint but visible in relief and native; right leg runs lower (to y~573) than the left (to ~500), as Rothöhler draws it. No fringe visible at the foot. Green box is ~300 crop px too far left/low: it holds the box/mat (x 500-715, y 480-560), not this sign. Low trace_score lock (off_cut) is expected: the legs are near-vertical grooves, seen in relief and native but weak in the scorer.

Vulture facing right, worn. Traced: head top/beak (clear horizontal groove, crop 388-464, y~206, FULL ~9867-9893, 2543), the back of the head/neck (faint vertical, x~389, 210->277), the long back line from the nape down-left to the tail tip (clear, (400,277)->(114,534)), the underside from the tail tip up to the breast (faint, partly merged with the back line's lit wall), the breast front (faint, (400,277)->(350,381)), and the clear ground line (250-468, y~516, FULL ~9821-9894, 2646). Legs/feet not traced: only a pitted pale hollow at crop ~300-345 x 437-480 where Rothoehler draws the legs, no groove edges. An oval wing groove inside the body (evidence at ~314-393 x 313-358) is only partly visible; not traced. Agrees with Rothoehler's G1 standing on a ground line (the 2646 line is his vulture's base, not a separate sign). roth.png within ~20-30 crop px.

signs.note: flat sign with small upright tick
signs.trace_notes: Flat sign with a small upright tick: a long sunk bar (rim traced as one closed outline, sunk) with a short sunk upright tick on its top edge right of centre (crop 332-358, top y~153). Bar FULL ~9784-9888 x 2684-2699, tick at FULL x ~9837-9845. Clear in photo, relief and native. Matches Rothoehler's thick flat bar with a small bump on top (his tick is nearer the middle; his bar is shorter on the right). Between the vulture's ground line R21 (above) and the thin mouth R23 (below).

Long thin sign in the green box: a small lens (x 479-590, y 435-465) with a short tail left to x~412 and a long single tail right to ~822, all at y~440-450; read as D21 mouth with very long tails (Rothöhler: a long bar thicker at its left end, the 2nd of two bars below the vulture). Sequence on the stone/Rothöhler: G1 vulture (base line y~192) -> bar with a small bump on top (x 442-752, y~327; 1901 '24 ?') -> this sign -> two heads (y~570-850). Rothöhler shows nothing for 1901's 23 ? (box upper right of the vulture) and 26 ? (box x 720-817, y 340-395, right of the bar); I see no clear carving in either, so the positional count here rests on the 1901 numbering. A pale vertical scratch crosses the tail at x~700.

Leopard head (left of the pair R24/R25), facing right: outer outline traced as one open stroke (rounded top, left side, bottom, and the lower right edge of the jaw), plus the clear mouth slit cutting in from the right (158,203)->(232,170). FULL ~9777-9830 x 2772-2825. The face is a pale smoothed (sunk) area; the outline follows its rim. The lower part of the right edge between mouth and jaw ((220,222)-(231,166)) is open, as on the stone. A faint inner curved groove in the upper face (relief only, ~100-190 x 140-240) is not traced (not in native, not in Rothoehler). The bright bar under the head (y~285-300) is the lit wall of the bottom groove. Shape agrees with Rothoehler's head with the mouth notch at the right; roth.png ~40-50 crop px too high.

Right leopard head (R25), very worn. Traced only the outline that shows as a pale hooked form in photo and relief: left side (back of head/neck) at x~174 from y~285 up, curving over the top (y~135) to the snout end at (283,176). Lower/right half of the head, the inner return to the neck and the interior are not traceable (no consistent groove edge); lock ~1.0, so the whole stroke is faint. Matched by sequence: below the D21 bar R23 (y<10), above viper R26 (y~410-470). roth.png draws the heads ~70 crop px too HIGH (his viper at y~310-390 vs stone ~410-470). The left head R24 (x 20-160) not traced here.

signs.note: horned viper; whole viper = 59.29's trace; 59.30 (I9) is its head, phantom
signs.trace_notes: The 'bar under the heads' in the green box is the TAIL of a horned viper: one continuous wavy groove from x~424 (y~538) rising to a flat stretch at y~487, a dip at x~690, and the head at x~760-797 (y~470) with one horn rising to (790,436) (faint). Rothöhler draws exactly one I9 here. So 1901's 59.29 '?' and 59.30 I9 (box x 731-820, y 356-454 in this crop, which sits just above the head) are the two ends of ONE sign; I traced the whole viper under 59.29. 59.30 should probably be merged/empty, or the numbering shifted. Below: D21 lens at y~600-650 (59.31).

D21 mouth: clear lens outline (left tip (222,215), right tip (437,213), top ~y190, bottom ~y235), traced as one closed outline. The interior shows some broken relief (worn), not traced. Sequence: directly under the viper R26 (59.29 trace) and above the three flags R28-R30. roth.png draws it ~40-50 crop px too high; his shape agrees. Right tip runs ~20 px past the green box.

Left (1st, left to right) of three god flags R28-R30 hanging from a shared top groove (y~100). Traced its part of the top groove (x 240-346, clear; the groove breaks at x~352-368 just left of the next pole) and its pole, a faint pale vertical line at x~240 from y~101 to ~290 (bright peak consistent in photo, relief and native; a break at y~190-200). Poles on the stone in this kit: x~240 (R28, this), ~370 (R29), ~488 (R30); FULL x ~9774, ~9817, ~9857, top FULL y ~2971. Lower pole end (~y 290-360) not visible. roth.png sits ~20 crop px left of and ~45 crop px above the stone. Separated from R29 by the gap in the top groove; R29's 1901-derived box (x 210-470) covers both this pole and R29's.

Middle (2nd, left to right) of three god flags R28-R30. Traced its part of the shared top groove (x 304-404, y~100, clear; gaps at the poles) and its pole, a faint pale vertical line at x~304 from y~101 to ~288 (bright peak consistent in photo, relief and native). Poles in this kit's frame: R28 x~174, R29 x~304 (this), R30 x~422. Two short pale horizontal bands right of the pole (y~120 and ~155, x 310-400) may be the flag cloth or stone texture; Rothoehler draws no cloth, not traced. Lower pole end not visible. roth.png ~20 crop px left and ~45 crop px high. The 1901 box of 59.34 (green, x 144-404) is centred between R28 and R29; I traced the 2nd flag by position.

Right (3rd, left to right) of three god flags R28-R30. Traced its part of the shared top groove (x 84-163, y~121, clear; it fades at x~165) and its pole, a faint pale vertical line at x~84 from y~120 to ~300 (bright peak consistent in photo, relief and native). Separated from R29 by the gap in the top groove at x~60-90 (R29's bar ends at x~56 here). The green box (x 147-237) is ~70 crop px right of the sign: it covers only the area under the bar's right end. Lower pole end not visible. roth.png agrees in shape (his pole ~13 px left, ~50 px high).

signs.note: quail chick; left of pair = 59.37's trace (bird)
signs.trace_notes: Positional: the 37th sign is the LEFT member of the bird+reed pair (read left to right), i.e. the bird, G43 per Rothöhler; the 1901 labels have 37=M17 (right) / 38=G43 (left), swapped as in 59.16/17. NB the tracer note 'reed of ꞽw expected' implies the pair reads reed-first (right to left within the group); if that is right, 59.17/59.37 and their partners should be swapped back. Surface very worn: traced only the bird's back as a faint diagonal groove (281,527)->(420,430), a faint lower body line y~561-580 (x 233-372) and the base line under the feet at y~671 (x 322-492). Head, legs and tail not resolvable; a pale broad diagonal band below the back line may be its lit wall, other diagonal pale streaks are wiping marks. signs.note: reed leaf (hooked, with crossbar); right of pair
signs.trace_notes: M17 (Rothoehler: reed leaf, hooked, with crossbar), right of the quail chick R31. Very worn. Traced: the horizontal top of the hook, a sharp groove with dark upper and bright lower wall at y~224 (x 255-328), turning down into the stem at (232,262); the stem as a faint pale line at x~224-232 down to y~420 (weak, vertical). Not traced: the hook's downturned right end (only a dark spot at x~335, y 225-260) and the arrow-like crossbar he draws near the bottom: the surface at y 380-500 is broken into flakes whose edges cannot be told from a cut (a horizontal band at y~405 in native may be it). Sequence: below the three flags (pole ends ~y 80 here), right of R31 (traced 59.37), above R33 htp. roth.png draws the sign ~45-50 crop px too high and ~20 left; shape agrees where visible. identity kept (M17 per Rothoehler).

htp: the mat is a clear long outlined bar (x 135-471, top groove y~305, bottom y~339, rounded right end), traced as one closed outline. The loaf on it is faint: a pale upright teardrop at x~249-294, y~214-302 (bright in relief and native at its top, y 222-250), traced as a faint closed outline; its edges are not crisp. A dark hollow right of the loaf above the mat (x 380-460, y 270-300) is damage/shadow, not traced. Sequence: below M17 R32 and quail R31, above V28 R34 (left) and Q3 R35 (right). roth.png ~70 crop px too high; shape agrees.

V28 wick, tall sign at left under the htp mat. Only its top is traceable, and uncertainly: a round sunk ring at (192-238, 308-360) with a very dark deep centre, at the place and size of the wick's top loop (Rothoehler's top loop, shifted by the ~70 crop px his drawing sits too high here). It may instead be a drilled/damage pit (roth.png shows the pit just right of his wick), so it is marked faint. Below it a pale vertical band at x~200-235 runs from y~380 to ~600 (consistent in photo, relief and native) where the twisted body should be, but no loop edges are distinguishable in the broken, flaked surface; not traced. Rothoehler's twisted loops and splayed foot not visible on the photo. roth_agrees refers to the top loop only.

signs.note: bread loaf; right stack, under Q3
signs.trace_notes: Group under R4 (mat line y~205): V28 at left (x~250-330, y~220-540, loop at (295,365)), and on the right Q3 above X1. Read left to right then top to bottom this gives 40=V28, 41=Q3, 42=X1, so position 41 is the Q3 stool (labelled X1 in 1901; 1901 order 40 Q3, 41 X1, 42 V28 reads the group right-first). Nothing traced: the Q3 place (approx. x 470-580, y 215-355, = 1901 59.40 box) is a flaked wedge-shaped hollow (dark from x~430-585 at y~220 narrowing to x~510 at y~315) with only fragmentary pale edges (a possible right side at x~577, y 220-300); no rectangle outline holds up in relief and native. The loaf X1 below it is clear (sunk half-loaf, x~462-560, bottom edge y~465, top of dome y~420; = green box) and belongs to 59.42 under the positional rule.

signs.note: branch (ḫt); 59.45's trace is this branch (m-ḫt), not Aa1
signs.trace_notes: Position 45 = the first sign after the G17 owl (owl body x~210-530, its base line is the bar at y~465, x 380-525, which is where the 1901 green box sits). The carving is a horizontal branch: stem x~178-420 at y~585, twig up and twig down at x~295, and a loop/forked end at x~420-502 (y 563-607): Rothöhler's M3 branch (m-ḫt written owl + branch). No Aa1 here; Rothöhler's Aa1 circle is lower right (stone ~x 400-500, y 690-790, with an X1 loaf at left ~x 160-310, y~800), i.e. the 1901 boxes 46-49 region.

signs.note: bread loaf; left of pair; 59.47 box ~25 FULL px above the loaf, like Breasted's circle 59.46
signs.trace_notes: X1 loaf, sunk: half-dome hollow at x 92-242, y ~262-314 (shadowed upper wall y~262-280, lit pale floor/lower wall y~280-313, flat bottom). Rim traced as a closed outline; lock is low as expected for a sunk rim (placed by eye). KIT: the green box (x 144-296, y 146-230) is ~120 crop px (~40 FULL px) ABOVE the loaf and empty (as the inventory note says); traced the loaf where it is, left of the ring R40 (traced 59.49 at x 325-433) and below the branch R38. roth.png ~65 crop px too high and ~15 left; shape agrees. trace_qa flags off_cut: the scorer prefers the dark->bright boundary at y~280 (top of the pale floor); I kept the rim at the top of the shadow (y~262) because the hollow is sunk and that height matches his loaf (~16 FULL px).

signs.note: placenta (ring); right of pair = 59.49's trace; 59.46 and 59.48 also point at this ring, phantom
signs.trace_notes: Stone sequence here: owl G17, M3 branch (59.45, y~300 in this crop), then a pair: X1 loaf at left/lower (sunk half-loaf x~490-640, y~480-525 = the green box) and Aa1 circle at right/upper, then D4 eye (x~480-760, y~620-660), X1, I9. The pair sits at slots 48/49 (anchored by 44 G17 and 50 D4); read left to right the loaf is 48 and the circle 49, so 59.49 = the circle (1901: 48 Aa1 / 49 X1, right-first, swapped as in 16/17 and 37/38). Traced the circle as the rim of a sunk disc (centre ~(775,462), ~108x100 crop px): top rim with shadow above clear, lower rim placed by eye at the lower edge of the lit band. signs.trace_notes: Positional: 5th sign of col 60 = the worn horizontal line in the green box (crop x~490-716, y~441-452), which is Rothoehler's N35 (O34, N35, Y-sign + tall sign side by side, N35, I9, G40). The 1901 label I9 belongs to the next sign: the clear line rising to the right at x~505-650, y~660->620 (60.6 box '?' sits on its left end), which matches Rothoehler's I9. Rothoehler overlay ~300 crop px left here. Caveat: the dark band above has a scalloped lower edge, so this could partly be the edge of a flaked patch rather than a cut; kept faint.

signs.note: horned viper drawn as a wavy line with thickened head at right; project '?' short bar; the I9 label of 60.5 belongs here
signs.trace_notes: Horned viper as Rothoehler draws it: a clear long groove rising from (300,214) to (452,171), ending in a small thickened knot (head, faint, x 464-484, y 170-191) and a faint short continuation to (530,184). Horns and the wave of the body are not readable; the body is nearly straight. Sequence: R5 (worn N35, y~0 in this kit) above, G40 duck (R7) below (diagonals from y~300). Rothoehler's sign agrees; roth.png draws it ~40 crop px (~13 FULL) too low and runs it further right (to x~600), where the stone shows nothing beyond x~530.

Flying duck with crossed wings, as Rothoehler draws it. Traced: (1) the upper-left wing groove from (190,276) down-right to the crossing (336,370); (2) the arched groove from lower left (236,455) up over the crossing (338,366) and down-right to (487,404), the clearest cut; (3) its faint continuation down-left to the tail end (165,503), where the stone has a small pale sunk triangle (155-236, 450-512); (4) the head/beak groove at upper right (398,250)-(495,214), clear; (5) a faint neck line from the head down-left to near the crossing (398,250)-(342,352), seen in photo and weakly in native (native's streak lies ~10-20 px further right). His short leg stroke under the crossing is not visible. The groove at y~150 above is R6 (viper); R8/R9 lie at y~600-650 below. roth.png is ~60 crop px (~20 FULL) too low; shapes match.

Bread loaf, sunk: a low half-dome hollow with flat floor line (x 168-292, y 196-232); rim traced as closed outline (lower edge placed by eye, sunk). Left of the pair; the ring at right (x~390-498 in this kit) is R9 (60.9, traced). Fits his X1 in shape and order; roth.png is ~20 FULL px low here as in R7.

signs.note: plain circle, right; project small ring
signs.trace_notes: Ring right of the 60.8 X1 (X1 bar at crop x230-340,y~620), under the G40 bird: Rothoehler draws X1 + plain circle side by side here, so 60.9 = the ring. Lower arc clear (y~628, x452-537), upper-right arc (x520-543) and top (y~555) fainter, left side weak and pitted. Green box (x452-610, y452-608) covers only its upper half. Inside: diagonal dark flake marks, not cuts.

Tall narrow round-topped sign, very worn; traced as one open outline: round top at y~274, left side x~220 (y 300-490, lost below), right side x~258-262 (y 295-585, ends at a small bright pit at (255,585)). Located by eye plus column/row profiles: both sides positive in relief, photo AND native (right side strongest). Green box (183-261,185-446) is ~90 crop px too high at the bottom; the carving runs y 271-588. Width ~42 crop (14 FULL) and height ~105 FULL agree with his S29, and he too draws the left side shorter than the right (roth.png ~40 crop px low). Sequence: below X1 (R8) + ring (R9) at y~200, above the N35 R11.

N35, clear: one wavy groove x 178-472, y ~162-176, with a few low broad waves (the fine zigzag is worn to 3-4 waves). Dark upper wall above a bright lit wall in relief; also in native. Directly above the U17 R12 (60.13, traced, pool at y~330 in this kit). Matches his N35 in place and length.

signs.note: Z-shaped pick over a long base line
signs.trace_notes: U17: Z-shaped pick (top bar crop x550-626 y~421, diagonal down-left to x~556 y~498 where it meets the pool) over a long flat pool cut as two parallel lines (y~493 and ~520, x~416-752) closing at the right end; left end open on the stone (Rothoehler closes it). Clear in all three views; matches Rothoehler's sign between the two N35 (60.12 above at y~330, 60.14 below at y~660). Green box (x452-770) misses the left ~35 px.

N35, clear: a zigzag groove of ~5 teeth from (160,232) to the highest tooth at (452,184), ending in a longer down-right leg to (504,244). Some teeth are flaked into pale patches (x 230-330), so the line through them is approximate. Between U17 R12 above (pool at y~85 in this kit, 60.13 traced) and the viper R14 below (y~350-400). Matches his N35.

Horned viper, clear: a long gently wavy groove from (150,283) rising to (285,246), level to (428,253), then a short up-step to the right end (500,221) = head end; the head is only slightly thicker, horns not readable. Visible in relief, photo and native. Below the N35 R13 (60.14) and above the bird R15. Matches his I9 (wavy body, head at right).

Standing bird (owl-like G17) cut as a sunk silhouette; rim traced as one closed outline: head top (318-358, y~40), neck down to the breast (~300,180), front edge down to the leg/thigh area (~255,312), underside back to the tail tips at lower left (57-82, 336-372), back line up to the head. The interior is partly flaked into pale diagonal and horizontal strips (x 190-305, y 165-215 and two parallel tail strips), which are drawn as one hollow. Feet/base groove traced separately (x 238-378, y ~346), clear. The ring at right (x~360-445, y~200-270) is R16 (60.17, traced). Fits his G17 in place (roth.png within ~15 crop px here) and outline; his breast bulges a little further left than the stone shows.

signs.note: plain circle under the bird's beak, right; he draws no hatching
signs.trace_notes: Ring/oval right of the long-necked bird (60.16, diagonal body x~150-460, y~260-590), in the green box at crop x~446-532, y~428-480. Lower arc clear and broad (lit floor y~468-498, possibly partly sunk), upper arc fainter (y~428-440), sides weak. Rothoehler draws a plain circle here (bird + ring side by side, as for 60.8/60.9); no internal hatching of Aa1 visible on the stone. Box of 60.16 G17 (x325-400) lies on the bird's lower body only.

signs.note: shrine (dome over a rectangle), left; first of three shrines
signs.trace_notes: Left of the three shrines, worn. Traced: the outline as one open stroke: left side x~147 (y 140-385), domed top (y~104), right side x~243 down to y~295 (lost below, where the surface is pitted); the horizontal line under the dome (y~197, x 150-241); and the base groove (y~387, x 147-250). Sides and dome are faint and were confirmed with column/row profiles (left side at x~147 positive in relief, photo AND native over its whole height). The base groove on the stone is one continuous cut from x~110 to ~490 under all three shrines (R17-R19); I traced only the part under this shrine (x 147-250); Rothoehler draws separate bases. A second pale horizontal band at y~168 inside the dome may be a further inner line (his shrine has a line there) but is too vague to trace. Neighbours: R18 middle shrine starts at x~285 (its left side shows at x~290 in the profiles); O34 R20 is the bar with central lozenge at y~490. roth.png is ~20 crop px too high here.

Middle shrine of three (R17-R19, left to right); surface very worn. Traced only what is cut: (1) a faint short horizontal groove high in the shrine (y~224, x 168-246), corresponding to the lower of Rothoehler's two short strokes ('=') at the top of this shrine; (2) the shrine's base, which on the stone is part of ONE continuous groove running under all three shrines (full x ~9936-10071, y ~2489); I traced only the stretch under this shrine (x 148-262), split per Rothoehler's base pieces (his middle base ~full x 9987-10026). Not visible: his upper top stroke, the right-hand vertical side and the small left hook at the bottom (no vertical grooves can be separated from the vertical tooling texture in relief or native). Rothoehler draws the group ~20 crop px (~7 FULL px) too high here. roth_agrees false only because most of his outline is not visible; the two traced parts match his drawing. 60.19's 1901 box covers this whole shrine group.

Right shrine of three (R17-R19, left to right); surface very worn. Traced: (1) a faint short groove at the top (y~163, x 207-252), probably the top of his dome (the dome's curved sides are not visible); (2) a faint horizontal groove at y~200 (x 175-255) = his inner line under the dome; (3) the base, part of ONE continuous groove under all three shrines (full x ~9936-10071, y ~2489), traced only under this shrine (x 150-258) per his base pieces. Not visible: both vertical sides and the dome's sides (vertical tooling texture, no separable grooves in relief or native). A further horizontal band at y~236 (x 160-260) shows in the evidence map but he draws nothing there and it fits the regular horizontal texture of this area; not traced. Rothoehler draws the group ~15-20 crop px too high. roth_agrees false because most of his outline is not on the photo; the traced parts match. 60.19's 1901 box covers this shrine.

signs.note: long bar with a central lozenge (door bolt); project X1 'long bar with central dome'
signs.trace_notes: Door bolt: one long horizontal groove (clear, full x ~9941-10065, y ~2524) with a lozenge-shaped widening just right of centre (x 326-374, y 212-244), traced as a closed outline (faint: a pale worn swelling, groove edges visible top and bottom in relief and native). The right half sits ~3-6 crop px higher than the left. Matches Rothoehler's O34 'bar with central lozenge'; he draws it ~10 FULL px too high (his bar lies over the stone's shrine base line at y~2491, which is NOT this sign). Old 1901 label X1 'long bar with central dome' is wrong.

N35 zigzag, clear, crop x~440-800, y~452-506, inside the green box: about five rounded teeth (peaks y~456-462, valleys y~470-478), both ends sloping down (right end long, to y~506). Above: 60.20 line at y~335 and the 60.19 shrine base at y~235; below: 60.22 at y~620. Rothoehler draws N35 after the shrine and bolt-like bar (his overlay ~100 px high, ~250 px left).

signs.note: small filled flat oval, top left; no project sid; sits above-left of the bird
signs.trace_notes: Sunk flat oval (lens-like, slightly tapering left), rim traced as closed outline; isolated hollow above-left of the bird R23, clearly separate from the bird's diagonal body (which starts ~25 crop px right of and below its right end). Full ~9935-9970, 2616-2628. A paler horizontal streak ~30 crop px above it (y~150, x 160-250) has no clear groove edges in native and Rothoehler draws nothing there; not traced. Rothoehler's oval matches in shape and position (his ~5-10 crop px higher).

signs.note: standing bird with upright neck; project '?' diagonal bird-like sign
signs.trace_notes: Standing bird, worn; traced what is cut: head/beak as a short horizontal groove at the top right (x 322-390, y~229), the long back line running from the head down-left to (226,418) (clear, broad groove), the tail/underside running left from there to (136,441), and the base line under the bird (x 176-368, y~551; full ~2720). Not visible: the separate neck/breast outline and the legs (Rothoehler draws two legs under the body down to the base; no grooves between y~455 and ~545). PAST CROP EDGE: the base line lies below the kit (crop height 462); traced in kit coordinates from extended views (work/scratch/roth-050/ext.py). Separated from neighbours: the oval at (330-455, 445-462) just below the head is R24 (60.24); the flat oval at upper left (x~110-200, y~240-270) is R22; the tall strokes at x>430 are R25. Rothoehler's bird matches in shape and sequence; his drawing sits ~30 crop px too high here. trace_qa 'absorbs:60.24' / 'overlap:60.R22' come only from bounding boxes: the R24 oval sits inside the bird's bbox (under the head) and R22's box touches the bird's top-left corner; no strokes are shared. fixup 2026-11-08: re-checked on the rebuilt kit; no strokes changed. None of the four strokes touches R22 (flat oval, kit crop ~137-248 x 179-217, FULL ~9934-9971, 2616-2628) or R24 (oval under the head, kit crop ~306-417 x 385-419, FULL ~9990-10027, 2684-2696): the back line passes ~35 crop px left of R24 and the tail ends ~165 crop px below R22. trace_qa absorbs:60.24 / overlap:60.R22 are bounding-box effects only (R24 lies inside the bird's bbox). The base line is now inside the rebuilt crop. The crop coordinates in the older note above predate the kit rebuild.

signs.note: small filled flat oval under the bird's head; project 'bar'
signs.trace_notes: Sunk flat oval (tapering left end, blunt right end), rim traced as closed outline; full ~9991-10027, 2685-2695, just under the bird's head (R23). GREEN BOX MISPLACED: the kit box (x 145-262, y 145-269) lies below-left of the sign; the oval is at x 262-367, y 121-149. Isolated hollow, separate from the bird R23 (its head groove lies ~30 FULL px above, at crop y~-96; its back line ends lower-left) and from R25's strokes to the right. Rothoehler draws it in the same place relative to the bird (his ~10 FULL px higher). Old 1901 label 'bar'.

signs.note: tall narrow round-topped sign, right; project '?' two tall strokes
signs.trace_notes: Tall narrow round-topped sign (S29), upper half only: rounded top at y~147 (full ~2611) with both sides as dark narrow grooves (right side x~267, clearest, down to y~280; left side x~238->226, slanting slightly left, down to y~292). Not visible below y~300 (full ~2662): Rothoehler draws both sides down to y~430-445; on the stone that stretch is pitted/worn, with only a vague pale ridge at x 230-250, y 340-420 (not traced). The second long dark vertical ~40 crop px to the right (x~305) is the column rule, which explains the old 1901 reading 'two tall strokes'. Matches Rothoehler's sign by position and sequence (right of the bird R23, above the man R26).

signs.note: standing man holding a staff; project A53; findings seeds-r2-3: man with staff
signs.trace_notes: Very worn standing figure, located where Rothöhler draws a man with a staff (his column drawing sits c. +145,+140 crop px off here). Traced only what shows: sunk round head (548,577), shoulder groove under it, the raised arm meeting the staff top as a diagonal (624,664)-(658,616), a faint body/leg line at x~540 and the foot/ground groove at y~900. Staff shaft and the hanging arm that Rothöhler draws are not visible on the photo. Bar at y~480 above the figure belongs to 60.24 (not traced). identity_ok false: the diagonal raised arm to a staff top (stone) and Rothöhler's man-with-staff argue against a mummy (A53, which has no free arm); exact A-code uncertain.

Water line: broad, knobbly wavy groove (full ~9928-10040, y ~2913), left end turning down to (112,228). Centre line on the upper (dark->bright) edge of the lit wall. Ripples on the stone are irregular, shallower than Rothoehler's regular zigzag; his position matches (sequence R27 between man R26 and viper R28). Green box sits ~70 crop px too far right: the line runs from x 112 to 447, box is 175-527.

Horned viper as a long wavy groove (clear) from the tail at lower left (125,283) rising, a shallow dip at x~400, then up to the head at the right; the head is only a slight widening/upturn at x 520-562 (faint), no horns visible. Full ~9906-10051, 2948-2976. A short separate pale groove above the left part (x 215-260, y~212) is not part of the viper in Rothoehler's drawing; not traced. Rothoehler's drawing matches in shape but sits ~30-40 crop px (~12 FULL px) too high.

signs.note: cobra; project F40; trace notes and findings: cobra
signs.trace_notes: Cobra I10, not F40: one continuous groove — tail curving down-left to (205,702), long straight body at y~513 (x 307-534), a faint vertical neck at x~537 rising to the head, a short head bar at (552-596, 431). Rothöhler draws exactly this cobra here (followed by Z1 + X1 dome below, i.e. dj + t). The head bar is Breasted's separate 60.28 'short bar' (its orange box lies just below it): it is part of this sign, so 60.28 is probably not a separate sign. Neck only faint (vertical groove, weak in relief); head and body clear in relief and native.

signs.note: short vertical stroke under the cobra, left; covered by 60.29's box
signs.trace_notes: Short vertical stroke (Z1), cut as a narrow sunk slot (pale lit floor, x~165-187), centre line traced; full ~9949-9957, 3065-3101, under the cobra R29's lower body, left of the dome R31. GREEN BOX OFF: kit box (x 144-165, y 144-240) sits ~15 crop px left and ~50 crop px above the stroke. Rothoehler's stroke matches (his ~10 FULL px higher and slightly left). A second, thinner and shallower vertical mark ~90 crop px to the right (x~268, y 207-238; full ~9983, 3071-3082), at the left end of the dome R31, is not in Rothoehler's drawing; not traced (scratch or part of R31?).

signs.note: small dome under the cobra, right; project '?' bar
signs.trace_notes: Sunk dome (X1-like, flat base, low rounded top): deep hollow whose upper wall is in shadow and floor/lower wall lit; rim traced as a closed outline (top edge placed at the top of the shadow, base at the bottom of the lit floor, by eye). Full ~9988-10029, 3086-3103. Rothoehler's small dome matches (his ~5-10 FULL px higher). A faint thin vertical mark just left of its left end (full ~9983, 3071-3082) is not part of it in his drawing; not traced (see 60.R30 notes). Old 1901 label 'bar'. trace_qa 'off_cut'/low lock: the scorer reads the shadow/lit boundary inside the hollow as a groove; for a sunk rim this is expected.

signs.note: tall narrow round-topped sign; project '?' tall round-topped upright
signs.trace_notes: Tall narrow round-topped sign (S29) as one outline: rounded top (y~190, full ~3126), left side down to y~410 (full ~3200), right side clear down to y~350, then faint (relief and a little in native) down to y~490 (full ~3226), so the right side is longer as Rothoehler draws it. Steep strokes get weak scorer evidence (lock <1 expected); the sides are visible as pale lit bands in photo and relief. Rothoehler's sign matches; his drawing sits ~20 crop px left and ~10-15 crop px higher. Old 1901 label 'tall round-topped upright'.

Water line: broad wavy groove (clear), full ~9907-10020, y ~3258-3270, both ends turning down; centre line on the upper (dark->bright) edge of the lit wall, ripples irregular. Green box (y 176-238) sits ~30 crop px too low. Matches Rothoehler's R33 by sequence (below S29 R32, above the mouth R34 = 60.33).

Mouth (D21) as a lens outline, x 535-806, y 479-523, directly below the N35 of 60.32; matches Rothöhler's lens (his strip sits c. +110,+135 crop px off). Upper outline and the right half of the lower outline clear in relief and native; left tip faint. Inner lower edge between x 660-720 is broken/worn but follows the lens.

signs.note: knob on a short stem standing on a long bar (htp-like); project '?' worn; the stone's long bar (60.35) is the base of this sign
signs.trace_notes: Rothoehler's htp-like sign: long base bar (clear, x 247-576, groove centre y ~377; this is the 1901 '60.35' bar) with a knob on a short stem over its middle. Knob and stem are very worn: only a pale oval patch with darker rim at x 388-421, y 268-330 (relief and native both show it) and no stem groove I can see beyond a faint trace; traced faint. The narrow diagonal line from (440,150) down to (400,300) in relief is a scratch, not traced. Rothoehler's knob is a bit more left (x~395 after his ~+30 x / +60 y offset here) and taller; same sign. roth.png sits ~60 crop px too high and ~30 too far left here.

signs.note: three short vertical strokes, left; no project sid (findings seeds-r2-3)
signs.trace_notes: EMPTY: surface lost. Rothoehler's three short vertical strokes should lie left of the F34 (R37) at about kit x 150-340, y 140-240 (FULL ~9894-9957, 3410-3443), between the R35 base bar (kit y ~55) and the bolt R38. The stone there is pitted and flaked: relief, native and the groove-evidence map show no vertical groove at all, only pits and pale damage patches (e.g. the pale flake at x 180-260, y 240-270). Nothing traced; Rothoehler's strokes are not visible on the photo.

Sunk F34 silhouette, rim traced as one closed outline (faint, worn): short neck at top (x 198-234, y 176-214), two side lugs (left x 140-192, right x 222-292, y ~206-258) and a rounded body below (x 170-234, y 255-335). The hollow floors show as pale patches in the photo; the lugs are clearest in relief and native. Rothoehler draws a ring with lugs (an open interior), the stone looks like a filled hollow; same sign. roth.png ~65 crop px too high and ~40 too far left here.

Door bolt O34 found c. 75 px (crop) below the green box: the long bar at y~591, x 438-765, with a worn central knob/lozenge (x 553-628) as in Rothöhler's bolt (his drawing fits at +70,+150 crop px here). The green box (y 455-525) holds only worn surface between the heart and this bar. Consequence for neighbours: Breasted's 60.38 N35 box (y~580-645) sits on THIS bolt; the real N35 is the wavy line at y~715-730. Rothöhler also draws three short strokes (III, x~450-550, y~430-500) left of the heart F34 (60.36), which Breasted's list has no sid for. Bar clear; central knob faint.

signs.note: water line; project box sits on the bolt; the real N35 is just below
signs.trace_notes: Water line N35 (Rothoehler R39), worn but clear: a broad shallow wavy groove x 142-500, centre y ~294-318 (crests at x ~160, ~280, ~450), traced along the upper dark/bright boundary. It is the line BELOW the bolt R38 (traced in 60.37, kit y ~185); the 1901 green box (y 173-235) sits on that bolt. Zigzag detail of the waves is not resolvable; traced as a gentle wave. roth.png ~70 crop px too high here.

signs.note: standing bird, left; project '?' worn small sign (iw?)
signs.trace_notes: Standing bird (Rothoehler R40), left member of the bird + f-sign pair; very worn. Traced only two parts: the long diagonal back/neck line rising to the right (x 314-404, y 241-112; faint, a narrow dark line in the photo with a lit band below-left in relief and native) and the horizontal base/foot groove (x 252-410, y ~362-366; clear). The base groove also runs under the f-sign's foot; I assign it to the bird as Rothoehler does (his foot line). Head, breast/underside and legs: no consistent groove edge (a broad pale band from (250,190) to (345,130) in relief may be the upper body but has no clear edge; not traced). The 1901 green box (146-352, 145-319) only covers the body. Separated from the f-sign R41 (upright at x ~450-480 in this kit). Matched by sequence: N35 R39 above (traced in 60.38), triangle R42 below (60.41). roth.png ~50 crop px too high here.

signs.note: f-shaped sign: upright with hooked top and a crossbar, right; project '?' tall sign, Breasted's cross-like form
signs.trace_notes: f-shaped sign (Rothoehler R41), right member of the pair, right of the bird R40; worn. Traced: the hooked top (clearest part: upright curving right into a short horizontal head at y ~248, x 240-318), the upright down to its foot at (238,558) (lower third a pale groove floor in the photo, bright in relief; middle stretch y 300-420 weak, kept faint), and the crossbar at y ~410-432 (x 160-302), slightly bowed as he draws it. The bright ring-like arc right of the upright (x 260-330, y 270-350) has no matching groove in native and is not traced (damage). The upright is low-lock as expected for a vertical groove. The 1901 green box (144-342, 146-519) is ~100 crop px too high. roth.png ~50-70 crop px too high and slightly left.

signs.note: small right-angled triangle; project D54; findings: sunk right triangle
signs.trace_notes: Sunk triangular sign directly above the bird 60.43, x 503-598, y 519-630, matching Rothöhler's triangle (his strip fits at +20,+140 crop px here): sloping front edge (clear, shadowed inner wall), base (clear, lit lower wall = the bright bar at y~625-640), vertical back faint. Traced as the rim of the hollow ('sunk'). Not walking legs D54: identity_ok false. The bright bar at its base is what Breasted boxed separately as 60.42 X1; in Rothöhler it is the triangle's base, so 60.42 is probably not a separate sign.

Bird with curved neck (Rothoehler R43). The body is cut as a long narrow sunk wedge from the tail tip (84,376) up to the neck at (405,250): upper rim = deep shadowed groove (clear), lower rim = tail/breast line (clear; rim of a sunk body, so read by eye). Neck and head (faint): neck bends back left to (370,216) then the head runs right along y ~196 to x 460, as his S-curved neck. Foot/base groove at y ~420 (x 212-450; clear). Legs between body and foot (he draws them at about x 240-290) are not visible: no groove edge. An inner pale streak inside the body (250,320)-(330,300) is the floor of the hollow, not traced. roth.png ~70 crop px too high here.

First (left) of the three god's flags R8 (Rothoehler R44-R46, read left to right); traced only this one. Flag top: horizontal groove at y ~232, x 178-292 (clear), ending where the middle flag's bar begins (60.45, pole at kit x ~297). Pole: vertical groove at x ~179 from the bar down to y ~522 (faint: a pale groove floor in the photo, weak evidence in relief/native as expected for a vertical; clearest near the bottom, (178,500)). The 1901 green box (144-237, 144-459) is ~90 crop px too high and covers only the pole's upper part. Neighbours: middle flag R45 (60.45) pole x ~297; right flag R46 pole at kit x ~417. Vertical line at x ~100 is the column rule. roth.png ~25 too high here.

Second (middle) of the three god-flags R8 in reading order (left to right): pole at x~592 from y 484 to ~755, flag top as a horizontal bar y~481, x 591-694. Matches Rothöhler's middle flag (strip fits at c. -25,+180 crop px). Others: flag 1 (60.44) pole x~470, y 500-775, top bar x 475-595 at y~487; flag 3 (60.46) pole x~715, y 500-750, top bar x 720-820 at y~485. Pole is a vertical groove (weak top-light evidence) but visible in relief and native. Small bright spots between poles (e.g. 640,567; 650,650) are surface, not cuts.

Third (right) of the three god's flags R8 (Rothoehler R44-R46, read left to right); traced only this one. Flag top: horizontal groove at y ~147, x 394-493 (clear). Pole: vertical groove at x ~396 from the bar down to y ~418 (faint: pale groove floor in the photo, bright spots in relief/native at y ~370-415; low lock is the usual vertical-groove effect). Others in this kit: left flag R44 (60.44) pole x ~150, bar y ~150 x 150-265; middle flag R45 (60.45) pole x ~267. The dark pit at (450,230) is damage. The 1901 green box (147-519) spans all three flags. roth.png ~20 too high here; his pole lengths agree with the stone.
